state_program_name: Adult Residential Facility (ARF) licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing and vendored by a regional center (DDS Title 17, service codes 915/905, ARM Levels 2–6)

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Adult Residential Facility (ARF) in California. The facility is licensed by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), Community Care Licensing Division (CCL), under Title 22 of the California Code of Regulations. It is vendored by **[REGIONAL CENTER NAME]** under Title 17 (service code 915 or 905, as approved), at the Alternative Residential Model (ARM) service level approved by the regional center (Levels 2–6).

The manual does four things:

1. **Turns regulatory requirements into daily practice.** Each policy states what must be done, who does it, by when, and what is documented. Topics include personal rights, health-related services, medications, reporting of incidents and abuse, staffing and night supervision, Needs and Services Plans, personnel qualifications and training, the physical plant, and regional center vendor obligations.
2. **Protects residents.** Residents have the right to dignity, safety, freedom from abuse and restraint, and the services in their Individual Program Plans. This manual supports those rights.
3. **Supports the licensing and vendorization reviews.** CCL reviews the plan of operation and supporting documents in the licensing application. The regional center reviews the vendor application and program design. The manual gives reviewers and the licensee one place to confirm that each required policy exists.
4. **Gives staff one reference.** The administrator, direct care staff, night staff, support staff, and relief staff use it for consistent practice and for orientation and in-service training.

This manual is a template. It does not replace the regulations, statutes, or instructions from CCL, CDSS, DDS, or the regional center. If the manual and an applicable law or regulation conflict, the law or regulation controls.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### Before first use: customize it
- Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every other bracketed field (facility name and address, licensee, administrator, regional center, service code, ARM level, capacity, phone numbers, local fire authority, local ombudsman, local health officer, consultants) with facility-specific information.
- Adjust each policy to match your plan of operation, program design, approved service level, and the residents you serve. Delete or revise any text that does not describe what your facility actually does. An unedited template does not satisfy regulatory review.
- Where the manual says "as the regional center requires" (for example, staffing ratios or night supervision for residents who rely on others for all activities of daily living), enter the specific requirement from your regional center.

### Adoption
- The licensee's **governing body** (board of directors, owner, or other governing authority) must formally adopt the manual. Record the adoption date, the approving body, and the signature of the authorized officer on the adoption page.
- Re-adopt the manual after any substantive revision.

### Keep it current
- Review the manual at least annually. Also review it whenever a regulation, statute, or regional center directive changes, when the plan of operation or program design changes, when the service level changes, or after an incident that exposes a gap.
- Some changes must be reported to CCL within 10 working days (see 22 CCR §80061(e)). Update the manual and the plan of operation together.
- Keep a revision log with the date, section changed, reason, and approver.
- Confirm the current text of regulations and forms before relying on them. For example, 17 CCR §56038 was amended in the DDS rulemaking effective 5/1/2026.

### Train staff
- Every employee, relief staff member, and volunteer must be oriented to the manual before working independently, and again whenever it changes.
- Document training in each personnel file: date, topics, trainer, and staff signature.
- Keep a copy where staff can reach it at all times, including on night shifts. Post the personal rights and visiting policy as required.

### Finding what you need
- Each policy is organized by topic and cites the regulation it implements.
- **Appendix A** maps each item on the official state licensing checklist to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to check completeness before submitting an application or preparing for a review.
- Where a policy has a related form, log, or plan (for example, the emergency disaster plan, the Needs and Services Plan, or the infection control plan), the policy points to it.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

This facility is a community care facility under the Community Care Facilities Act (HSC §1500 et seq.). Licensing authority rests with CDSS Community Care Licensing. Regional center vendorization is governed by Title 17 and the Lanterman Act. The rules below are cited exactly as they appear in the source citations for this manual. Always confirm the current text before relying on a provision.

### Governing rules

**Personal rights, reporting, and health-related services (Title 22)**
- **22 CCR §80061**, Reporting Requirements: reports to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days, for deaths, injuries needing medical treatment, unusual incidents, and similar events. Suspected physical abuse of a dependent adult is reported within 2 hours if serious bodily injury results, otherwise within 24 hours. Organizational and plan-of-operation changes are reported within 10 working days.
- **22 CCR §80072**, Personal Rights: the list of personal rights, advising clients and authorized representatives at admission, posting the rights and visiting policy, and the licensee's duty to ensure the rights are honored.
- **22 CCR §80075**, Health-Related Services: first aid and medical care, assistance with medications, inhalers and injections, PRN medications, oxygen, first-aid training and supplies, emergency contacts, central storage, and destruction of medications.
- **WIC §15630**, Elder/Dependent Adult Abuse Mandated Reporting. CCL timelines are restated in 22 CCR §80061(c)-(d).

**Personnel and staffing (Title 22)**
- **22 CCR §80065**, Personnel Requirements (general)
- **22 CCR §85065**, ARF Personnel Requirements
- **22 CCR §85065.5**, Day Staff-Client Ratio
- **22 CCR §85065.6**, Night Supervision
- **22 CCR §85064**, ARF Administrator Qualifications and Duties
- **22 CCR §85064.2**, ARF Administrator Certification Requirements
- **22 CCR §85064.3**, ARF Administrator Recertification Requirements
- **22 CCR §80019**, Criminal Record Clearance

**Client services, plant, and operations (Title 22)**
- **22 CCR §85068.2**, Needs and Services Plan
- **22 CCR §85087**, ARF Buildings and Grounds
- **22 CCR §85088**, Fixtures, Furniture, Equipment and Supplies
- **22 CCR §80020**, Fire Clearance
- **22 CCR §80022**, Plan of Operation
- **22 CCR §85022**, ARF Plan of Operation

**Licensing application (Title 22)**
- **22 CCR §80018**, Application for License
- **22 CCR §85018**, ARF Application for License

**Regional center vendorization and program (Title 17 and Welfare & Institutions Code)**
- **17 CCR §56003**, Residential Services Orientation
- **17 CCR §56004**, Facility Service Levels
- **17 CCR §56005**, Facility Service Level Approval Process
- **17 CCR §56013**, Program Design Requirements
- **17 CCR §56033**, Direct Care Staff Competency-Based Training and Testing
- **17 CCR §56037**, Administrator Qualifications and Continuing Education
- **17 CCR §56038**, Direct Care Staff Qualifications and Continuing Education (amended effective 5/1/2026; confirm the current text)
- **17 CCR §54310**, Vendor Application Requirements
- **17 CCR §54320**, Regional Center Review of Vendor Application
- **17 CCR §54326**, General Requirements for Vendors and Regional Centers
- **17 CCR §54342**, Types of Services
- **WIC §4500 et seq.**, Lanterman Developmental Disabilities Services Act
- **WIC §4652.5**, Independent audit / independent review of vendors

**Fees**
- **HSC §1523.1**, Community care facility license fees

The Title 22 ARF regulations (22 CCR §85000 et seq., together with the general community care facility regulations at §80000 et seq.) set the detailed content of the plan of operation. Policies in this manual that rely on them should be checked against their current text.

### Regulators and contacts

| **California Department of Developmental Services (DDS)** | Sets residential (ARM) rates under rate reform, Title 17 rules, QIP, and DSPT; oversees the 21 regional centers | 833-421-0061; RatesQuestions@dds.ca.gov (rates); vendorization@dds.ca.gov (vendorization); QIPQuestions@dds.ca.gov (QIP); https://www.dds.ca.gov/rc/vendor-provider/ |
| **Vendoring regional center: [REGIONAL CENTER NAME]** | Vendorization, service level approval (17 CCR §56005), residential orientation, placements, monitoring, and payment | **[Phone / email of your regional center's vendor and residential services unit]**; directory at https://www.dds.ca.gov/rc/listings/ |
| **Local fire authority / State Fire Marshal: [LOCAL FIRE AUTHORITY]** | Fire clearance (ordered through CAB); separate clearance before admitting nonambulatory residents | **[Phone / email of your local fire authority]** |

Also record in the customized manual the contacts for your local ombudsman, local health officer, and the CCL regional office that handles complaints for your area. These contacts are used in the reporting policies.

### Official policy checklist and application document

The state reviews this manual against the following official document:

- **LIC 281, Application Instructions for a Facility License (Application Booklet for Facility License), Sections A and B**, issued by the California Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing Division. It covers Adult Residential Facilities. Section B is the plan-of-operation and supporting-documents checklist for ARF applicants. Policy and program-content items marked Required for ARFs are the items this manual addresses, including A14, the Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610D for ARFs).

**Appendix A maps every official checklist item to the policy in this manual that satisfies it.** Use it to confirm each item is covered before submitting the application packet or preparing for review.

Points to note about LIC 281:
- The edition used to build this manual is **LIC 281 (9/04)**, supplied by the owner. A newer version has not been confirmed. **Confirm the current version with the CDSS Centralized Applications Bureau before submitting.**
- The supplied text did not include the narrative content criteria for items B4–B11 and B15, so Appendix A lists them by title. For their required content, use the Title 22 ARF regulations listed above.
- Application forms, financial and ownership documents, certificates, the facility sketch, the fire inspection, and the water analysis are not policy items and are outside this manual.
- The booklet requires the application fee and all Section A and B documents to be submitted to the licensing agency as one packet in booklet sequence. Incomplete packets are returned in full.
- Title 17 vendorization documents required by the regional center are separate from LIC 281. Obtain them from your regional center.

### Responsibilities of the licensee

- **Customize** this manual for the facility, replacing all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other placeholders.
- Have the **governing body adopt** it, and re-adopt it after substantive revisions.
- **Keep it current** as laws, regulations, forms, the plan of operation, or the program design change, and report required changes to CCL and the regional center on time.
- **Train all staff** on the manual and document the training in personnel files.

citations.title: Reporting Requirements
citations.requirement: CCL report by the next working day, then a written report within 7 days, for: any death; deaths from injury, abuse or other than natural causes (including deaths away from the facility); AED use; injury needing medical treatment; unusual incident or client absence that threatens health or safety; suspected psychological abuse; epidemic outbreaks; poisonings; catastrophes; fires or explosions. Written report must give client name/age/sex/admission date, date and nature of event, physician findings and treatment, and disposition. (c)-(d): suspected physical abuse of a dependent adult goes to the local ombudsman, CCL and law enforcement within 2 hours if serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours (WIC 15630(b)(1)). (e): within 10 working days report organizational changes, mailing address changes, change of corporate CEO (with fingerprints), and plan-of-operation changes that affect services. (f)-(i): items (b)(1)(A)-(H) also go to the authorized representative; (E)-(G) go to the local health officer when appropriate; epidemic outbreaks go immediately to the local fire authority; substantiated complaints are copied to designated parties.

citations.title: Personal Rights
citations.requirement: (a)(1)-(10) personal rights: dignity; safe and comfortable accommodations; freedom from corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, punitive actions, interference with eating/sleeping/toileting, and withholding of shelter, clothing, medication or aids; being told the CCL complaint unit address and phone and confidentiality information; religious freedom; leaving the facility at any time (curfews and house rules allowed; not applicable to clients with a conservator or other legal authority); not being locked in any room or the premises (exterior doors and windows may be locked if clients can exit; other securing means need prior CCL approval); no restraining devices (postural supports and protective devices only under strict conditions); right to receive or reject medical care; being told the visiting policy (HSC 1512). (d) at admission the client and authorized representative are personally advised of and given the list of rights; (e) rights and visiting policy are posted prominently; (f) the licensee ensures the rights are honored.

citations.title: Health-Related Services
citations.requirement: Licensee ensures first aid and needed medical/dental care, including transportation. Clients are assisted with self-administration of prescription and nonprescription medications. ARF staff may assist with metered-dose and dry-powder inhalers only after training by a licensed professional, with written documentation of procedures and trained staff names, annual review by the professional, and training documented in personnel files. Staff may not give injections except as authorized by law; designated staff may assist with self-administration of injections. No forcing, hiding or camouflaging medication. PRN rules in (b)(4)-(6). Oxygen requirements in (e). First-aid training for direct care staff (f). First-aid supplies list (g). Emergency communication person and contact list at all times (h). Central storage rules (j)-(k) with records kept at least 1 year. Destruction of unretained prescriptions witnessed by the administrator and one other adult non-client, record kept at least 1 year (l).

citations.title: Personnel Requirements (general)
citations.requirement: Personnel competent and in numbers needed to meet client needs; CCL may require added staff (documented, with written reasons), considering client needs, services, physical plant and any emergency or disaster. Volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan. Staff who supervise or give care must be 18+. Direct supervision at potentially dangerous activities or areas; an adult non-client present whenever clients use a pool or body of water needing swim rescue, with a valid water safety certificate. On-the-job training topics in (f). Health screening including TB test by or under a physician no more than 1 year before or 7 days after employment (g). Ill personnel relieved of duty (h). California criminal record clearance or exemption before employment or initial presence (i). Clients are not substitutes for required staff (j). Coverage by capable personnel during absences (k). Care without physical or verbal abuse, exploitation or prejudice (l). All personnel instructed to report personal-rights violations (m). (o): ARFs using secured perimeters must train direct care staff in Emergency Intervention (§85300).

citations.title: ARF Application for License
citations.requirement: Financial plan of operation on CDSS forms. Start-up funds must cover the first three months of operation, and CCL may require written verification. Applicant submits administrator name, addresses, background and qualifications, and documentation of required education and administrator certification.

citations.title: ARF Personnel Requirements
citations.requirement: Licensee employs staff as necessary to provide care and supervision that meets client needs (b), and support staff for office work, cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance (c). Food service staffing must ensure clients' food service needs are met (e)(1). Services requiring specialized skills must be performed by licensed or certified personnel; where no license or certification exists, prior CCL approval is required for an unlicensed person to provide the service (f).

citations.title: Night Supervision
citations.requirement: Night staff (10 p.m.-7 a.m.) must be able to help in an emergency and be trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and in first aid (b). Facilities with 15 or fewer clients need at least one person on call on the premises (c). For 7+ clients who rely on others for all ADLs, one person on duty, on the premises and awake, plus one more per additional 14 such clients (f). For Regional Center clients who rely on others for all ADLs, night supervision is as the RC requires but no less than (f)/(f)(1) (g). Where a signal system is required (§85088), a staff person is responsible for responding to it (i).

citations.title: Needs and Services Plan
citations.requirement: Before admission the licensee determines the program can meet the person's needs, then completes a written Needs and Services Plan. The plan covers: client desires and background; entrance to the facility; specific service needs; written medical assessment (§80069); mental and emotional functioning; mental health intake assessment if any (§85069.3); functional capabilities assessment (§80069.2); the HSC 1180.4(a) initial assessment on or before the day of admission; the individual emergency intervention plan (§85168.2(a)); and facility plans to meet the needs. The 1180.4(a) assessment includes input from the client, authorized representative and any person the client chooses; the client's advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion or manual restraint (honored unless it violates law or endangers safety); early warning signs and triggers; calming techniques; medical conditions raising restraint risk; and trauma history. If the client has a restricted health condition (§80092), the plan includes the Restricted Health Condition Care Plan (§80092.2). Involve the client or representative, participating relatives, the placement or referral agency, and the person responsible for admissions.

citations.title: Day Staff-Client Ratio
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: for Regional Center clients who rely on others for all ADLs, day staffing is as the RC specifies, no less than 1:3.

citations.title: ARF Buildings and Grounds
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: no more than two clients per bedroom; bedrooms not used as passageways.

citations.title: Fixtures, Furniture, Equipment and Supplies
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family; per-resident bed, chair, nightstand, lamp and drawers (2 drawers or 8 cu ft); linens; hygiene supplies; emergency lighting; night lights; signal system where required.

citations.title: Fire Clearance
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: fire clearance is obtained through CCL; a separate clearance is required before admitting nonambulatory clients or persons 65+. §80072(a)(8)(D) requires a fire clearance before using a postural support that makes a client nonambulatory.

citations.title: Criminal Record Clearance
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Live Scan clearance or exemption is required before staff presence. §80065(i) confirms clearance, exemption or an approved transfer before employment or initial presence; §80019(d) fingerprints are required for a new corporate CEO.

citations.title: Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: written plan covering purpose, admissions, admission agreement, staffing plan, in-service plan, floor plan and grounds sketch, menus, transportation, rate and refund policy, handling of resident money, consultants and visiting policy. It must be kept current; changes that affect services go to CCL within 10 working days (§80061(e)(4)).

citations.title: ARF Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research checklist: ARF plan of operation includes the infection control plan (§85022(a)(1)) and consultants (§85022(a)(2)).

citations.title: Application for License
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: CCL orientation is completed before filing; sets application contents, including the lease and landlord information in (d)(3).

citations.title: ARF Administrator Qualifications and Duties
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: certified administrator, age 21+, high school diploma or GED; HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator and updated every two years ((k)); 7-15 client homes need one year of residential care experience.

citations.title: ARF Administrator Certification Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 35-hour CDSS-approved Initial Certification Training Program; exam within 60 days of finishing, maximum 3 attempts ($100); apply on LIC 9214 within 30 days of passing, with LIC 508 and Live Scan (LIC 9163), $140 fee.

citations.title: ARF Administrator Recertification Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 40 hours of continuing education every two years (4 hours on laws and regulations); up to 24 hours of RC-approved DDS training may count.

citations.title: Facility Service Levels
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: basic direct care staffing whenever residents are under facility supervision: Level 2 1 per up to 6; Levels 3/4A/4B 1 per up to 3; 4C-4E 1 per up to 2; 4F-4I 1 for the first resident. Above those resident counts, weekly direct care hours are added by level (§56004(d) table); 2-7 hours per resident per week of program preparation can count. Consultant hours of 8/12/16 per consumer per six months (§56004(f)). The text uses legacy levels; map to Levels 2-6 using the DDS crosswalk (L3 = old 3/4A/4B; L4 = 4C-4E; L5 = 4F-4H; L6 = 4I).

citations.title: Facility Service Level Approval Process
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: written service level request with administrator qualifications; RC decides within 45 days; a level change is allowed only on a change of ownership or when most residents' ID teams identify a new need ((c)(1)).

citations.title: Residential Services Orientation
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: the administrator completes the RC residential services orientation before the first admission. RCs hold it at least every six months.

citations.title: Program Design Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: written program design with org chart, purpose and outcomes, entrance/exit criteria, program preparation duties, staff qualifications and duty statements, sample schedule and training plan; Level 3 and 4 designs have extra content.

citations.title: Direct Care Staff Competency-Based Training and Testing
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: two 35-hour DSPT segments (year 1 and year 2) with tests or a challenge test; §56033(a)(2)(B) segment 2 within two years of hire. DDS DSPT is free to first- and second-year DSPs (dds.ca.gov/services/dspt).

citations.title: Administrator Qualifications and Continuing Education
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 6/9/12 months of DD experience for Level 2/3/4 (RC may waive); 8/12/12 hours of annual continuing education.

citations.title: Direct Care Staff Qualifications and Continuing Education
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 40-hour on-site orientation ((a)(1)) covering program design, IPPs, rights, medications, emergencies and fire, SIRs and abuse reporting; CE of 8 hours/year (L2) or 12 hours/year (L3-L4); Level 4 staff without 6 months' experience add 12 hours in the first six months. This section was amended in the DDS SIR rulemaking effective 5/1/2026; confirm current text.

citations.title: Vendor Application Requirements
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: DS 1890 with disclosures, service type (915/905), capacity and consultants; copy of license or proof of application; signed HCBS Provider Agreement ((a)(10)(J)) for Medi-Cal-eligible services.

citations.title: Regional Center Review of Vendor Application
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 45-day review; the RC cannot approve or refer until the license is received ((c)).

citations.title: General Requirements for Vendors and Regional Centers
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: vendor allows monitoring access ((a)(2)); keeps records at least 5 years ((a)(3)); bills only authorized, delivered services and the rate is payment in full ((a)(10),(12)); vendored by the RC where the facility is located ((a)(14)); HCBS Provider Agreement ((a)(16)); no payment for pre-vendorization services and no referrals before vendorization ((d)(4)).

citations.title: Types of Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: service codes 905/910 owner-operated and 915/920 staff-operated residential facilities.

citations.title: Elder/Dependent Adult Abuse Mandated Reporting
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: mandated reporter duties for abuse of elders and dependent adults. CCL timelines are restated in 22 CCR §80061(c)-(d): 2 hours for suspected physical abuse resulting in serious bodily injury, 24 hours otherwise.

citations.title: Independent audit / independent review of vendors
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: independent review if RC payments are $500,000-$1,999,999 a year; independent audit at $2,000,000 or more; due 9 months after fiscal year end.

citations.title: Lanterman Developmental Disabilities Services Act
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: entitlement to services and the statutory basis for regional center services and vendorization.

citations.title: Community care facility license fees
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: 4-6 beds $908 with the application and $454 annual; late annual fee adds 50%. Facility is within the Community Care Facilities Act, HSC §1500 et seq.

policies.category: Section A – Forms by Type of Facility
policies.title: Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610D) and Relocation Sites
policies.applies_to: Administrator, lead/house manager, all direct support professionals (day, evening and night staff), support staff, and relief staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] has a written, current Emergency Disaster Plan on form LIC 610D that protects every resident in a fire, earthquake, flood, power or water loss, or other catastrophe. The plan names two relocation sites away from the facility, each able to hold the full licensed census. It also ensures staff are trained to carry the plan out and that required reports are made to Community Care Licensing (CCL).
policies.policy:
This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section A, item A14 — Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610D for Adult Residential Facilities), including the requirement to show two relocation sites away from the facility that can accommodate the number of clients in the facility, and the requirement for written authorization from the agency or person in possession when the applicant does not currently occupy the property.

[AGENCY NAME] will complete form LIC 610D and keep it current as part of its plan of operation (22 CCR §80022 and §85022). The plan will name two relocation sites away from the facility. Each site must be able to hold the full licensed census of [LICENSED CAPACITY] residents, including any resident who uses a wheelchair or other mobility aid. If [AGENCY NAME] does not yet occupy the property, or does not own or control a relocation site, the administrator will obtain written authorization for each relocation site from the agency or person in possession and keep it with the plan. Before any nonambulatory resident or resident age 65 or older is admitted, the administrator will confirm that the separate fire clearance required under 22 CCR §80020 is in place and that both relocation sites can safely receive that resident.

Night staff (10 p.m. to 7 a.m.) must be able to help in an emergency and must be trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and in first aid (22 CCR §85065.6). Catastrophes, fires and explosions are reported to CCL by the next working day, followed by a written report within 7 days (22 CCR §80061). Emergency planning must respect resident rights and the person-centered, accessible nature of the home under the federal HCBS settings rule (42 CFR 441.301(c)) and the Americans with Disabilities Act, so evacuation and relocation arrangements must account for each resident's mobility, communication, sensory and behavioral support needs.

definitions.definition: The CCL Emergency Disaster Plan form for Adult Residential Facilities.
A location away from the facility, with written authorization, where all residents can be taken and cared for if the home cannot be occupied.
The maximum number of residents the facility's CCL license allows.
A resident who cannot move from a place of danger without physical assistance or a mobility device. This status requires a separate fire clearance before admission.
Staff on duty between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m.

procedures: 1. Before the license application is submitted, the Administrator completes every section of LIC 610D, and the plan is kept in the facility's plan of operation binder at [ADDRESS].

2. The Administrator selects two relocation sites in different directions from the facility, away from the facility and unlikely to be affected by the same hazard. The Administrator records the name, address, phone number and contact person for each site.

3. The Administrator visits each site and confirms in writing that it can hold the full licensed census. The check covers sleeping space, toilets, kitchen or food access, accessibility for residents with mobility needs, and power and water.

4. If [AGENCY NAME] does not currently occupy the property or does not control the relocation site, the Administrator obtains written authorization from the agency or person in possession of each site. The authorization is signed and dated, with the signer's name, title and phone number.
5. The Administrator places the signed authorizations behind the LIC 610D and verifies them once a year by phone, noting the date and the person contacted.

6. The Administrator keeps current at the facility a resident roster listing each resident's mobility, communication, medical, medication and behavioral support needs. The roster also shows the authorized representative and regional center service coordinator contacts. It is placed in the emergency kit so staff can take it during evacuation.

7. The Administrator posts the evacuation routes and emergency contact list where staff can see them, and keeps a stocked emergency kit with medications, first-aid supplies, resident information, water and food. Staff check the kit monthly and record the date.

8. Before working alone, every new employee is oriented to LIC 610D, the relocation sites, evacuation routes and each resident's evacuation needs. Orientation is documented in the personnel file and training log (see SB-03 and STF-05).
9. Before working any shift between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m., each staff member is trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and in first aid. The Administrator signs off the training record.

10. Before admitting a nonambulatory resident or a resident age 65 or older, the Administrator confirms the separate fire clearance is in place and confirms both relocation sites can safely receive the resident.

11. In an emergency, the staff person in charge first protects life by calling 911 when needed and evacuating residents using the plan's routes and each resident's support needs. Staff take the roster and emergency kit and account for every resident by name once outside.

12. If the home cannot be occupied, the staff person in charge moves residents to the first relocation site, or to the second if the first is unusable, and keeps residents supervised with enough staff throughout.

13. The staff person in charge notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator notifies each resident's authorized representative and the regional center service coordinator as soon as possible.

14. For any catastrophe, fire or explosion, the Administrator reports to CCL by the next working day by phone. The Administrator submits a written report within 7 days that gives each affected resident's name, age, sex and admission date, the date and nature of the event, physician findings and treatment if any, and the disposition. A copy is kept in the facility file (see BSP-04 and REC-02).
15. After the event, the Administrator holds a debrief with staff within 7 days. The Administrator documents problems found and corrects the plan, equipment or training.

16. The Administrator reviews LIC 610D at least once a year and whenever the census, a resident's mobility or support needs, or a relocation site changes. The plan is revised and re-dated. If a change affects the plan of operation, the Administrator reports it to CCL within 10 working days (22 CCR §80061(e)).
17. The Administrator coordinates this plan with the fire safety program and drills in HE-02 so that drill findings feed into plan updates.

responsibilities.duty: Completes and updates LIC 610D, selects and verifies relocation sites, obtains written authorizations, trains staff, makes CCL, representative and regional center notifications, and leads the post-event debrief.

policies.title: Job Descriptions and Duty Statements
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body/owner, lead/house manager, direct support professionals, support staff
policies.purpose: To define in writing the qualifications, duties, supervision and training for every position at [AGENCY NAME], so each employee knows what is expected and the regulators can see that duties match resident needs and Title 17 program design requirements.
policies.policy:
This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B4 — Job Description - each position.

[AGENCY NAME] maintains a written job description and duty statement for every position: Administrator, Lead/House Manager, Direct Support Professional (DSP), and Support Staff (cook, housekeeping, laundry and maintenance). The Title 17 program design includes staff qualifications and duty statements (17 CCR §56013), and these job descriptions form that part of the program design.

The agency employs staff as necessary to provide care and supervision that meet resident needs, and support staff for office work, cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance (22 CCR §85065(b)–(c)). Any person who supervises or gives care to residents must be at least 18 years old (22 CCR §80065). Tasks that require specialized skills are performed only by licensed or certified personnel. If no license or certification exists for a task, an unlicensed person may perform it only with prior CCL approval (22 CCR §85065(f)). Each duty statement states the minimum age, qualifications and required training, and the agency's program design is built from these duty statements. Duty statements do not authorize any person to exceed their license, certification or training.

definitions.definition: A written statement of a position's title, qualifications, supervisor, responsibilities and working conditions.
The specific tasks assigned to a position, used in the Title 17 program design.
Direct care staff who give care, supervision and support to residents in the home.
Tasks that by law must be done by a licensed or certified person, such as nursing tasks.

procedures: 1. The Administrator writes a job description for each position before the license and vendorization applications are submitted, and reviews each at least once a year.

2. Each job description states title, reports-to, minimum age (18 or older for any person who supervises or gives care), education or experience, required training, and physical requirements with reasonable accommodation language.

3. The Administrator job description requires an ARF administrator certificate, age 21 or older, a high school diploma or GED, and HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator, updated every two years (22 CCR §85064). If the home will serve 7 to 15 residents, one year of residential care experience is also required.

4. The Direct Support Professional job description lists duties: care and supervision, assistance with activities of daily living, implementation of each resident's supports, assistance with self-administered medications only as trained, community integration support, documentation, incident and abuse reporting, and emergency response.

5. The DSP description lists the 40-hour on-site orientation and continuing education required under 17 CCR §56038: 8 hours per year at Level 2 and 12 hours per year at Levels 3–4. Level 4 staff without six months' experience complete an additional 12 hours in the first six months. The Administrator confirms the current §56038 text, which was amended effective May 1, 2026.
6. The Lead/House Manager description covers scheduling, staff supervision, orientation, house operations and daily oversight. It states that the Lead/House Manager reports to the Administrator.

7. The Support Staff description covers cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance only. It states that support staff do not count toward direct care staffing unless also trained and scheduled as DSPs.
8. Each description states that tasks requiring specialized skills are given only to licensed or certified personnel, and that any exception requires prior CCL approval under 22 CCR §85065(f).

9. Each description requires that the employee clear a criminal record check or exemption and a TB screening before starting work (see STF-02 and STF-04) and care for residents without physical or verbal abuse, exploitation or prejudice.
10. Each description requires the employee to report any violation of residents' personal rights and to act as a mandated reporter as set out in BSP-03.
11. The Administrator gives each new hire their job description at the time of the offer, reviews it with them on the first day, and obtains a signed, dated acknowledgment.
12. The Administrator places the signed job description in the employee's personnel file (STF-05) and keeps a master copy in the program design binder.

13. When duties, a resident's service level or the program design change, the Administrator revises the affected descriptions within 30 days, re-issues them to affected staff, and obtains new acknowledgments.

responsibilities.duty: Writes and updates all job descriptions, ensures qualification requirements are met before assignment, and keeps signed acknowledgments.
Approves positions and ensures budgeted staffing supports the duty statements.
Assigns work consistent with duty statements and reports any staff working outside their qualifications.
Perform duties as written, work only within their training, and report any task they are asked to do beyond their qualifications.

documentation: Job description and duty statement for each position
Signed acknowledgment in each personnel file
Annual review log of job descriptions
Program design binder containing duty statements and the organizational chart

policies.title: Personnel Policies
policies.applies_to: Administrator, all employees, volunteers and relief staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To set clear, lawful rules for hiring, supervision, conduct, training, health, pay and discipline of all personnel, so residents receive safe and respectful care and the agency complies with Title 22, Title 17 and employment law.
policies.policy:
This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B5 — Personnel Policies.

[AGENCY NAME] employs personnel who are competent and in the numbers needed to meet resident needs (22 CCR §80065). CCL may require added staff, and the agency will provide them. Staff who supervise or give care are at least 18 years old. Clients are never used as substitutes for required staff, and capable personnel cover all absences. Volunteers are supervised at all times and are not counted in the staffing plan. Support staff for cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance are provided as needed (22 CCR §85065), and tasks requiring specialized skills are performed only by licensed or certified personnel.

No person may be employed or be present at the facility until California criminal record clearance, an exemption, or an approved transfer is on file (22 CCR §80019 and §80065(i)). Each employee must have a health screening including a TB test by or under a physician no more than one year before or seven days after employment. Ill personnel are relieved of duty until they are well. All care is given without physical or verbal abuse, exploitation or prejudice, and every employee must report any violation of residents' personal rights. Employees receive the orientation, training and continuing education required under 17 CCR §56033 and §56038.

As an employer, [AGENCY NAME] pays at or above the California minimum wage ($16.90 per hour in 2026) or the higher local rate where the home is located, and provides paid sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year under California paid sick leave law. It follows the domestic-service rules at 29 CFR 552, the bloodborne pathogen standard at 29 CFR 1910.1030, and the HIPAA administrative requirements at 45 CFR 164.530 for training, safeguards and sanctions.

definitions.definition: All paid staff, relief staff, and anyone who provides care or services at the facility on behalf of the agency.
An unpaid person who assists at the facility under supervision. A volunteer is not counted in the staffing plan.
A Live Scan-based clearance or exemption issued before the person starts work or is present at the facility.
Removed from work, with no resident contact, until the person is no longer ill or contagious.

procedures: 1. Before an offer, the Administrator confirms the applicant meets the qualifications in the job description (SB-01), is at least 18 if the person will supervise or give care, and has valid references.

2. Before the first day of work or any presence at the facility, the Administrator submits fingerprints through Live Scan and confirms that clearance, an exemption, or an approved transfer is on file. The person is not left alone with, or allowed in the presence of, residents before this is done (see STF-02).

3. The Administrator obtains the new employee's TB test result, from no more than one year before or seven days after the start of employment, and a physician's health screening, and files both (see STF-04).

4. On the first day, the employee receives and signs for the personnel policies, job description, resident rights, abuse reporting duties, confidentiality rules and the staff conduct standards in STF-06.
5. New employees begin the 40-hour on-site orientation and the DSPT training plan under SB-03 and STF-03. They are supervised until the Administrator signs off their competence.

6. The Administrator sets the work schedule so that staff are present in the numbers the staffing policy requires (STF-01). Residents are never assigned staff duties, and volunteers are never counted.
7. If a person is absent, the Lead/House Manager calls capable, cleared and trained relief staff. If none is available the Lead/House Manager calls the Administrator, who covers the shift.

8. Any employee with a fever, vomiting, diarrhea, a contagious rash or another illness that could spread to residents notifies the Lead/House Manager before the shift, or immediately on onset, and is relieved of duty until well. Infection control rules are in HE-03.
9. The Administrator offers sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year, does not retaliate for its use, and records accruals and use.
10. The Administrator pays each employee at or above the state minimum wage of $16.90 per hour (2026) or the higher local rate, and keeps timekeeping and pay records (see STF-08).

11. Employees report any suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation or personal-rights violation to the Administrator immediately and make required outside reports under BSP-03. No employee is disciplined for making a good-faith report.

12. Prohibited conduct includes physical or verbal abuse, exploitation, prejudice, theft, borrowing from residents, and being impaired on duty. Violations lead to corrective action up to immediate termination and, where required, a report to CCL and law enforcement.
13. The Administrator reviews each employee's performance within 90 days of hire and at least annually after that, in writing, and discusses training needs.
14. The Administrator offers bloodborne pathogen training at hire and annually, and trains employees on resident privacy rules under HIPAA (IR-04). Records are kept in the training log.
15. The Administrator keeps all personnel records in a locked file (STF-05) and reviews these personnel policies annually under GOV-03.

Supervises daily work, covers absences with qualified staff, and sends ill staff home.
Follow these policies, complete training, report illness and rights violations, and keep resident information confidential.
Approves personnel policies and funds wages, leave and training.

policies.title: In-Service Training Plan for Staff
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Lead/House Manager, all direct support professionals, relief staff and night staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every direct care employee receives the orientation, competency-based training, continuing education, first aid and special training needed to care for residents safely, and that [AGENCY NAME] can prove it with a current plan and a training log for each employee.
policies.policy:
This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B6 — In service Training for Staff.

The in-service plan is part of [AGENCY NAME]'s plan of operation (22 CCR §80022), and the Administrator keeps it current. Direct care staff receive a 40-hour on-site orientation (17 CCR §56038(a)(1)) covering the program design, individual program plans (IPPs), resident rights, medications, emergencies and fire, special incident reports and abuse reporting.

Direct care staff also complete two 35-hour Direct Support Professional Training (DSPT) segments (17 CCR §56033): segment 1 in the first year and segment 2 within two years of hire, each with a test or challenge test. The DDS DSPT program is free to first- and second-year staff.

Continuing education (CE) under 17 CCR §56038 is 8 hours per year at Level 2 and 12 hours per year at Levels 3–4. Level 4 staff without 6 months' experience add 12 hours in the first six months. The Administrator will confirm the current text of §56038, which was amended effective May 1, 2026, and update this plan if it changes. For Levels 5 and 6, the Administrator will follow the CE requirement confirmed with the vendoring regional center.

Staff giving direct care must have first-aid training. Night staff must be trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and in first aid (22 CCR §85065.6). Staff who help residents with metered-dose or dry-powder inhalers must first be trained by a licensed professional. The training and trained staff names are documented in the personnel file, and the licensed professional reviews it annually (22 CCR §80075). Training on bloodborne pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) and on privacy and security under HIPAA (45 CFR 164.530) is provided at hire and annually.

definitions.definition: Training given to staff while employed, including orientation, DSPT, CE and special topics.
Direct Support Professional Training: two 35-hour competency-based segments given in years one and two of employment.
Annual hours of training required by Title 17 for direct care staff based on service level.
The record for each employee showing the date, topic, hours, trainer and sign-off for every training.

procedures: 1. Each January the Administrator writes the annual training calendar showing topic, date, trainer, hours and staff required, and files it in the plan of operation.

2. On the first day, each new direct care employee begins the 40-hour on-site orientation. Topics include program design, IPPs, resident rights, medication assistance, emergencies and fire, special incident reports and abuse reporting, and the person-specific needs of each resident.

3. The Administrator or Lead/House Manager gives orientation and signs off each topic. A new employee does not work alone with residents until orientation covering emergencies, rights and abuse reporting is complete and signed off.

4. The Administrator enrolls each direct care employee in DSPT segment 1 within the first year and segment 2 within two years of hire, using the free DDS program, and records test or challenge test results.

5. The Administrator assigns CE hours each year: 8 hours at Level 2, 12 hours at Levels 3–4, and Level 4 staff without 6 months' experience add 12 hours in their first six months. Hours follow the current §56038 text as confirmed by the Administrator.
6. Each direct care employee completes a first-aid course, and the certificate is filed. The Administrator tracks expiration dates and schedules renewals before they lapse.

7. Before working between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m., each staff member is trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and in first aid. The Administrator documents this before the first night shift.

8. Where a resident uses a metered-dose or dry-powder inhaler, the Administrator arranges training by a licensed professional. The Administrator records the procedures and the names of trained staff, files the record in each trained employee's personnel file, and arranges the professional's annual review (see HW-01).
9. At hire and annually, the Administrator trains all staff on bloodborne pathogens and infection control (HE-03) and on HIPAA privacy and confidentiality (IR-04).

10. Topics also include positive behavior support (BSP-01), rights and restrictions (IR-01, IR-02), health monitoring and choking (HW-03), and each resident's person-centered plan (PCS-01). Staff are trained on these before supporting a resident who needs them.
11. Staff sign an attendance sheet for each session. The Administrator records the date, topic, hours, trainer and result in the employee's training log.
12. When a resident is admitted or a resident's needs change, the Administrator provides person-specific training to all staff before the resident arrives or the change takes effect.

13. Each quarter, the Administrator reviews the training logs, identifies employees behind on hours or segments, and sets a written deadline to complete them. An employee who does not complete required training is not scheduled for unsupervised shifts.
14. Each year the Administrator evaluates the plan against incident reports, resident needs and staff feedback, and updates it under GOV-03.

Helps deliver orientation, observes competence on shift, and reports training gaps.
Attend and complete all required training and tests, keep first-aid certification current, and ask for help when unsure of a task.

policies.title: Facility Program Description (Plan of Operation and Title 17 Program Design)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body/owner, lead/house manager, all staff
policies.purpose: To describe in one written program description what [AGENCY NAME] will do, for whom, with what staff and how, so that CCL can approve a plan of operation under Title 22 and the regional center can approve a program design and service level under Title 17.
policies.policy:
This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B7 — Facility Program Description.

[AGENCY NAME] operates [FACILITY NAME] at [ADDRESS] as a licensed Adult Residential Facility serving up to [LICENSED CAPACITY] adults with developmental disabilities, and is vendored by [REGIONAL CENTER NAME] under WIC §4500 et seq. (the Lanterman Developmental Disabilities Services Act). The facility will be vendored as service code [915 (staff-operated) or 905 (owner-operated)] (17 CCR §54342; code 910 is owner-operated and 920 staff-operated for other facility types) at a requested service level of [LEVEL 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6].

The program description has two parts. The Title 22 plan of operation (22 CCR §80022) covers purpose, admissions, the admission agreement, staffing plan, in-service plan, floor plan and grounds sketch, menus, transportation, rate and refund policy, handling of resident money, consultants and the visiting policy. The Title 17 program design (17 CCR §56013) covers the organization chart, purpose and outcomes, entrance and exit criteria, program preparation duties, staff qualifications and duty statements, a sample schedule and a training plan. Level 3 and Level 4 designs add the further content required by §56013.

The program description is kept current. Changes to the plan of operation that affect services are reported to CCL within 10 working days (22 CCR §80061(e)). A service level change is allowed only on a change of ownership or when most residents' interdisciplinary (ID) teams identify a new need (17 CCR §56005(c)(1)). The program is designed so that residents receive services in a setting that supports choice, independence and community integration, consistent with the federal HCBS settings rule (42 CFR 441.301(c)).

definitions.definition: The written Title 22 description of the facility's purpose, services, staffing, policies and procedures, required for licensing.
The written Title 17 description of the vendored service, its outcomes, staffing, schedule and training, required for regional center vendorization.

The rate-reform residential service level for the staffing and support intensity a home provides. The crosswalk from legacy levels is: Level 3 = old 3/4A/4B; Level 4 = 4C–4E; Level 5 = 4F–4H; Level 6 = 4I.
Staff time spent on planning, training and preparing activities and supports for residents. It may count toward hours as set in 17 CCR §56004.

procedures: 1. The Administrator drafts the plan of operation using the required Title 22 topics in 22 CCR §80022 and the ARF-specific items, including the infection control plan and consultants (22 CCR §85022(a)(1)–(2)). It includes a statement of purpose, who will be served, services offered and the program's limits.

2. The Administrator writes the admission section: referral sources, entrance and exit criteria, admission agreement, and the resident's rights and visiting policy. Details are in SB-06, SB-05 and PCS-04.

3. The Administrator writes the staffing plan. Basic direct care staffing, whenever residents are under facility supervision, follows 17 CCR §56004: Level 2 one staff per up to 6 residents; Level 3 one per up to 3; Level 4 one per up to 2; Levels 5–6 one for the first resident. Above those resident counts, additional weekly direct care hours are added by level according to the §56004(d) table. Details are in STF-01.

4. The Administrator includes the program preparation hours (2 to 7 hours per resident per week as allowed by §56004) and the consultant hours required by level (8, 12 or 16 hours per consumer per six months, per §56004(f)), and names the consultants (see HW-02).
5. The Administrator attaches the floor plan and grounds sketch, sample menu (SB-07), transportation plan (HE-05), rate and refund policy, and policy on resident money (SB-08).

6. The rate section states that SSI/SSP residents pay the board-and-care amount of $1,444.07 per month and keep $182.00 per month for personal needs (amounts as of January 1, 2026; the Administrator confirms current amounts each January).

7. The Administrator writes the Title 17 program design (17 CCR §56013): organization chart, purpose and expected outcomes for residents, entrance and exit criteria, program preparation duties, staff duty statements (SB-01), a sample weekly schedule showing community integration and individual activities, and the training plan (SB-03). For Level 3 and Level 4, the Administrator adds the extra content §56013 requires.

8. The Administrator submits a written service level request to the regional center, including the administrator's qualifications. The regional center decides within 45 days (17 CCR §56005). The Administrator keeps the approval letter in the facility file.

9. The Administrator submits the plan of operation with the license application to CCL (Centralized Applications Bureau) and the program design to the vendoring regional center, and answers any requests for corrections promptly in writing.
10. The Governing body/Owner reviews and approves the program description before submission and after any major revision.
11. The Administrator gives each staff member a copy of the sections on their duties during orientation, and gives residents and authorized representatives a plain-language summary at admission.
12. The Administrator reviews the program description at least once a year, comparing it to actual practice, resident IPPs and outcomes (GOV-04), and revises it under GOV-03.

13. If a change affects services, such as capacity, staffing, program, floor plan or services offered, the Administrator updates the plan and notifies CCL within 10 working days. The Administrator also notifies the regional center. Organizational changes, address changes and changes of corporate CEO are reported on the same 10-working-day timeline (22 CCR §80061(e)).

14. The Administrator does not request or accept a change in service level except at a change of ownership or when most residents' ID teams identify a new need, and keeps the ID team documentation with the request (17 CCR §56005(c)(1)).

Approves the program description and the service level request, and funds staffing and consultants.
Carries out the schedule and daily program, and reports any gap between the written program and actual practice.
Provide referrals, review the service level and monitor program delivery (regional center role, not delegated to [AGENCY NAME]).

policies.title: Rules of Discipline and Personal Rights
policies.applies_to: Administrator, all staff, volunteers, residents and their authorized representatives
policies.purpose: To state how [AGENCY NAME] sets house rules without punishing residents, and to protect, tell residents about, and enforce each resident's personal rights.
policies.policy:
This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B8 — Rules of Discipline/Personal Rights.

[AGENCY NAME] does not discipline residents. Residents will never be subjected to corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, or other punitive action. Staff will never interfere with a resident's eating, sleeping or toileting as a consequence, and will never withhold shelter, clothing, medication or aids (22 CCR §80072(a)). Behavior concerns are handled through positive behavior support (BSP-01), not punishment.

Each resident has the following personal rights (22 CCR §80072(a)(1)–(10)): to be treated with dignity; to live in safe and comfortable accommodations; to be free from the punishments and interference listed above; to be told the address and phone number of the CCL complaint unit and how complaints are kept confidential; to religious freedom; to leave the facility at any time; to not be locked in any room or in the premises; to be free of restraining devices; to receive or reject medical care; and to be told the facility's visiting policy.

House rules and curfews are permitted but must be reasonable and must not take away rights. The right to leave the facility at any time does not apply to a resident who has a conservator or other legal authority that limits it. Exterior doors and windows may be locked only if residents can exit; any other securing means requires prior CCL approval. Postural supports and protective devices are used only under strict conditions and written authorization (see BSP-02 and IR-02), and a fire clearance is required before using a postural support that makes a resident nonambulatory (22 CCR §80020).

At admission, each resident and authorized representative are personally told of and given the list of rights. The rights and the visiting policy are posted prominently. The licensee ensures the rights are honored (22 CCR §80072(d)–(f)). All staff care for residents without physical or verbal abuse, exploitation or prejudice, and all staff are instructed to report violations of personal rights (22 CCR §80065(l)–(m)). These rules are consistent with the federal HCBS settings rule (42 CFR 441.301(c)) and nondiscrimination under the Americans with Disabilities Act.

definitions.definition: The rights each resident has under 22 CCR §80072, which the licensee must honor and may not waive or restrict except as the regulations allow.
General rules of the home, such as quiet hours and curfews, that apply fairly to all and do not remove personal rights.
Physical punishment or any penalty that causes pain, fear or humiliation, including withholding food, sleep or toileting.
The person with legal authority to act for a resident, such as a conservator or parent, or one the resident designates.
A device used only under strict regulatory conditions and authorization to help a resident's body position or protect from injury, never as a restraint for discipline.

procedures: 1. The Administrator writes the house rules with resident input, keeping them to what is needed for safety and for the home's smooth running, and reviews them at least once a year with residents.

2. Before posting, the Administrator checks that no house rule or curfew removes or limits a right listed in §80072(a). Any restriction personal to one resident goes through the rights restriction process in IR-02.

3. At or before admission, the Administrator personally reviews the list of personal rights with the resident and the authorized representative in plain language, in the person's preferred language or communication format (IR-06), and gives them a copy.
4. The resident and authorized representative sign and date an acknowledgment that they were advised of the rights. The Administrator files it in the resident's record (REC-01).
5. The Administrator posts the full list of personal rights and the visiting policy in a prominent place that residents and visitors can see, and checks monthly that the postings are in place.

6. At admission, and again whenever the information changes, the Administrator gives each resident the address and phone number of the CCL complaint unit ([LOCAL CCL REGIONAL OFFICE ADDRESS AND PHONE]), and the contact for the regional center's clients' rights advocate ([PHONE]). The Administrator explains that complaints are confidential.

7. The Administrator states the visiting policy in writing: visitors are welcome at times the resident chooses, with [VISITING POLICY DETAILS]. Any limit on a particular resident's visitors is allowed only through IR-02.
8. Staff do not use or threaten punishment of any kind. They do not withhold food, sleep, toileting, shelter, clothing, medication or aids, and do not use humiliation, ridicule, threats or coercion.

9. When a resident's behavior creates a concern, staff respond with the positive supports in BSP-01 and the resident's person-centered plan, and tell the Administrator. Restrictive interventions are used only as BSP-02 permits.

10. Staff never lock a resident in any room or in the premises. Exterior doors and windows may be locked only if residents can exit. Any other securing means requires prior CCL approval, which the Administrator keeps on file.

11. Residents may leave the facility at any time, subject to reasonable house rules, except where a conservator or other legal authority applies. Staff record the legal authority in the resident's record. Staff follow BSP-05 if a resident leaves and may be at risk.

12. Residents may receive or reject medical care. The Administrator respects each resident's choice and decision-making supports (IR-05) and records refusals, then notifies the physician and authorized representative.

13. Every employee signs an acknowledgment that they must report any violation of personal rights to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator investigates the same day, protects the resident, acts to correct the violation, and makes outside reports where required (BSP-03, BSP-04).
14. A staff member who violates a resident's rights is removed from resident care while the matter is reviewed and is disciplined up to termination under SB-02.
15. The Administrator reviews rights compliance at least quarterly through observation, resident interviews and grievance logs (IR-03, GOV-04), and records and corrects any problems.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures personal rights are honored, reviews rights at admission, posts rights and the visiting policy, investigates violations and corrects them.
Applies house rules fairly, monitors staff practice on every shift and reports concerns the same day.
Treat residents with dignity, never punish, and report any suspected rights violation immediately.
May raise concerns at any time with the Administrator, CCL, the regional center or the clients' rights advocate.

policies.title: Admission Policies, Referral and Transition In
policies.applies_to: All staff involved in referrals, admissions and the first 90 days of placement; the Administrator; the Admissions Coordinator; the Program Director; direct support staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] admits only people whose needs the home can meet, only after the home is licensed, vendored and approved for its service level, and in a way that protects each person's rights, choice and dignity during the move in.
policies.policy: This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B9 — Admission Policies. [AGENCY NAME] operates an Adult Residential Facility licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing (CCL) and vendored by the regional center (RC) as service code 915 (staff-operated) or 905 (owner-operated). The home will accept a first placement only when it holds (1) a CCL license, (2) a vendor number from the RC where the home is located, and (3) an RC-approved service level (ARM Level 2–6). The RC cannot approve or refer a person until the license is received (17 CCR §54320(c)), and no payment is made for services before vendorization and no referrals are accepted before vendorization (17 CCR §54326(d)(4)). [AGENCY NAME] will not accept, hold a bed for, or begin services for any person before those conditions are met. The Administrator will have completed the regional center residential services orientation before the first admission (17 CCR §56003). Before each admission, the agency determines that the program can meet the person's needs and completes a written Needs and Services Plan (22 CCR §85068.2). Admission is voluntary and based on the person's choice. Decisions are made without discrimination on the basis of disability type, race, color, national origin, language, religion, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity, consistent with the ADA and Title VI. The home will not admit a person whose needs exceed the approved service level, the program design, the license or the physical plant. The service level may change only as allowed by 17 CCR §56005 (on a change of ownership, or when most residents' ID teams identify a new need). The home will not admit a person who needs a level of care the license does not allow.

definitions.definition: The written plan required before admission under 22 CCR §85068.2. It documents the person's desires and background, service needs, medical and functional assessments, the initial assessment on or before the day of admission, the individual emergency intervention plan, and how the facility will meet the person's needs.
The regional center's approval of [AGENCY NAME] as a provider, evidenced by a vendor number, for service code 915 or 905 at the facility's location.
A person with legal authority to act for the resident, such as a conservator or other legally authorized representative.
The ARM level (2 through 6) approved by the regional center for the facility under 17 CCR §56005.
A person who is unable to leave a building unassisted in an emergency. Nonambulatory residents, and residents age 65 or older, require a separate fire clearance before admission.

procedures: Before accepting any referral, the Administrator verifies and records that the home holds a current CCL license, an RC vendor number for service code [915/905], and an approved service level. If any is missing, the referral is declined in writing and the RC referring staff is told the home cannot yet accept placements.
The Administrator completes the RC residential services orientation before the first admission and files the completion record in the Administrator's file.

The Admissions Coordinator logs each referral (date, source, person's name, requested service level) in the Referral Log. Referrals are accepted only from the vendoring RC, a placement agency, or the person or authorized representative, and only after vendorization.

The Admissions Coordinator gives the person and authorized representative a copy of the program description, the home's rate and refund policy, and the visiting policy, in plain language and in the person's preferred language or format.

Before the move, the person is invited to visit the home, meet the housemates and staff, and see the bedroom. Visits and the person's reaction are documented. The person's own choice about where and with whom to live is recorded.

The Administrator and Program Director review the referral packet, including the Individual Program Plan (IPP), medical and psychological information, behavior and health supports, and the person's requested supports, against the program design, the staffing plan, the approved service level and the building. The review is documented on the Admission Decision Form.

Admission is declined or deferred, with written reasons given to the referring RC, if the home cannot meet the person's needs, if staffing or the approved level is not adequate, or if the physical plant does not fit the person's mobility needs. Declines never rest on a prohibited basis.

If the person is nonambulatory or age 65 or older, the Administrator confirms that the separate fire clearance has been obtained from the local fire authority before admission and files a copy. The admission date is not set until clearance is received.

Before admission, the Program Director completes the written Needs and Services Plan under 22 CCR §85068.2, including the person's desires and background, entrance to the facility, specific service needs, the written medical assessment, mental and emotional functioning, any mental health intake assessment, the functional capabilities assessment, and the facility's plans to meet needs. The client, authorized representative, participating relatives, the RC service coordinator and anyone the person chooses take part.

On or before the day of admission, the Program Director completes the HSC 1180.4(a) initial assessment with input from the person, the authorized representative and any person the client chooses. The assessment records any advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion or manual restraint (honored unless it violates law or endangers safety), early warning signs and triggers, calming techniques, medical conditions that raise restraint risk, and trauma history. The individual emergency intervention plan is completed and added to the Needs and Services Plan.
If the person has a restricted health condition, the Restricted Health Condition Care Plan is added to the Needs and Services Plan and shared with the nursing consultant (see HW-02).

The Administrator reviews and signs a written Admission Agreement with the person or authorized representative before or at admission. It states the rate and the SSI/SSP board-and-care portion, the refund policy, the visiting policy, the services included in the rate, and the discharge conditions. The agency gives a signed copy to the person or representative and keeps the original in the individual record.

At admission, the Administrator or designee personally reviews the list of personal rights with the person and the authorized representative, gives them the written list, and records that on the Personal Rights Acknowledgment. The CCL complaint unit address and phone number and the visiting policy are explained. The rights and visiting policy are posted prominently (22 CCR §80072).

On the day of admission, staff inventory and record the person's belongings with the person (see SB-08), review medications and orders for assistance with self-administered medications (see HW-01), and review dietary needs (see SB-07 and HE-04).

For the first 30 days after admission, the Program Director meets with the person and staff weekly to review how the transition is going, adjusts supports, and keeps notes in the consumer notes. The RC service coordinator is notified of any significant concern within one business day.

Within [number] days after admission, the Program Director ensures the Needs and Services Plan and the person's IPP supports are consistent and that the first progress report is scheduled (see PCS-01 and PCS-02).
The Administrator reviews the Referral Log and Admission Decision Forms quarterly for patterns of declines or delays and reports the review to the governing body (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Verifies license, vendor number and service level before any referral is accepted; completes RC orientation; makes the final admission decision; signs the Admission Agreement; obtains fire clearance when required.
Maintains the Referral Log, communicates with referral sources, gathers referral packets and schedules pre-admission visits.
Completes the Needs and Services Plan and the HSC 1180.4(a) initial assessment, coordinates the transition and monitors the first 30 days.
Welcome the person, assist with the inventory of belongings, follow the plan and record the person's adjustment in consumer notes.
Provides the referral, the IPP and the vendor and service level approvals; takes part in the planning.

documentation: Referral Log and referral packets
Admission Decision Form with reasons for any decline
Copy of CCL license, vendor number and service level approval
Administrator's RC orientation completion record
Fire clearance (nonambulatory or 65+ residents)
Needs and Services Plan, HSC 1180.4(a) initial assessment, individual emergency intervention plan, and Restricted Health Condition Care Plan if applicable
Signed Admission Agreement with rate, refund and visiting policy
Personal Rights Acknowledgment
Belongings inventory
Transition notes for the first 30 days

policies.title: Sample Menu and Food Service Plan
policies.applies_to: Administrator, cooks and food service staff, direct support staff, nursing consultant, residents
policies.purpose: To make sure residents receive nutritious, appealing meals that reflect their choices, cultural preferences and individual dietary needs, and that the home's menus and food service staffing are documented and consistent with the plan of operation.
policies.policy: This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B10 — Sample Menu. A sample menu is included in the plan of operation (22 CCR §80022) and is attached to this policy as Attachment A ([ATTACHMENT A – SAMPLE MENU]). [AGENCY NAME] employs food service staff, or assigns trained direct support staff, in sufficient numbers so that residents' food service needs are met (22 CCR §85065(e)(1)). Modified diets and other individual needs identified in each resident's Needs and Services Plan (22 CCR §85068.2) are accommodated. Menus are planned in advance, posted or provided to residents, and any substitution is recorded. Residents take part in choosing meals and snacks to the extent they wish.

definitions.definition: A written menu showing the types and variety of meals and snacks the home regularly serves, kept with the plan of operation.

A diet changed in texture, consistency, content or amount because of a medical condition, a swallowing or choking risk, an allergy, or a religious or personal need, as identified in the Needs and Services Plan or ordered by a physician.
Any change from the posted menu, including a resident's own request for a different food.

procedures: The Administrator, with residents and the cook, develops a written menu cycle of at least [number] weeks that includes breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks, varied from day to day and by season, and attaches the sample menu to the plan of operation as Attachment A.

At admission and at each Needs and Services Plan review, the Program Director records each resident's food allergies, intolerances, preferences, cultural or religious needs, and any modified diet in the Needs and Services Plan.

A modified or therapeutic diet is served only on a written physician or dietitian order. The order is kept in the resident's record and posted in the kitchen where staff can see it, protecting the resident's privacy.
Where a resident has a swallowing or choking risk, the diet texture and mealtime supports in the plan are followed exactly and staff are trained on them before serving the resident (see HW-03).
The Administrator reviews menus with the nursing consultant at least [frequency] and whenever a resident's dietary needs change, and records the review.
The Administrator posts the weekly menu in the dining area, in plain language, with pictures or other formats as residents need, and gives each resident a copy on request.
At [frequency] house meetings, residents give suggestions and choose meals, snacks and special occasion foods. Suggestions are recorded and used in menu planning.

Staff record any substitution on the Menu Substitution Log (date, meal, what was served instead and the reason). A resident's own preference for another food is honored where it is consistent with the resident's diet orders.

Cooks and food service staff, or direct support staff who prepare food, use the staffing schedule so that someone trained in safe food handling and in resident dietary needs is available at every meal. The Administrator confirms coverage against the staffing plan weekly.
