Staff encourage and assist residents to take part in shopping, preparing and serving meals according to their goals, and record the participation in consumer notes.
Staff follow safe food storage, temperature, cleaning and hand washing practices (see HE-03 and HE-04). Food is not withheld or used as a punishment or a reward.
Staff keep records of the menus as served for [number] months, and make them and the Menu Substitution Log available to CCL and the regional center on request.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the menu cycle and sample menu, ensures food service staffing is adequate, and reviews substitutions and resident feedback.
Records dietary needs in the Needs and Services Plan and makes sure diet orders are current.
Prepare meals following the posted menu and diet orders, record substitutions and keep the kitchen safe and clean.
Assist residents at meals, follow texture and mealtime supports, and report changes in eating or weight.
Reviews menus and modified diets for residents with health needs.
Share preferences and take part in meal planning as they choose.

documentation: Sample menu (Attachment A) and menu cycle
Weekly posted menus as served
Menu Substitution Log
Physician or dietitian diet orders
House meeting notes on menu suggestions
Nursing consultant menu review notes

policies.title: Control of Property, Personal Funds and Resident Money
policies.applies_to: Administrator, bookkeeper or designee, direct support staff, residents and their authorized representatives and representative payees
policies.purpose: To protect residents' ownership and control of their own money and belongings, to prevent loss or misuse, and to set clear procedures for any money or property the home handles at a resident's written request.
policies.policy: This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B11 — Control of Property. Residents may keep and control their own cash and personal items, and each resident has individual storage space for personal belongings. [AGENCY NAME] will not take, use, withhold or restrict access to a resident's money or property except as a resident or authorized representative has agreed in writing, and any restriction is handled under IR-02. If the facility handles resident money, it is kept separate from operating funds and the procedure is described in the plan of operation (22 CCR §80022). Residents' personal rights (22 CCR §80072) and the person-centered plan (22 CCR §85068.2) guide how each person manages money. SSI/SSP board-and-care is $1,444.07 per month, paid by the resident or the representative payee, and the resident keeps $182.00 per month for personal needs. The regional center rate is payment in full (17 CCR §54326(a)(12)). [AGENCY NAME] does not charge residents or representatives extra for services covered by the rate.

definitions.definition: Any cash, check, benefit payment, bank balance or other funds belonging to a resident.
The $182.00 per month the resident keeps from SSI/SSP for personal needs. It is not part of the board-and-care payment.
A person or organization appointed by the Social Security Administration to receive and manage a person's benefits.
The individual written record of each deposit and withdrawal, with receipts and signatures, kept for each resident whose money the home holds.
An itemized, signed list of a resident's belongings, made at admission and updated when items come or go.

procedures: At admission, the Program Director asks each person and the authorized representative how the person wants to manage money and belongings, and records the choices (including who is the representative payee, if any) in the Needs and Services Plan.

Staff help each resident to hold and spend their own money to the extent the person wants and is able, and teach money skills when the person's plan includes that goal. Support given is recorded in consumer notes.

Each resident has a bedroom dresser or closet and a lockable or otherwise secure space for valuables, if wanted. Staff do not open or search a resident's personal storage unless the resident agrees or there is an immediate danger to health or safety, and any such action is documented.

At admission, a staff member and the resident (or representative) complete an itemized property inventory, including clothing, electronics, jewelry and other valuables, and both sign and date it. The resident or representative receives a copy.
The inventory is updated when the resident acquires or disposes of an item, and at least every [number] months it is reviewed with the resident. The updated list is signed by both.

The home holds a resident's money only when the resident or authorized representative requests it in writing. The Written Authorization to Hold Funds states the amounts and purpose, may be withdrawn at any time, and is kept in the record.

Funds held are kept in a [separate resident trust account / locked cash box] that is kept apart from operating funds and from other residents' funds. Staff never combine resident money with agency money, borrow from it or use it for agency expenses.

For each resident whose money is held, the bookkeeper keeps an individual ledger recording the date, amount, purpose, balance and the signature of the staff member. A receipt is kept for each purchase and the resident or representative signs for every withdrawal.
Two people (the staff member and the resident, or a second staff member) count and verify cash held whenever it is deposited or withdrawn.
The Administrator reconciles every ledger with the cash or bank balance monthly, signs the reconciliation and gives the resident or representative a statement on request, or at least quarterly.

The home helps residents deposit the SSI/SSP check or other income as they choose. The board-and-care amount of $1,444.07 is paid by the resident or representative payee under the Admission Agreement. The resident always keeps the $182.00 personal needs amount, and the home does not deduct charges from it without the resident's written consent.

No staff member may borrow from, lend to, sell to, accept gifts of value from or accept a bequest from a resident (see STF-06). Staff who suspect that anyone is misusing a resident's money or property report it under BSP-03.

If a resident's property is lost, stolen or damaged, staff report it to the Administrator the same day, search for the item, document the findings and tell the resident or representative. Where the loss is due to the home's negligence, the Administrator arranges repair or replacement as appropriate.

When a resident leaves, the Administrator returns all money and property with a final accounting, using the signed inventory and ledger, and the resident or representative signs a receipt. Items left behind are held and returned as set out in the Admission Agreement.

The Administrator reviews ledgers, inventories and any complaints about money or property at least annually during the quality review (see GOV-04), and makes them available to CCL and the regional center on request.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures resident funds are kept separately, reconciles ledgers monthly, investigates losses and ensures no charges are made beyond the rate.
Maintains ledgers, receipts and bank records for any funds held.
Records each resident's money management choices and goals in the Needs and Services Plan.
Support residents to manage their own money, complete inventories, never use or borrow resident funds, and report concerns.
Decide how the person's money is used and sign for deposits, withdrawals and statements.

documentation: Written Authorization to Hold Funds
Individual resident money ledgers with receipts and signatures
Monthly reconciliation signed by the Administrator
Itemized property inventory signed by staff and the resident
Loss, theft or damage reports
Final accounting and receipt on discharge
Admission Agreement showing the rate and the SSI/SSP board-and-care amount

policies.title: Neighborhood Complaint Policy (Non-Resident Owner Homes of Six or Fewer)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, the designated neighborhood contact person, all staff who may receive a call or visit from a neighbor
policies.purpose: To give neighbors a clear, respectful way to raise concerns about the home and to make sure each concern is logged, answered and resolved in a timely way.
policies.policy: This policy meets LIC 281 (9/04), Section B, item B15 — Neighborhood Complaint Policy. It applies only to non-resident owner community care facilities providing residential care for six or fewer persons. If the owner or licensee lives in the home, the Administrator marks this policy 'Not applicable – owner resides in the home' on the policy index and in the plan of operation. If it applies, [AGENCY NAME] names a contact person and phone number so neighbors can raise complaints, logs each complaint with the date, the response and the resolution, and keeps this policy with the plan of operation (22 CCR §80022) and the application materials (22 CCR §80018). Complaints from neighbors are never answered by disclosing any resident's confidential information. Neighbors' concerns never lead to any retaliation against residents.

definitions.definition: Any concern raised by a neighbor or member of the community about the operation of the home, such as noise, parking, trash, appearance of the property, or visitors.
The staff member named by [AGENCY NAME] to receive neighborhood complaints: [CONTACT PERSON NAME], [PHONE].
An owner or licensee who does not live in the facility.

procedures: The Administrator decides whether the home is a non-resident owner home serving six or fewer. If the owner lives in the home, the Administrator records 'Not applicable' and no further steps are needed.
If it applies, the Administrator names a contact person and a working phone number, [CONTACT PERSON NAME], [PHONE], available [days and hours], and records them on the Neighborhood Contact Notice.

Before the home opens and again whenever the contact person or number changes, the Administrator gives the Neighborhood Contact Notice to the neighbors immediately next to and across from the home at [ADDRESS], by hand delivery or mail, and keeps a list of who received it and when.

All staff are told in orientation that any neighbor who calls or visits with a concern is to be treated politely and referred to the contact person or Administrator the same day. Staff do not argue, make promises or discuss residents.
The contact person records each complaint on the Neighborhood Complaint Log: date and time, the complainant's name and contact details (if given), the nature of the concern, and who took the call.
The contact person acknowledges the complaint to the neighbor within [one business day] and tells the neighbor when to expect a reply.

The contact person looks into the concern, speaks with staff on duty, and works with the Administrator on a response. Where the concern is valid, the Administrator takes corrective action (for example, adjusting trash collection, parking or noise) and records what was done.

The contact person or Administrator replies to the neighbor, by phone or in writing, within [five business days] with what was found and what was done, and records the response date and outcome in the log.

If a complaint involves possible abuse, neglect or a health and safety risk to a resident, the Administrator treats it under BSP-03 and BSP-04 and reports as required. If the neighbor remains unsatisfied, the Administrator offers a meeting and records the result.
The Administrator reviews the log at least quarterly for repeat or unresolved issues, and a summary is given to the governing body (see GOV-04).
The Administrator keeps this policy, the Neighborhood Contact Notice and the Complaint Log with the plan of operation, and shows them to CCL and the regional center on request.

responsibilities.duty: Decides applicability, names the contact person, ensures neighbors are notified, reviews the log and approves corrective actions.
Receives, logs, investigates and answers neighborhood complaints within the stated timelines.
Treat neighbors courteously, refer all concerns to the contact person the same day and keep resident information confidential.

documentation: Applicability determination (applicable / not applicable)
Neighborhood Contact Notice and list of neighbors notified
Neighborhood Complaint Log with date, response and resolution
Written replies to neighbors
Quarterly log review notes

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing body (owner or board), Administrator, Program Director, all managers
policies.purpose: To define who is responsible for the home, how the home is organized and governed, the qualifications and duties of the Administrator, and when changes must be reported to CCL.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by [OWNER / BOARD OF DIRECTORS], the licensee, which is ultimately responsible for compliance with licensing law and regional center requirements. A certified administrator is responsible for the facility. The Administrator is at least 21 years old, holds a high school diploma or GED, and holds a current Adult Residential Facility administrator certificate (22 CCR §85064). The Administrator completes HIV/TB training within six months of becoming the administrator and updates it every two years (22 CCR §85064(k)). For regional center vendorization, the Administrator also meets the Title 17 experience requirement of 6, 9 or 12 months of developmental disability experience for Level 2, 3 or 4, unless the regional center waives it, and completes 8, 12 or 12 hours of continuing education each year for Levels 2, 3 and 4 respectively (17 CCR §56037). The home keeps an organization chart in the program design (17 CCR §56013) and a current plan of operation (22 CCR §80016). Within 10 working days, [AGENCY NAME] reports to CCL any organizational change, change of mailing address, change of corporate chief executive officer (with fingerprints) and any plan of operation change that affects services (22 CCR §80061(e)).

definitions.definition: The person or entity that holds the CCL license and is legally responsible for the facility.
The owner, partners or board of directors that sets policy and holds the Administrator accountable.
A person who has completed the CDSS Initial Certification Training Program, passed the state exam and holds a current administrator certificate.
The written Title 17 description of the home's purpose, outcomes, staffing, entrance and exit criteria and organization.

procedures: The governing body adopts a written statement of organization naming the licensee, the governing body members, the Administrator and the lines of authority, and attaches it to the plan of operation.

The governing body appoints a certified Administrator who meets the age, education and certification requirements and the Title 17 experience for the home's service level. The Administrator's certificate, diploma or GED, HIV/TB training and experience documents are filed in the Administrator's personnel file (see STF-05 and STF-07).

The Administrator completes HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator and renews it every two years. The Administrator tracks CDSS recertification (40 hours of continuing education every two years) and the Title 17 annual continuing education hours for the home's level on a training calendar and gives the governing body proof of completion.

If the Administrator will be absent, the governing body names in writing a qualified, certified person to act in the Administrator's place and records the dates. Staff are told who is in charge at all times.
The Administrator keeps a current organization chart and job descriptions (see SB-01) as part of the program design, and updates them when positions change.
The Administrator reports to the governing body at least [quarterly] on resident outcomes, incidents, staffing, complaints, finances and licensing and regional center findings.
The governing body reviews the plan of operation, program design and this manual annually and whenever the home's services change (see GOV-03).

The Administrator tells the CCL regional office in writing within 10 working days of any change in the organization, the mailing address, or the corporate chief executive officer (with fingerprints for the new officer), and of any plan of operation change that affects services.

The Administrator tells the regional center promptly about any change to the Administrator, ownership, service level need or program design, and for a service level change follows the regional center process under 17 CCR §56005.
The Administrator ensures that required reports (see REC-02 and BSP-04) are made on time, and ensures licensing and regional center monitors are given prompt access (see GOV-06).
The governing body documents its meetings, decisions and annual evaluation of the Administrator, and keeps the minutes in the administrative file.

responsibilities.duty: Holds final responsibility for compliance, appoints and evaluates the Administrator, approves policies and ensures resources are adequate.
Directs daily operations, keeps certification and training current, supervises staff, makes required reports and works with CCL and the regional center.
Carries out the program design and supports the Administrator in supervising direct support staff.
Acts for the Administrator during absences within the written delegation.

documentation: Statement of organization and organization chart
Administrator certificate, education, experience and training records
HIV/TB and continuing education tracking calendar
Written delegation for absences
Governing body minutes and annual evaluation
10-working-day change notifications to CCL and proof of delivery

policies.title: Licensure, Vendorization and Provider Agreements
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing body, Administrator, anyone preparing or maintaining licensing and vendorization files
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] obtains and keeps its CCL license, its regional center vendorization and its HCBS Provider Agreement, and when it may begin to accept referrals and bill for services.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not accept residents, advertise vacancies as available for regional center placement, or bill for services until it holds a CCL license for the home and a regional center vendor number for the service. CDSS Community Care Licensing (Centralized Applications Bureau) licenses the home as an Adult Residential Facility, and the process generally takes 90–120 days. The application fee for a 4–6 bed home is $908, paid with the application, and the annual fee is $454, with a 50% late fee added if the annual fee is late (HSC §1523.1). The financial plan of operation shows start-up funds that cover the first three months of operation (22 CCR §85018). The Administrator completes CCL orientation before the application is filed (22 CCR §80018). The home is then vendored by the regional center where it is located (17 CCR §54326(a)(14)), with one vendorization per service per location, using form DS 1890, a copy of the license or proof of application, and the signed HCBS Provider Agreement (17 CCR §54310). The service code is 915 for a staff-operated home and 905 for an owner-operated home (17 CCR §54342). The Administrator completes the regional center residential services orientation before the first admission (17 CCR §56003).

definitions.definition: The regional center vendor application form that discloses ownership, service type, capacity and consultants.
The signed agreement, required for Medi-Cal-eligible services, that the provider will meet the federal home and community-based settings requirements and the regional center's terms.
Title 17 service codes for a staff-operated (915) or owner-operated (905) residential facility.
The regional center's approval of a provider to deliver and be paid for a specific service at a specific location.

procedures: The Administrator and licensee attend CCL orientation before filing and keep the completion record on file.

The licensee prepares the application package for the CDSS Centralized Applications Bureau: the application forms, the fee of $908 for a 4–6 bed home, the Administrator's name, addresses, background and qualifications, proof of the Administrator's certification and education, and lease and landlord information if the property is leased. The Administrator keeps a copy of everything submitted.

The licensee completes the financial plan of operation on the CDSS forms, showing start-up funds sufficient for the first three months of operation. If CCL asks, the licensee provides written verification of those funds (22 CCR §85018).

The Administrator tracks the licensing process (generally 90–120 days) on a timeline, answers CCL requests promptly, schedules the pre-licensing inspection and orders the fire clearance through the Centralized Applications Bureau.

Once the application is filed or the license is issued, the Administrator contacts the regional center in the area where the home is located and starts the vendor application, because vendorization is by the regional center where the facility is located.

The Administrator completes DS 1890 with all required disclosures, the service type (915 or 905), the capacity and any consultants, and attaches a copy of the license or proof of application, and the signed HCBS Provider Agreement (17 CCR §54310).

The Administrator follows the standardized vendorization steps and dates: the regional center has 15 days to screen for minimum requirements, then 30 days to confirm the application is complete (the applicant has 30 days to cure any gaps), then 45 days to approve or deny. The Administrator records each date in the Vendorization Tracker.

The Administrator requests the service level the home will provide (ARM Level 2–6) in writing, with administrator qualifications, under 17 CCR §56005, and keeps the regional center's written decision.

The Administrator accepts no referral and makes no placement, and [AGENCY NAME] bills no services, before the license is received and vendorization is complete. The regional center cannot approve or refer until the license is received (17 CCR §54320(c)), and no payment is made for services before vendorization (17 CCR §54326(d)(4)).
The Administrator completes the regional center residential services orientation before the first admission and files the record.

The licensee keeps one vendorization for each service at each location. If the home moves or adds a service or location, the licensee starts a new application with the regional center where that location is.
The licensee pays the $454 annual license fee on time, and calendars the due date [60] days ahead so the 50% late fee is not triggered. Proof of payment is filed.

The Administrator keeps the license, vendor number, service code, service level approval, signed HCBS Provider Agreement and fee receipts in a Licensing and Vendorization binder, posts the license where required, and makes the binder available to CCL and the regional center.

The Administrator reports changes to CCL within 10 working days (see GOV-01), tells the regional center of changes that affect vendorization or service level, and complies with the vendor requirements under 17 CCR §54326, including monitoring access and record retention (see GOV-05 and GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Signs applications and agreements, provides the financial plan and start-up funds, pays fees and holds legal responsibility for the license.
Completes orientations, prepares and tracks the licensing and vendorization applications, requests the service level and keeps the binder current.
Tracks fee due dates and keeps payment records.
Review applications, inspect the home, issue the license, vendorize the provider and approve the service level.

documentation: CCL orientation and regional center residential services orientation completion records
Licensing application package, fee receipt and financial plan of operation
License and fire clearance
DS 1890, signed HCBS Provider Agreement and vendor number
Service level request and approval letter
Vendorization Tracker with dates
Annual fee payment records

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designated alternates, all direct care staff, and the governing body of [AGENCY NAME], Adult Residential Facility (service code 915/905, ARM Levels 2-6)
policies.purpose: To keep the Policy & Procedure Manual and the Plan of Operation current, controlled, version-dated and signed off by staff. It also ensures that regulatory changes, including the DDS Special Incident Reporting amendments effective 5/1/2026, are carried into daily practice and reported to Community Care Licensing (CCL) on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] reviews this manual at least once every 12 months and whenever a regulation, licensing notice or regional center directive changes. The Plan of Operation (22 CCR §80022) must be kept current. Any plan-of-operation change that affects services is reported to CCL within 10 working days (22 CCR §80061(e)). The Administrator tracks the DDS Special Incident Reporting amendments effective 5/1/2026 (17 CCR §§54327, 56026 and 56038) and updates every affected policy and training. Staff training content under 17 CCR §56038 is checked against the current text. Every policy carries a version number and effective date, and each staff member signs that they have read the current version. No official checklist items are assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: The written plan required by 22 CCR §80022. It covers purpose, admissions, admission agreement, staffing plan, in-service plan, floor plan and grounds sketch, menus, transportation, rate and refund policy, handling of resident money, consultants and visiting policy.

Any change to a plan-of-operation element that alters what is provided to residents, who provides it, or how. Examples are a new staffing pattern, a new rate or refund policy, a change in the visiting policy, a change in admission criteria, or a new consultant.
The current, signed and version-dated master copy of a policy, kept by the Administrator.
The DDS Special Incident Reporting rulemaking effective 5/1/2026, which amended 17 CCR §§54327, 56026 and 56038.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], is the document owner. The Administrator keeps a Master Policy Index listing each policy ID, title, version number, effective date, last review date and next review date.
At adoption, the Administrator assigns each policy Version 1.0 and an effective date, and records the governing body's approval signature and date on the index.

The Administrator schedules a full manual review every year in [REVIEW MONTH]. The review is completed within 30 days. Each policy is read against current regulations, the Plan of Operation, actual practice and the findings of the quality review (GOV-04).

Every month the Administrator checks the CCL, DDS and [VENDORING REGIONAL CENTER] websites and notices for new or amended regulations, provider bulletins and directives. The Administrator logs what was checked, the date and any action needed on the Regulatory Watch Log.

For the SIR amendments effective 5/1/2026, the Administrator compares the amended 17 CCR §§54327, 56026 and 56038 against the current official text. The Administrator then updates BSP-04, REC-02, PCS-02, GOV-04 and STF-03, including the 40-hour orientation and continuing-education content under 17 CCR §56038. The Administrator records the date of comparison and the changes made.

Any regulatory change, license or vendor monitoring finding, or incident-review lesson that shows a policy is out of date triggers a policy review. The review is started within 10 days and finished within 30 days of discovery, unless the rule sets a sooner date.
The Administrator revises the policy, marks changes (redline or revision note), increases the version number, enters the new effective date and keeps the prior version marked SUPERSEDED.

Before finalizing, the Administrator decides whether the revision changes an element of the Plan of Operation that affects services (22 CCR §80022). The Administrator records the decision and reason on the Change Determination Form.

If the change affects services, the Administrator submits the revised plan-of-operation pages or a written notice to CCL at [LICENSING REGIONAL OFFICE ADDRESS/EMAIL] within 10 working days of the change (22 CCR §80061(e)). The Administrator keeps the transmittal and proof of delivery. If the change also affects the program the regional center vendored, the Administrator notifies [VENDORING REGIONAL CENTER] as the vendor agreement requires.

The Administrator posts or distributes the revised policy and trains staff on it. Each staff member signs and dates the Policy Acknowledgment Sheet within 14 days of the effective date. The signature is kept in the personnel file (STF-05). Staff hired later sign during orientation.

The Administrator keeps one controlled printed manual in [LOCATION] and an electronic copy with restricted edit access. The manual is available to staff at all times and to CCL and regional center monitors on request (GOV-06).
Each annual review is documented on the Annual Review Log with the reviewer's name, date, policies changed and policies confirmed unchanged. The governing body signs the log.
Superseded versions and review logs are kept for at least five years, to match the vendor record-retention period in GOV-05 and REC-01.
The Administrator reports the number of policies revised, overdue reviews and overdue staff sign-offs to the governing body at its next meeting (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Approves the manual at adoption and each annual review, and signs the Annual Review Log.
Owns the manual, tracks regulatory changes, makes the services-change determination, files notices with CCL within 10 working days, and trains staff.
Keeps the controlled manual and acknowledgment sheets available to inspectors in the Administrator's absence.
Read each revised policy and sign the acknowledgment within 14 days; follow current versions only.

documentation: Master Policy Index with version dates
Annual Review Log signed by the governing body
Regulatory Watch Log
Change Determination Forms
CCL submissions and proof of delivery for plan-of-operation changes
Policy Acknowledgment Sheets in personnel files
Superseded policy versions

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body, program staff and nursing/health consultants of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To review incidents, Special Incident Reports (SIRs), consumer notes and progress-report data on a set schedule, to act on barriers, and to review each death for cause and lessons learned. This supports the HCBS settings expectations and positions the home to earn the Quality Incentive Program (QIP) portion of the rate.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] runs a documented quality improvement review at least quarterly. It covers incident reports, SIRs, consumer notes and quarterly progress-report data, and it feeds the program design outcomes required by 17 CCR §56013. Level 4 quarterly reports include a data summary, barriers and actions taken (17 CCR §56026). The Administrator confirms with [VENDORING REGIONAL CENTER] how this applies to Levels 5-6. Every death is reviewed for cause and lessons learned, in addition to the reports required by 22 CCR §80061. The review supports compliance with the HCBS settings rule at 42 CFR 441.301(c). Records are kept at least five years and made available for monitoring (17 CCR §54326(a)(2)-(3)). QIP can earn the other 10% of the rate, and eligibility requires HCBS, EVV and audit compliance. No official checklist items are assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: A meeting held at least once every three months, with minutes, to review incident, SIR, consumer-note and progress-report data and to assign corrective actions.
A structured review of each resident death covering cause, circumstances, care provided, contributing factors and lessons learned.
The DDS Quality Incentive Program, which can earn the other 10% of the residential rate beyond the 90% base paid to a new vendor.
Electronic Visit Verification, used where it applies to the service.

procedures: The Administrator sets four quality review dates each year ([Q1 DATE], [Q2 DATE], [Q3 DATE], [Q4 DATE]) and invites the governing body representative, the nurse or health consultant, the program director or lead staff and a direct care staff representative.

One week before each review, the Administrator compiles: all incident reports and SIRs for the quarter; consumer notes (PCS-02); the quarterly progress reports; medication errors; falls and injuries; restraint or rights-restriction data; complaints and grievances; and missing-person events.
The Administrator prepares a one-page data summary with counts, trends by resident and by shift, and comparison with the prior quarter.
At the meeting the group identifies patterns, barriers to each resident's IPP goals, and system causes. It assigns each corrective action to a named person with a due date.

For Level 4 residents, the Administrator makes sure the quarterly report sent to the service coordinator includes the data summary, barriers and actions taken (17 CCR §56026). For Levels 5-6, the Administrator obtains written direction from [VENDORING REGIONAL CENTER] and the Administrator records it in the QI file.
Within 14 days of the meeting, the Administrator finishes the minutes, sends them to the governing body and puts action items on the Corrective Action Tracker.
At the next review, the group checks whether each action was completed and whether it worked, and closes or re-opens it.

Within two working days of any death, the Administrator confirms the required reports were made. CCL is notified by the next working day and a written report is sent within 7 days (22 CCR §80061). The authorized representative and others required by that section are also notified (BSP-04, HW-05, REC-02).

Within 30 days of each death, the Administrator convenes a mortality review. Participants include the nurse or health consultant, the primary physician's records when available, and staff on duty. The review covers the cause of death, recent change of condition, medical and behavioral history, the response, any medication or choking/seizure factors, and any facility or system contribution.

The mortality review writes down lessons learned and corrective actions, such as retraining, a protocol change, or a new health-monitoring step. The Administrator updates affected policies (GOV-03), shares findings with staff within 14 days with names and personal details protected, and cooperates with any regional center or CCL review.

The Administrator checks each year that the home meets the QIP prerequisites: HCBS settings compliance, EVV compliance where applicable, and independent audit or review compliance (GOV-05). The Administrator records the status on the QIP Readiness Checklist.
The Administrator reviews HCBS settings performance (IR-01, IR-02), including rights restrictions, visitor access and community integration, and records any gaps and fixes in the quarterly minutes.
The Administrator reports the quarterly results, open corrective actions and mortality review findings to the governing body at its next meeting (GOV-01).
QI minutes, data summaries, mortality reviews and tracker entries are kept for at least five years and made available to CCL and regional center monitors on request (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Reviews quarterly results and mortality reviews, and ensures corrective actions get resources.
Schedules and leads reviews, compiles data, confirms Level 4-6 reporting requirements, runs mortality reviews and keeps the tracker.
Takes part in health-data and mortality reviews and advises on clinical corrective actions (HW-02).
Complete accurate incident reports and consumer notes on time and take part in corrective actions.

documentation: Quarterly QI meeting minutes and data summaries
Corrective Action Tracker
Mortality review reports
Quarterly progress reports with Level 4 data summary, barriers and actions
Written regional center direction on Levels 5-6 reporting
QIP Readiness Checklist

policies.title: Regional Center Billing, Service Documentation and Independent Audit/Review
policies.applies_to: Administrator, billing/office staff, and direct care staff who document services at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills the regional center only for authorized services that were actually delivered, documents services, keeps records at least five years, and meets the independent review/audit requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is vendored by the regional center in whose area the facility is located (17 CCR §54326(a)(14)) as a staff-operated (915) or owner-operated (905) residential facility under 17 CCR §54342, and it serves people entitled to services under the Lanterman Act (WIC §4500 et seq.). The home bills monthly, only for authorized and delivered services (17 CCR §54326(a)(10)). The regional center rate is payment in full (17 CCR §54326(a)(12)). The home does not bill for services before vendorization (17 CCR §54326(d)(4)). Billing and service records are kept at least five years (17 CCR §54326(a)(3)) and are open to monitoring (17 CCR §54326(a)(2)). The home signs and follows its HCBS Provider Agreement (17 CCR §54326(a)(16)) and uses EVV where it applies to the service (42 USC 1396b(l)). Independent review or audit is arranged as WIC §4652.5 requires. New vendors are paid 90% of the regional-center portion plus SSI/SSP, and the QIP can earn the other 10%. No official checklist items are assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: A residential service approved by the regional center in the person's IPP and in a current authorization for a stated service code, level and period.
The Title 17 service codes for staff-operated (915) and owner-operated (905) residential facilities (17 CCR §54342). Codes 920 and 910 are the related codes for those facility types.
Review (payments $500,000-$1,999,999 a year) or audit (payments $2,000,000 or more) by an independent accountant under WIC §4652.5, due 9 months after fiscal year end.
Electronic Visit Verification, used where it is required for the service.

procedures: The Administrator confirms before any billing that the facility is licensed by CCL, vendored by [VENDORING REGIONAL CENTER] with a vendor number, and that the HCBS Provider Agreement is signed. The home does not bill, and does not accept payment, for any period before vendorization (GOV-02).

For each resident, the Administrator keeps the current authorization showing service code (915/905), ARM service level, rate and authorization dates. The Administrator checks it against the IPP and files it in the resident's billing file.
Direct care staff document services each shift in consumer notes (PCS-02), including attendance, absences and hospital stays. Notes are signed or initialed and dated the same shift.

Where EVV applies to the service, staff record visits through the approved EVV system at the time of service. The Administrator reviews EVV exceptions weekly and corrects them within 5 days with a documented reason.

By the [DAY] day after month end, the billing designee prepares the monthly invoice or attendance/billing report. It lists each resident, authorization number, service code, days of service and the rate authorized.

Before submission, the Administrator compares the invoice with the attendance records and consumer notes, and excludes any day the resident was absent without an authorized bill. The Administrator signs the invoice to certify accuracy.

The home submits the invoice to [VENDORING REGIONAL CENTER] by the regional center's deadline and keeps the submission confirmation. The home bills no more than the authorized rate. The rate is payment in full, and the home does not ask residents or families for additional payment for the authorized service, except as authorized for SSI/SSP board and care and personal and incidental items (SB-08).
Overpayments or billing errors found by the home or the regional center are reported to the regional center in writing within 10 business days, with a correction plan and repayment as directed.
The billing designee reconciles regional center payments to invoices each month. Unpaid or short-paid items are followed up within 15 days.

The Administrator tracks the home's total regional center payments each fiscal year. When payments reach $500,000 the home arranges an independent review, and at $2,000,000 or more an independent audit, to be delivered within 9 months after fiscal year end (WIC §4652.5). The Administrator engages the independent accountant at least 90 days before the due date, delivers the report to [VENDORING REGIONAL CENTER] by the deadline and keeps proof.
The Administrator keeps billing records, authorizations, service documentation, EVV records, financial statements and review or audit reports for at least five years (17 CCR §54326(a)(3)).
The Administrator provides these records to regional center or DDS monitors on request without delay (17 CCR §54326(a)(2); GOV-06).
Each year, the Administrator reviews the QIP requirements and confirms the home meets HCBS, EVV and audit compliance (GOV-04), and records any QIP payments received in the finance records.
The governing body receives a quarterly summary of billing accuracy, audit status and any repayments (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures resources for accurate billing and funds the independent review/audit.
Certifies invoices, ensures authorizations match billing, arranges the review/audit and keeps records at least five years.
Prepares invoices, reconciles payments and tracks deadlines.
Document services, absences and EVV entries accurately and on time.

documentation: Vendor authorization and HCBS Provider Agreement
Monthly invoices with attendance support
EVV records and exception log
Payment reconciliation records
Overpayment correction records
Independent review/audit reports and transmittals
Five-year retention index

policies.title: Licensing and Regional Center Monitoring Access
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designated alternates and all staff on duty at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure that Community Care Licensing (CCL) staff and regional center monitors are admitted promptly, that records are produced by authorized persons, that rights and complaint information are visible, and that every deficiency is corrected and tracked.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] allows unannounced visits by CCL and monitoring access by the regional center (17 CCR §54326(a)(2)). The Administrator names the persons who receive inspectors and who may show records. The CCL complaint-unit address and phone, the personal rights and the visiting policy are posted prominently where residents and visitors can see them (22 CCR §80072(a), (e)). All deficiencies are tracked to correction, and copies of substantiated complaints are kept and shared with designated parties (22 CCR §80061). No official checklist items are assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: Entry to the facility, residents, staff and records by CCL, DDS, the regional center and other agencies with legal authority.
The Administrator or a designee named in writing to produce facility and resident records.
A finding of non-compliance on a CCL licensing report or a regional center monitoring report.

procedures: The Administrator posts in a common area: the CCL complaint-unit address and telephone ([CCL COMPLAINT UNIT ADDRESS/PHONE]) with confidentiality information, the list of personal rights, the visiting policy, the facility license and the emergency numbers (22 CCR §80072(a), (e)). The Administrator checks the postings monthly and records the check.

The Administrator designates in writing [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and [ALTERNATE NAME(S)] to receive inspectors and to authorize production of records. This designation is posted in the staff office and every staff member signs that they have read it.

Any staff member who is approached by a CCL representative or regional center monitor asks for identification, admits the person immediately, does not delay entry, and calls the Administrator or alternate at [PHONE] at once. Staff may not refuse entry or tell an inspector to come back later.
The Administrator or alternate meets the inspector, logs the name, agency, time of arrival and purpose, and offers a private space to review records and interview residents and staff.
The inspector's access to residents and staff for interviews is allowed with privacy. Staff do not coach, discourage or retaliate against any resident or staff member who speaks with an inspector.

The Administrator or alternate produces the records requested, including resident files, personnel files, medication records, fire drill and incident records, staffing schedules, billing records and the Plan of Operation. Records are shown only to authorized persons, and anything copied is logged (IR-04).

If the Administrator and alternate are both unavailable, the senior staff on duty admits the inspector and shows the facility but contacts the Administrator by phone, and records that the inspector requested records that were to be produced when the Administrator arrives.

At the exit conference, the Administrator takes notes, asks questions about any finding and obtains a copy of the visit report (e.g., Licensing Report or Notice of Deficiency) before the inspector leaves.

Within one working day of a visit, the Administrator logs each deficiency on the Deficiency Tracker with the finding, the cited requirement, the corrective action, the responsible person and the date due (the plan-of-correction date in the report).

The Administrator corrects each deficiency by the date due, writes the plan of correction or submits proof of correction to CCL or the regional center as required, and keeps the proof (photos, receipts, training sign-ins, revised policy).
The Administrator reviews every deficiency in the next quarterly quality review (GOV-04) for repeat findings and system causes.

The Administrator keeps copies of substantiated complaints and sends copies to the designated parties required by 22 CCR §80061, including the authorized representative and others as listed in that section, and records the transmittal.
Visit reports, plans of correction and tracker entries are kept at least five years and are available at the next inspection (17 CCR §54326(a)(3)).

responsibilities.duty: Receives inspectors or delegates in writing, authorizes records, corrects deficiencies on time and distributes substantiated complaint copies.
Receives inspectors and produces records in the Administrator's absence.
Admit inspectors without delay, notify the Administrator immediately, and never obstruct or retaliate.
Reviews deficiency trends and makes sure corrections are completed.

documentation: Inspector/visitor log
Written designation of record custodians
Posting checklist
CCL and regional center visit reports
Deficiency Tracker and proof of correction
Substantiated complaint copies and transmittals

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: All residents, authorized representatives, staff and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident's personal rights under 22 CCR §80072 are honored, and that the home operates as a community-based, non-institutional setting consistent with HCBS requirements and the Lanterman Act.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] honors every right in 22 CCR §80072(a): dignity; safe and comfortable accommodations; freedom from corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, punitive actions and interference with eating, sleeping or toileting; freedom from withholding of shelter, clothing, medication or aids; being told the CCL complaint-unit address, phone and confidentiality information; religious freedom; the right to leave the facility at any time; the right not to be locked in any room or the premises; freedom from restraining devices; the right to receive or reject medical care; and being told the visiting policy. Residents may have private visits, including with advocacy representatives, during waking hours. They may make confidential phone calls, receive unopened mail, wear their own clothing and receive help with voting (§85072(b); the Administrator confirms the current full text). Residents are free to come and go, and no resident is ever locked in a room or the premises. The licensee ensures rights are honored (22 CCR §80072(f)). At admission, the resident and authorized representative are personally advised of the rights and given the list, which is also posted (22 CCR §80072(d)-(e)). The home follows the HCBS settings requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c) and 42 CFR 441.710 and the ADA, and the rights of persons with developmental disabilities under WIC §4500 et seq. No official checklist items are assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: The rights in 22 CCR §80072(a)(1)-(10) that the licensee must ensure for each resident.
The person with legal authority to act for the resident, such as a conservator or other legal representative, or a person the resident designates under law.

The federal standards under 42 CFR 441.301(c) and 441.710 that make a home a community-based setting. They include integration, privacy, dignity, choice, control over schedule and visitors, and freedom from coercion.
The hours when residents are awake and may reasonably receive visitors, set in the visiting policy and consistent with each resident's preferences.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the list of personal rights, the CCL complaint-unit address and phone, and the visiting policy posted prominently in a common area at all times (22 CCR §80072(e)). Rights are available in the languages and formats residents use (IR-06).

At admission, the Administrator or designee personally reviews the rights with the resident and the authorized representative in a format they can understand. They give them the rights list and the complaint-unit information. The resident and representative sign and date the Acknowledgment of Rights, and a copy is kept in the resident file (22 CCR §80072(d)).
The review is repeated at least annually, at each IPP meeting, whenever rights or the visiting policy change, and whenever a resident or representative asks. The date and who attended are recorded.
Staff treat residents with dignity at all times: address them by their preferred name, knock before entering a bedroom or bathroom, provide personal care privately, and speak to residents as adults.
Residents may practice their religion or none, and attend services of their choice, with transportation support as set in the IPP (PCS-03, HE-05).

Residents may leave the facility at any time. The home may set reasonable curfews and house rules, but these do not apply to a resident with a conservator or other legal authority who sets different limits. Staff record departures and returns only as the plan requires for safety and not to restrict movement (BSP-05).
No resident is locked in any room or in the premises. Exterior doors and windows may be locked only if residents can exit on their own. Any other securing means needs prior CCL approval (IR-02).

Residents receive visitors, including advocacy representatives such as the Office of Clients' Rights Advocacy, and the ombudsman, in private during waking hours. Staff do not screen, delay or require advance notice beyond what the posted visiting policy states and the resident agrees to.

Residents may make and receive phone calls in private, receive their mail unopened, wear their own clothing, and have their own belongings. Staff offer help with voting, including registration, ballots and transportation, on request (§85072(b), subject to confirmation).

Residents choose their daily schedule, meals and snacks within the home's menu plan (SB-07, HE-04), and their activities and community involvement (PCS-03). They also choose their roommate where practical and decorate their own space (HE-01).

A resident may accept or reject medical care. Staff give information in plain language, support decision-making and do not coerce (IR-05). A refusal is recorded and reported to the authorized representative and service coordinator (HW-04).

Staff never use corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threats, mental abuse or punitive actions. They never interfere with eating, sleeping or toileting, and never withhold shelter, clothing, medication or aids (SB-05, BSP-03).

Any suspected rights violation is reported to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator records it, stops the practice, and follows IR-03 (grievances) and BSP-03/BSP-04 where abuse or a reportable event is suspected. No retaliation is allowed against a resident, family member or staff member who raises a concern.
The Administrator checks rights compliance monthly through observation, resident interviews and record review, and reports results at the quarterly quality review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures rights are honored, posted and reviewed at admission and as needed (22 CCR §80072(d)-(f)).
Honor each right in daily practice and report concerns immediately.
Receive the rights, ask questions and use the complaint process if needed.
Informed of any concern or change relating to rights through the IPP process.

documentation: Signed Acknowledgment of Rights
Posted rights list, complaint-unit information and visiting policy
Annual and as-needed rights review notes
Monthly rights compliance check
Grievance and incident records for any violation

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
policies.applies_to: Administrator, program staff, interdisciplinary team members and all direct care staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure any limit on a resident's rights is lawful, individually justified, documented with informed consent, reviewed and communicated, and that locking and securing methods, postural supports and protective devices are used only under the conditions of 22 CCR §80072.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not restrict a resident's rights except as allowed by law and documented in the resident's plan. Exterior doors and windows may be locked only if residents can exit. Any other securing means requires prior CCL approval (22 CCR §80072(a)). No resident is locked in a room or the premises. No restraining devices are used, other than postural supports and protective devices under the strict conditions in 22 CCR §80072(a)(8). A fire clearance must be obtained first if a postural support would make a client nonambulatory (22 CCR §80020; §80072(a)(8)(D)). Any modification of a right is documented in the plan, per 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F), with the assessed need, the less-intrusive methods tried and informed consent. The authorized representative and the service coordinator are notified of every restriction. No official checklist items are assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: Any limit on a right, such as access to belongings, food, visitors or leaving the home, that is not applied to others in the home.
A lock or other device that keeps persons from leaving a room or building. Locking exterior doors and windows is allowed only if residents can exit. Other securing means need prior CCL approval.
A device used to achieve proper body position or balance. It is allowed only under the conditions in 22 CCR §80072.
A device used for the person's protection and not as a restraint. It is allowed only under the conditions in 22 CCR §80072.
Unable to leave the building without assistance in an emergency. A separate fire clearance is required before admitting a nonambulatory person (22 CCR §80020).

procedures: No staff member may restrict, limit or condition a resident's right on their own. Only the process in this policy may be used, and any urgent safety action is handled under BSP-02 and HW-04.

When a concern arises that a right may need limiting, the Administrator convenes the interdisciplinary team within 5 working days. The team includes the resident, the authorized representative, the service coordinator, relevant clinicians and any person the resident chooses.

The team documents the specific, individualized assessed need that justifies the limit, the evidence for it, and the right that would be affected. It does not use a general or house-wide justification.
The team lists the positive interventions and less-intrusive methods already tried and why they did not work, and what supports will be used to help the resident end the restriction (BSP-01).
The team describes the condition or limit so that it is no more than needed for the assessed need and ends as soon as possible.

The plan states how data will be collected on the effect of the limit, a time limit and set dates for periodic review (at least every [90] days or sooner if the team decides), and the criteria for ending it.

The resident, or the authorized representative where the resident lacks capacity, gives informed consent in writing after receiving a plain-language explanation (IR-05). If consent is refused or withdrawn, the restriction is not applied, and the team reconvenes.
The team records an assurance that the limit will not cause harm to the resident. The modification is entered in the Needs and Services Plan (22 CCR §85068.2) and the IPP (PCS-01).

The Administrator notifies the authorized representative and the service coordinator of the restriction in writing within 2 working days of the decision, and tells the resident about the grievance process and the CCL complaint unit (IR-03).

Locking: exterior doors and windows are locked only if every resident can exit on their own. If any other securing means is considered, such as a delayed-egress device or a locked room, the Administrator submits the request to CCL and waits for written approval before using it. The approval is kept on file, and fire safety is reviewed (HE-02).

Postural supports and protective devices are used only if the conditions in 22 CCR §80072(a)(8) are met: a physician's written order, a plan for the resident, regular checks and release as the rule requires. They are never used for the convenience of staff or as a punishment.
Before any postural support that would make a resident nonambulatory is used, the Administrator obtains the fire clearance through CCL and a copy is placed on file (22 CCR §80020; §80072(a)(8)(D)).

Staff apply and review the restriction exactly as written and document each use and the resident's response in consumer notes (PCS-02). Staff report any concern or complaint about it to the Administrator the same day.

The team reviews each restriction on its set dates, using data to decide whether to continue, reduce or end it. The review is documented, and the representative and service coordinator are notified of the outcome.
The Administrator keeps a Rights Restriction Register of all active restrictions, consents, CCL approvals, fire clearances and review dates, and reports it at each quarterly quality review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Convenes the team, obtains CCL approval and fire clearance, ensures consent and notifications, and keeps the register.
Documents need, less-intrusive methods tried, time limits and review dates.
Apply restrictions only as written, document use and report concerns.
Give or withhold informed consent and take part in reviews.
Receives notice of each restriction and takes part in plan reviews.

documentation: Written modification in the Needs and Services Plan and IPP, with assessed need, less-intrusive methods, data plan, time limit and consent
CCL prior approval for any non-exterior securing means
Fire clearance for any support that makes a resident nonambulatory
Physician order for postural supports or protective devices
Notification to authorized representative and service coordinator
Rights Restriction Register and review records

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All residents, authorized representatives, relatives, and all [AGENCY NAME] staff at the Adult Residential Facility
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident, authorized representative and relative can raise a concern or complaint, inside or outside the agency, without fear of retaliation, and that each concern is answered promptly, resolved where possible, and recorded.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] honors each resident's personal right to be told how to reach the Community Care Licensing (CCL) complaint unit and to be treated with dignity and free from punitive action, coercion, threat, intimidation or ridicule (22 CCR §80072) [C2]. Residents may complain to [AGENCY NAME], CCL, their regional center, the long-term care ombudsman, Disability Rights California, or any other person or agency of their choice. No resident, representative, relative or staff member will be retaliated against for making a complaint. Complaints from relatives and authorized representatives receive a prompt response. Every complaint and its resolution is logged. Where CCL substantiates a complaint, copies are provided to the designated parties as 22 CCR §80061 requires [C1]. This policy supports the HCBS settings rights described in 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: Any expression of dissatisfaction or concern about services, staff, other residents, the home, or a rights restriction, whether spoken, written, signed, or communicated through an advocate.
Any adverse action, threat, loss of privilege, change in treatment, or pressure directed at a person because they made or supported a complaint.
A conservator, parent, guardian or other person legally authorized to act for the resident.
The Community Care Licensing office that receives complaints about licensed facilities, using the address and phone number posted in the home.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator or designee personally tells the resident and authorized representative, in a manner they can understand, that they may complain to CCL and gives them the CCL complaint unit address and phone number: [CCL REGIONAL OFFICE ADDRESS] / [CCL PHONE]. The resident or representative signs the acknowledgment on the personal rights form, and the signed copy goes in the resident's record.

At admission, the Administrator also gives the resident the contact information for the vendoring regional center ([REGIONAL CENTER PHONE]), the local long-term care ombudsman ([OMBUDSMAN PHONE]), and Disability Rights California ([DRC PHONE]), and explains that the resident may use any of them at any time.

The Administrator posts a notice in a common area, at a height and in a format residents can read, with the CCL complaint unit contact information, the other outside contacts and the agency's internal complaint steps. Pictorial, large-print, translated or audio versions are provided when needed.

Residents may use a telephone privately, send mail unopened, and ask any person to help them make a complaint. Staff never screen, discourage, delay or read a complaint addressed to an outside agency.

Any staff member who hears a complaint, including one made informally, stops and listens, thanks the person, and writes it down the same shift on the Complaint Log. Staff do not argue, defend, or tell the person to wait.

If the complaint alleges abuse, neglect, exploitation, a rights violation, injury or a health or safety threat, staff immediately follow BSP-03 and BSP-04, notify the Administrator, and make the required reports. The complaint process does not delay required reporting under 22 CCR §80061 [C1].

The Administrator reviews each complaint within one working day. For other complaints, the Administrator contacts the complainant within [TWO] working days to acknowledge, clarify the concern, and ask what outcome they want.

The Administrator responds promptly to complaints from relatives and authorized representatives, and in any event gives an initial response within [TWO] working days. The response is documented, including the date, the person spoken to, and the action taken.

The Administrator investigates by interviewing the complainant, any witnesses and involved staff, and reviewing records. Staff who are the subject of a complaint do not investigate it and do not handle the resident's care in a way that could be seen as retaliatory while the review is under way.

The Administrator decides on a resolution, takes the corrective action (for example staff coaching, a change of routine, repairs, or a care plan update), and informs the complainant in writing or in the way they prefer, within [FIVE] working days where possible. If more time is needed, the Administrator explains why and gives a target date.

If the complainant is not satisfied, the Administrator offers to help them take the complaint to the regional center service coordinator, CCL, the ombudsman or Disability Rights California, and provides a phone, transport or other help to do so.

Each complaint and its resolution is entered on the Complaint Log: date received, complainant, nature of complaint, who took it, investigation steps, outcome, date the complainant was informed and any follow-up. The log is kept in a locked file with limited access.

When CCL or the regional center investigates a complaint, the Administrator cooperates fully, supplies records on request, and promptly sends copies of any substantiated complaint to the designated parties as 22 CCR §80061 requires [C1]. Copies are filed in the facility's licensing file.
The Administrator reviews the Complaint Log at least quarterly for patterns (same staff, same topic, same resident) and reports findings to the governing body and the quality review in GOV-04.

Any form of retaliation is grounds for discipline up to and including termination. Staff who observe or suspect retaliation report it to the Administrator, or to [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT] if the Administrator is involved.
Staff are trained on this policy at orientation and annually, including how to receive a complaint, communication-access needs, and non-retaliation.

responsibilities.duty: Gives admission notices, posts contact information, reviews and investigates complaints, ensures responses and log entries, and prevents retaliation.
Listen to and record complaints the same shift, report urgent matters immediately, and never discourage or retaliate.
Reviews complaint trends and investigates complaints involving the Administrator.
May raise concerns at any time, in any form, with any internal or external party.
