Staff secure the resident's medications and medication administration record. They count the medications with a second staff member and record the count. They dispose of the medications only as directed by HW-01 and by law enforcement or the pharmacy if instructed.

Two staff members inventory the resident's personal property and any personal funds, sign and date the inventory, and lock the property in a secure place. The Administrator releases property and funds only to the authorized representative or the legally responsible person for the estate, following SB-08.

The Administrator releases the body only as directed by the coroner or medical examiner and the authorized representative or their chosen funeral home. Staff assist family members and honor the resident's documented cultural and religious wishes where possible.

The Administrator or a designated senior staff member tells the other residents about the death in a sensitive, individualized way, taking into account each person's communication needs and relationship to the resident. The facility offers extra support or counseling, coordinating with each resident's regional center service coordinator.

The Administrator preserves, without alteration, the resident's file, consumer notes, medication records, incident reports, health records, staffing schedules for the week before the death, and any video or logs that exist. The Administrator places these records under a hold until the investigation and review are closed. Retention follows REC-01.

The Administrator completes the mortality review within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days of the death, using the form in GOV-04. The review looks at health history, recent changes in condition, supports and supervision, emergency response, and whether any policies or training need to change. The Administrator records corrective actions and a completion date for each.

The Administrator completes discharge and closing documentation for the resident under PCS-04, notifies the regional center so that billing and placement records are updated under GOV-05, and files the CCL, regional center and mortality review records in the incident file.
The Administrator meets with staff on duty at the time of the death within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days to review the response and to offer support. The Administrator documents the meeting.

responsibilities.duty: Call 911, begin emergency care, notify the Administrator immediately, preserve the scene when appropriate, and document facts in writing before the end of the shift.
Notify the authorized representative, regional center and CCL on time; submit written reports; secure records, medications and property; complete the mortality review; and ensure staff support.
Perform the Administrator's immediate duties when the Administrator cannot be reached.
Review each mortality review and approve corrective actions through GOV-04.

documentation: Staff written account of the death, with time and actions
Incident or CCL report (LIC 624 or current form) with proof of the next-working-day report and the 7-day written report
Regional center SIR and any follow-up reports, with date and time sent
Log of notifications to the authorized representative, with times and names
WIC §15630 report records, if applicable
Medication count record and property inventory, signed and dated
Mortality review form with corrective action plan
Record hold notice and discharge documentation

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support
policies.applies_to: Administrator, direct care staff, behavioral consultants, and the resident's planning team
policies.purpose: To make sure that every resident is supported with positive, person-centered strategies that prevent distress and challenging behavior, protect personal rights and promote a meaningful life in the community.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] supports each resident through positive behavior support. This means understanding the reasons for behavior, teaching new skills, changing the environment and responding calmly and respectfully. Early warning signs, triggers and calming techniques for each resident are recorded in the Needs and Services Plan (22 CCR §85068.2) and used by all staff. The facility never uses punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion or threats. It never interferes with eating, sleeping or toileting, and never withholds shelter, clothing, medication or aids (22 CCR §80072). Behavioral consultant hours are used as required by the facility's approved service level under 17 CCR §56004(f), at 8, 12 or 16 hours per consumer per six months. Where a resident has a rights restriction, it follows IR-02 and the person-centered planning and documentation requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c) for home and community-based settings. Staff are trained on each resident's plan and results are tracked in consumer notes.

definitions.definition: An approach that uses assessment of the reasons for behavior, skill teaching, environmental changes and positive reinforcement to reduce challenging behavior and improve quality of life.
Changes in mood, speech, body language or routine that show a resident may be becoming distressed.
A person, place, event, sensory experience or memory that is likely to cause distress for a resident.
A strategy the resident has said helps them, or that has been found to help, such as a walk, music, a quiet space or talking to a trusted person.
A qualified professional engaged by [AGENCY NAME] or the regional center to assess behavior and advise on supports.

procedures: Before admission, the Administrator or designee reviews the referral packet, the IPP and any behavioral assessments, and meets with the resident and the authorized representative to learn the resident's preferences, history and communication style. This forms part of the pre-admission determination in SB-06 and 22 CCR §85068.2.

On or before the day of admission, the Administrator completes the initial assessment in the Needs and Services Plan with the resident, the authorized representative and anyone the resident chooses. The assessment records early warning signs, triggers, calming techniques, medical conditions that could increase risk during an emergency intervention, trauma history, and any advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion or manual restraint.

The Administrator writes the resident's support strategies in the Needs and Services Plan in plain language. The strategies cover how to prevent distress, how to respond at each stage, how to help the resident calm down, and how to help the resident return to routine. The resident reviews the plan with support and receives a copy in an understandable format.

Staff are trained on each resident's plan before they work alone with that resident and whenever the plan changes. The Administrator records the training, who delivered it and the date, under SB-03 and STF-03.

Staff use proactive strategies every day: offering choices, keeping routines predictable, honoring communication preferences, offering preferred activities, reducing noise or crowding, and teaching new skills. Staff praise and reinforce positive behavior.

When a resident shows early warning signs, staff respond by following the calming techniques listed in the plan. They speak calmly, offer space and choices, remove triggers where possible and avoid arguing, threatening or crowding the resident.

Staff do not use punishment of any kind. This includes humiliation, ridicule, loss of meals, sleep or toileting access, removal of clothing, medication or aids, threats, or removing items or privileges as a consequence for behavior. Staff who see or suspect these actions report to the Administrator immediately and follow BSP-03.
Staff record each significant behavior event, the setting, what happened before and after, what staff did and what worked, in consumer notes on the same shift under PCS-02.

If a resident's behavior puts the person or others at immediate risk of serious harm, staff stay calm, protect others, call 911 if needed and notify the Administrator. They do not use restraint or seclusion, and follow BSP-02. The Administrator submits any required reports under BSP-04.

The Administrator reviews behavior data and consumer notes at least monthly with the staff supporting the resident. The review looks at patterns, triggers, staff responses, health issues, medication effects, environmental factors and how supports are working. The Administrator documents the review and any changes.

The Administrator engages behavioral consultants when a resident's behavior continues after routine strategies, when a new behavior develops, or as the approved service level requires. Consultant hours of 8, 12 or 16 per consumer per six months are scheduled so that they are used during each six-month period, and the Administrator tracks hours used against that requirement.

The consultant assesses the behavior, recommends supports and trains staff. The Administrator ensures that recommendations are consistent with the resident's rights, the person-centered plan and the IPP, and are added to the Needs and Services Plan only after the resident and authorized representative have been consulted.

If a recommendation would limit a resident's rights or choices, the Administrator follows IR-02 before it is used. This includes documenting the specific assessed need, the less intrusive methods tried, informed consent, a time limit and regular review, as the HCBS settings rule requires under 42 CFR 441.301(c).

If behavior supports are not working, or the resident has an increase in incidents, the Administrator asks the regional center service coordinator to convene the planning team, and updates the Needs and Services Plan afterward. The Administrator requests a health review if a medical cause may be involved, under HW-02.
The Administrator reviews the facility's behavior support data, incident trends and training records at least quarterly through GOV-04, and acts on any trend.

responsibilities.duty: Complete and update the assessment and support strategies, train staff, review data monthly, engage consultants and ensure no prohibited practices are used.
Know each resident's plan, use prevention and calming strategies, treat residents respectfully, document events and report concerns.
Assess behavior, recommend supports, train staff and review results.
Take part in developing the plan and in reviews to the extent they choose.
Convene the planning team when supports need to change.

documentation: Needs and Services Plan with early warning signs, triggers and calming techniques
Staff training records on each resident's plan
Consumer notes of behavior events and responses
Monthly behavior data review notes
Consultant reports and log of consultant hours per consumer per six months
Records of consent and rights review when a support limits choices

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
policies.applies_to: Administrator, all direct care staff, on-call managers, and consultants
policies.purpose: To protect residents from restraint, seclusion and other restrictive interventions, to make sure staff know what is prohibited and what to do in a crisis, and to meet California personal-rights rules and federal home and community-based settings requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not use restraining devices, seclusion or locked rooms. Under 22 CCR §80072 a resident may not be locked in any room or in the premises, may not be restrained by devices, and may be subject to postural supports or protective devices only under the strict conditions in that regulation. The facility does not use restraint or seclusion for discipline, punishment, convenience or staff shortage. Each resident's individual emergency intervention plan is part of the Needs and Services Plan (22 CCR §85068.2). The facility honors a resident's advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion and manual restraint unless it violates the law or endangers safety. Secured-perimeter status for this facility: [YES / NO]. If YES, direct care staff are trained in Emergency Intervention under 22 CCR §85300 as required by 22 CCR §80065(o). Any modification of a resident's rights must meet 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F) and IR-02.

definitions.definition: Any device or equipment that restricts a person's movement or access to their body, other than a postural support or protective device used under the strict conditions of 22 CCR §80072.
Physical holding of a person that restricts movement.
Involuntary confinement of a person alone in a room or area from which they are physically prevented from leaving.
A device used only to support body position or protect from injury, under the strict conditions in 22 CCR §80072 and the resident's written plan.
The resident's written plan within the Needs and Services Plan describing how staff respond to an emergency, as required by 22 CCR §85068.2.

definitions.term: Advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion or manual restraint
definitions.definition: A resident's own written or recorded preferences about how staff should respond in a behavioral emergency.

procedures: The Administrator confirms in writing with the CCL licensing analyst whether Health and Safety Code §1180 through §1180.6 applies to this ARF, and which of its requirements apply. The Administrator records the answer and updates this policy and staff training if the answer changes anything. Until that is confirmed, [AGENCY NAME] treats restraint and seclusion as prohibited except where the resident's emergency intervention plan permits and the law allows.

The Administrator orients every new staff member to this policy before they work with residents, and again annually. Orientation covers what is prohibited, de-escalation techniques, residents' individual plans, and when and how to call 911.

At admission, the Administrator documents each resident's advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion and manual restraint, if one exists, in the Needs and Services Plan. If the resident has none, the Administrator offers them the opportunity to make one, with support from a person they choose.

The Administrator completes the resident's individual emergency intervention plan with the resident and authorized representative. It lists early warning signs, triggers, calming techniques, medical conditions that increase restraint risk, trauma history, and the steps staff take, in order.

Staff do not lock a resident in a room or in the premises. Exterior doors and windows may be locked only if residents can exit. Any other means of securing the perimeter requires prior CCL approval, which the Administrator holds in the facility file. Delayed-egress or alarm devices are not used without that approval.

Staff do not use restraining devices on any resident. This includes tying, strapping, bed rails used to confine, locked chairs, wrist or ankle restraints, and clothing or devices that prevent movement.

A postural support or protective device is used only when it meets the strict conditions of 22 CCR §80072. The Administrator verifies those conditions against the regulation and with CCL before any use. The device must be ordered by a physician, written into the Needs and Services Plan, consented to by the resident or authorized representative, and reviewed regularly. Staff never use it for discipline or convenience.

In a crisis, staff first use the de-escalation steps in the resident's plan. They keep a safe distance, remove other people and hazards, speak calmly and offer space and choices. Staff do not corner, chase, shout at or threaten the resident.

If anyone is in immediate danger of serious harm, staff move others to safety, call 911 and the Administrator, and stay close enough to monitor the resident. Staff use physical contact only as the resident's emergency intervention plan permits and the law allows, and only for as long as needed to prevent imminent serious harm.

Staff do not use seclusion, locked rooms, removal of clothing, withholding of food or toileting, or any form of punishment as a response to behavior. Staff do not use another resident to help restrain or control a resident, and residents are never substitutes for required staff (22 CCR §80065(j)).

If a resident has an advance directive about de-escalation, seclusion or manual restraint, staff follow it unless following it would violate the law or endanger anyone's safety. If staff do not follow it, they record why in consumer notes, and the Administrator reviews the decision.

Staff document any use of physical contact or a postural support or protective device in consumer notes before the end of the shift. The notes include what happened beforehand, what de-escalation was tried, what intervention was used and for how long, the resident's condition after, and who was told.

The Administrator reports the event under BSP-04 to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days, where it is an injury needing treatment, an unusual incident or an event threatening health or safety, and to the regional center as an SIR where required. The Administrator also reviews the event within 1 business day and offers the resident an opportunity to talk about it.

After any use of physical intervention, the Administrator holds a debrief with staff and, as the resident chooses, with the resident. The debrief examines triggers, staff actions and any changes needed to the plan, and the Administrator updates the Needs and Services Plan and notifies the regional center service coordinator.

If a restriction on a resident's rights is proposed, the Administrator follows IR-02 and does not apply the restriction until the requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F) are met, including a specific assessed need, prior less intrusive methods, informed consent, a time limit and regular review.

If [AGENCY NAME] uses a secured perimeter, the Administrator keeps CCL's approval on file and trains all direct care staff in Emergency Intervention under 22 CCR §85300 before they work alone, as required by 22 CCR §80065(o). The Administrator keeps training certificates in personnel records under STF-05.
The Administrator reviews every restrictive intervention event, rights restriction and related complaint at least quarterly under GOV-04, and reports patterns to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Keep restrictive practices prohibited, verify the scope of HSC §1180-1180.6 with CCL, obtain CCL approvals where needed, ensure training, complete reports and review every event.
Use de-escalation and the resident's emergency intervention plan, call 911 for imminent danger, avoid all prohibited practices, document and report every event.
Help develop the emergency intervention plan and any advance directive, and take part in debriefs.
Review trend reports and make sure no practice is approved that violates 22 CCR §80072.

documentation: Needs and Services Plan with individual emergency intervention plan and advance directive
Written confirmation from CCL on the scope of HSC §1180-1180.6
CCL approval of any securing means other than exterior doors and windows that residents can exit
Physician order, consent and review records for any postural support or protective device
Consumer notes of any physical intervention or crisis response
Incident reports, SIRs and debrief records
Staff training records, including Emergency Intervention (§85300) where applicable
Rights restriction documentation under IR-02

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, contractors, the Administrator and the governing body
policies.purpose: To prevent abuse, neglect and exploitation of residents, to make sure suspected abuse is reported within the required time limits, and to protect people who report from retaliation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has zero tolerance for abuse, neglect, exploitation or personal-rights violations. All staff are mandated reporters of dependent adult abuse under WIC §15630. Suspected physical abuse resulting in serious bodily injury is reported to the local ombudsman, CCL and law enforcement within 2 hours. All other suspected physical abuse is reported within 24 hours (22 CCR §80061(c)-(d)). Suspected psychological abuse is reported to CCL by the next working day with a written report within 7 days (22 CCR §80061). Events are also reported to the regional center as a Special Incident Report under 17 CCR §54327. All personnel must report violations of personal rights (22 CCR §80065(m)). The facility does not retaliate against anyone who makes a report in good faith, and does not allow others to do so, consistent with 45 CFR 164.530.

definitions.definition: A person aged 18 to 64 with physical or mental limitations that restrict their ability to carry out normal activities or protect their rights. This includes all residents of this ARF who meet that description.

Assault, battery, unreasonable physical constraint, prolonged or continual deprivation of food or water, use of physical or chemical restraint or psychotropic medication in a way that is not allowed, and other conduct defined in WIC §15610.63.
Verbal or emotional conduct that causes fear, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion or threat.
Failure to provide the care, supervision, food, shelter, clothing, medical care or protection that a resident needs.
Taking, using or misusing a resident's money, property or benefits.

An injury involving extreme physical pain, substantial risk of death, protracted loss or impairment of a body part, or that requires medical intervention such as surgery, hospitalization or physical rehabilitation.
A person who must report suspected abuse of a dependent adult by law, including care custodians and their employees.

procedures: Before starting work, every employee signs a statement acknowledging they are a mandated reporter under WIC §15630 and that they have read this policy. The Administrator keeps the statement in the personnel record under STF-05.

At orientation and annually, the Administrator trains all staff on the types and signs of abuse, neglect and exploitation, on reporting duties and timelines, on resident personal rights under 22 CCR §80072, and on the no-retaliation rule. The training is recorded under SB-03.

Staff who see, hear about or reasonably suspect abuse, neglect, exploitation or a violation of personal rights tell the Administrator or on-call manager right away. Staff may also make a report directly to the ombudsman, CCL or law enforcement without asking permission. Reporting to the Administrator does not replace the staff member's own legal duty to report.
If a resident is injured or in danger, staff first make the resident safe and call 911 if needed. Staff keep the resident away from the suspected person and preserve any evidence.

For suspected physical abuse with serious bodily injury, the Administrator or the staff member makes a phone report to the local ombudsman, CCL and law enforcement within 2 hours. For other suspected physical abuse, the report is made within 24 hours. The person making the report records the time and the name of the person who took it.

A written follow-up report is submitted to the agencies as required by WIC §15630 on the state's current report form. The Administrator confirms the form and deadline with the ombudsman or county adult protective services office when the policy is adopted and each year.

For suspected psychological abuse, the Administrator reports to CCL by the next working day and sends a written report within 7 days, on the CCL incident form (LIC 624 or current form). The written report states the resident's name, age, sex and admission date, the date and nature of the event, physician findings and treatment if any, and what was done.

The Administrator makes a Special Incident Report to the regional center by phone or email immediately after the event is known, and in writing within the timelines in BSP-04, and confirms the current requirements of 17 CCR §54327 with the regional center. The Administrator also notifies the resident's authorized representative as required by 22 CCR §80061.

The Administrator separates the accused staff member from residents immediately, using administrative leave or a reassignment that does not include resident contact, while the matter is investigated. The Administrator does not conduct interviews that could interfere with a law enforcement or licensing investigation, and follows the direction of those agencies.
If the suspected person is another resident, staff protect both residents, notify each authorized representative, and ask the regional center and planning team to review supports under BSP-01.

If the suspected person is the Administrator or owner, any staff member or the on-call manager reports directly to the agencies listed above and to the governing body. The facility has no authority to stop that report.

The Administrator reviews every report within 1 business day to decide whether other residents are at risk and what protective steps to take. The Administrator documents these steps and tells the resident what happened, in a way they can understand, and offers support.

Staff do not retaliate against, threaten, discipline or treat differently any person who reports in good faith. The Administrator investigates any claim of retaliation and takes disciplinary action under SB-02. Retaliation is grounds for termination.
Staff who violate this policy, including failing to report, are subject to discipline up to termination, in line with SB-02 and STF-06.

The Administrator posts the CCL complaint unit address and phone number and the resident personal rights where residents and visitors can see them, and tells residents about them at admission and at least annually under 22 CCR §80072.

Staff do not take, borrow, use or direct a resident's money or property for staff or facility use. The Administrator reviews personal funds under SB-08 at least monthly, and reports suspected exploitation under this policy.

The Administrator keeps all abuse reports, records and outcomes in a confidential incident file. This file is kept separate from the personnel file and resident record where required, and disclosed only as the law allows under IR-04 and 45 CFR 164.530.
The Administrator reviews abuse, neglect and exploitation reports and outcomes quarterly under GOV-04, looks for patterns and updates training and supervision.

responsibilities.duty: Be mandated reporters, report suspected abuse and rights violations promptly, protect residents, and never retaliate.
Train staff, make or confirm reports within time limits, protect residents, separate suspected staff, and keep records.
Take reports and perform the Administrator's duties when the Administrator is unavailable.
Receive reports about the Administrator, ensure compliance and review quarterly trends.

documentation: Mandated reporter acknowledgment for each employee
Training records on abuse prevention and reporting
WIC §15630 phone report log and written follow-up reports
CCL incident report (LIC 624 or current form) and 7-day written report
Regional center SIR records
Notes on protective actions, investigation outcome and corrective action
Record of notice to the resident and authorized representative
Posted notice of the CCL complaint line and personal rights

policies.title: Reportable Incidents, Special Incident Reports and Investigations
policies.applies_to: Administrator, all direct care staff, on-call managers
policies.purpose: To make sure every reportable incident is identified, reported to CCL, the regional center and the authorized representative on time, investigated and used to improve care.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] reports incidents to CCL by the next working day and sends a written report within 7 days (22 CCR §80061). Reportable incidents are listed below. The facility also reports to the vendoring regional center through a Special Incident Report (SIR) under 17 CCR §54327. Before May 1, 2026 the regional center timeline was an immediate phone, email or fax notice and written notice within 24 hours, with a written report within 48 hours. DDS has indicated the 24-hour and 48-hour timelines continue under the amended rule. The Administrator confirms the current §54327 text and the category list, along with 17 CCR §56027, with the regional center, and follows whichever requirement is stricter. The regional center is copied on any later written report sent to CCL. Every SIR is recorded in consumer notes.

definitions.definition: Any event listed in 22 CCR §80061: any death; death from injury, abuse or other than natural causes (including away from the facility); AED use; injury needing medical treatment; unusual incident or client absence that threatens health or safety; suspected psychological abuse; epidemic outbreak; poisoning; catastrophe; fire or explosion.
The written report to the regional center of an incident that falls in the categories of 17 CCR §54327, such as death, missing person, serious injury or suspected abuse.
The person legally authorized to act for the resident, who must also be notified of certain incidents.
An event that is out of the ordinary and threatens or could threaten the health or safety of a resident.

procedures: Staff respond first to the immediate needs of the resident: first aid, 911 if needed, protecting others, and securing the area. Staff notify the Administrator or on-call manager by phone as soon as the person is safe.

The Administrator decides on the same day whether the event is reportable to CCL and to the regional center, using the lists in 22 CCR §80061 and 17 CCR §54327 posted in the office. When there is any doubt, the Administrator reports and does not wait.

The staff member who was present writes an incident account on the facility incident form before the end of the shift. It records the resident's name, date, time and place, what happened, who was present, what staff did, injuries and treatment, who was notified and the outcome. Staff stick to facts and do not guess.

The Administrator notifies CCL by phone or email by the next working day for each reportable event, and sends the written report within 7 days on LIC 624 or the current CCL form. The written report gives the client's name, age, sex and admission date, the date and nature of the event, physician findings and treatment, and the disposition.

The Administrator notifies the regional center by phone, email or fax immediately for urgent events (such as death, missing person, suspected abuse or serious injury) and no later than 24 hours after learning of the event for all other SIR categories. The Administrator submits the written SIR within 48 hours. Where the regional center instructs a different timeline in writing, the Administrator follows the regional center and keeps the instruction on file.
The Administrator copies the regional center on any later written report sent to CCL, and sends the regional center any follow-up information as it becomes available.

The Administrator notifies the authorized representative of the events in 22 CCR §80061(b)(1)(A)-(H) and provides a copy of the report, using the contact in the resident's record. The Administrator records the time and the person told.

For an epidemic outbreak, the Administrator immediately notifies the local fire authority as §80061 requires and, when appropriate, the local health officer. This also applies to poisonings and catastrophes. The Administrator follows HE-03.
For suspected physical abuse, the Administrator also makes the 2-hour or 24-hour reports under WIC §15630 as set out in BSP-03. For a death, the Administrator also follows HW-05.

The Administrator records a short factual SIR entry in the resident's consumer notes, listing the date, time, type of incident, who was notified, report numbers if any and follow-up. The full incident file is kept separate under REC-01.

The Administrator starts an internal review within 1 business day. The review covers what happened, why, whether policies and plans were followed, whether the resident and others are now safe, and whether staffing, training, environment or supports need to change.

The Administrator completes the review within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days and records findings, corrective actions, who is responsible and due dates. The Administrator updates the Needs and Services Plan and tells the planning team where a resident's plan changes.

The Administrator cooperates fully with CCL, the regional center, law enforcement and any other agency that investigates. The Administrator provides requested records promptly and does not interfere with interviews. Staff may speak with investigators without prior approval.

The Administrator keeps a reportable incident log that lists each event, date, reports made, dates sent, and follow-up status. The Administrator checks the log weekly so that no 7-day or 48-hour deadline is missed.

Within 10 working days of any change in organization, mailing address, corporate CEO or plan of operation that affects services, the Administrator also reports the change to CCL under 22 CCR §80061(e), and notifies the regional center under REC-02.

Each quarter the Administrator reviews incident trends by type, time, place, resident and staff under GOV-04, and reports to the governing body. The Administrator confirms, at least once a year and whenever DDS announces rule changes, that this policy still matches 17 CCR §54327 and §56027.

responsibilities.duty: Make residents safe, call the Administrator, and write factual incident accounts before the end of the shift.
Decide reportability, submit CCL and regional center reports on time, notify authorized representatives, investigate, and track corrective actions.
Receive after-hours incident calls and make time-sensitive notifications when the Administrator cannot be reached.
Review incident trends and make sure corrective actions are carried out.

CCL reports (LIC 624 or current form) with proof of the next-working-day notice and the 7-day written report
Regional center SIRs and later written reports, with time sent
Notification log for authorized representatives
Consumer notes entry for each SIR
Internal review and corrective action record
Reportable incident tracking log

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
policies.applies_to: Administrator, all direct care staff, on-call managers, and transportation staff
policies.purpose: To protect residents who may leave the facility without a safe plan, to respond quickly when a resident is missing, and to do so without limiting any resident's right to leave the facility.
policies.policy: Residents have the right to leave the facility at any time. Curfews and house rules are allowed, but this right does not apply to a resident with a conservator or other legal authority that limits it (22 CCR §80072). [AGENCY NAME] does not lock residents in any room or in the building, and does not use locks to prevent exit without prior CCL approval. Elopement protocols apply only to residents who are at risk because of a documented need, and each at-risk resident's risk and response are recorded in the Needs and Services Plan (22 CCR §85068.2). If a resident's absence threatens their health or safety, the facility reports it to CCL by the next working day and in writing within 7 days (22 CCR §80061). A missing resident for whom a missing-persons report has been filed is also reported to the regional center as a Special Incident Report.

definitions.definition: A resident whose whereabouts are unknown, who is not where their plan says they should be, and whose absence may threaten their health or safety.
A documented risk that a resident may leave the facility or a supervised activity and be unable to stay safe, for example because of confusion, lack of safety awareness or a history of wandering.

definitions.term: Absence that threatens health or safety
definitions.definition: An absence in which the resident may be in danger because of their health, medication needs, disabilities, weather, location, or other circumstances.
A voluntary record in which a resident or staff notes the resident's departure time, destination and expected return.

procedures: Before or on the day of admission, the Administrator assesses each resident's elopement risk from the referral packet, the IPP, history, health conditions and the resident's own account. The assessment is recorded in the Needs and Services Plan.

For a resident who is at risk, the plan states the specific warning signs, the level of supervision, routes and places the person has gone before, a current photograph and description, contact details of family and friends, and the steps staff take if the resident leaves. The resident and authorized representative take part in writing the plan.

The facility uses the least restrictive supports to keep at-risk residents safe, such as staff accompaniment, planned activity, a door chime that alerts staff, a buddy system on outings, or ID that the resident agrees to carry. Any support that limits freedom to leave goes through IR-02. Staff do not lock exits or lock residents in a room, and a secured perimeter is used only with CCL's prior approval, as described in BSP-02.

Residents who are not at risk may come and go as they choose. The facility invites residents to tell staff where they are going and when they expect to return, but a resident is not required to sign out and is not penalized for leaving. Staff record voluntary sign-outs.

If staff notice a resident is not where expected, the staff member immediately checks the house, yard, bathrooms, bedrooms, vehicles and nearby places. The staff member calls the person by name and asks other residents and staff. Another staff member covers the rest of the residents so that they are not left without supervision. Residents never count as staff and are not asked to supervise others (22 CCR §80065(j)).
The staff member immediately tells the Administrator or on-call manager that a resident is missing, and calls additional staff as needed to search. The Administrator takes charge of the response.

If the missing resident is at risk, or if the resident cannot be found after 15 minutes of searching, the Administrator or staff calls 911 or the local law enforcement agency and files a missing-persons report. The staff member gives the resident's description, photograph, clothing, health needs, medications and likely locations.

The Administrator notifies the authorized representative and family contacts as soon as possible, and the regional center by phone, email or fax immediately. The regional center is also told when the resident is found. The Administrator records each call, the time and the person spoken to.

Staff continue the search, with a staff member staying at the facility in case the resident returns. Searchers check places where the resident has gone before, and carry a phone so the Administrator can update them. Staff do not put themselves or other residents in danger.

When the resident is found, staff check for injuries and health needs, call 911 or arrange medical care if necessary, offer comfort and food, and return the resident to the facility. Staff tell law enforcement, the authorized representative and the regional center that the resident has been found.

If the absence threatens the resident's health or safety, the Administrator reports it to CCL by the next working day and submits the written report within 7 days on LIC 624 or the current CCL form, under 22 CCR §80061. The report gives the resident's name, age, sex and admission date, the date and nature of the event, any medical findings and treatment, and what happened. The Administrator copies the authorized representative and the regional center.

A missing-persons report filed with law enforcement is an SIR category. The Administrator submits an SIR to the regional center under BSP-04 and 17 CCR §54327, and confirms current requirements with the regional center.

The Administrator records the event in consumer notes the same day and reviews the event within 1 business day. The review asks whether staffing was adequate, whether the resident's plan was followed, what the resident was trying to do or avoid, and whether the plan needs updating.

The Administrator updates the Needs and Services Plan and elopement risk strategies after each event, meets with the resident and authorized representative, and asks the regional center service coordinator to convene the planning team when supports need to change. The Administrator trains staff on any change.

A resident who is away by choice and returns late is welcomed back. Staff do not punish or reprimand a resident for leaving or returning late, and do not remove privileges as a consequence (22 CCR §80072). Staff check the resident's wellbeing and note any safety concerns.
The Administrator holds a missing-person drill for staff at least once a year on each shift pattern, records it, and reviews the results through GOV-04.

Assess risk at admission, write plans with the resident, direct the response, notify the authorities, representative and regional center, and file reports on time.
Lead the response and notifications when the Administrator is unavailable.

policies.title: Residential Environment, Accessibility and Bedrooms
policies.applies_to: All staff, the Administrator, and the licensee; the physical home, grounds, and every resident bedroom and bathroom
policies.purpose: To make sure the home is safe, clean, accessible, homelike and set up as Title 22 requires, so that each resident has private, comfortable living space and the facility remains eligible for CCL licensure and regional center vendorization.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates its Adult Residential Facility in a physical plant that meets 22 CCR §85087 (ARF Buildings and Grounds) and 22 CCR §85088 (Fixtures, Furniture, Equipment and Supplies). No more than two residents share a bedroom, and no bedroom is used as a passageway to another room, bathroom or exit. The home has at least one toilet and washbasin for every six persons and at least one tub or shower for every ten persons, counting live-in staff and family members who share the fixtures. Every resident has a bed, chair, nightstand, lamp and drawer space of at least two drawers or 8 cubic feet. [AGENCY NAME] provides clean linens, hygiene supplies, emergency lighting and night lights, and a signal system where one is required. Before any lease is signed or the application is filed, the Administrator confirms that the lease allows licensed residential care, consistent with 22 CCR §80018(d)(3). Fire clearance is obtained through CCL under 22 CCR §80020, and a separate fire clearance is obtained before [AGENCY NAME] admits any nonambulatory resident or any person age 65 or older. The home is kept accessible and free of architectural barriers in line with the Americans with Disabilities Act, and reasonable modifications are made for residents with physical disabilities. This policy meets the facility-environment requirements of 22 CCR §85087, §85088, §80020 and §80018(d)(3).

definitions.definition: A person who is unable to leave the building without assistance in an emergency, including a person who uses a wheelchair or whose postural support makes them unable to move independently. A separate fire clearance is required before admission.
A room that must be walked through to reach another room, bathroom or exit. Bedrooms may not serve this purpose.
An audible or visual call or alarm system that lets a resident summon staff, installed where Title 22 requires it.

procedures: Before signing or renewing any lease, the Administrator reads the lease and confirms in writing with the landlord that the property may be used for licensed residential care, and keeps the lease and landlord information in the licensing file as required by 22 CCR §80018(d)(3).

Before CCL orientation and application filing, the Administrator completes a floor plan and grounds sketch showing every bedroom, bathroom, exit, hallway and outdoor area, and keeps it with the plan of operation.
The Administrator measures and records bedroom capacity and assigns no more than two residents per bedroom, based on the home's approved capacity and each resident's compatibility and preferences.

The Administrator checks the floor plan and walks the home to confirm that no bedroom is a passageway to another room, bathroom, kitchen or exit; any change to room use is made only after review against 22 CCR §85087.

The Administrator counts all persons who share bathroom fixtures, including live-in staff and family members, and confirms there is at least one toilet and washbasin per six persons and one tub or shower per ten persons. The count is recalculated before each admission and whenever a live-in person is added.

At admission, the Program Manager confirms that each resident's bedroom has a bed, chair, nightstand, lamp and drawers (at least two drawers or 8 cubic feet), and that clean linens, towels and hygiene supplies are available. Residents may bring and arrange their own furnishings and decorate their rooms.

The Program Manager walks the home weekly using a written environment checklist covering cleanliness, working lights, night lights, emergency lighting, floors and walkways, grab bars, water temperature, locks and signal system, and records the date, findings and corrective action.

Any hazard found is corrected immediately where possible. If it cannot be corrected the same day, the Program Manager removes the hazard from use, protects residents from it, writes a repair request to the Administrator, and records the target date.
Emergency lighting and night lights are tested monthly and batteries are replaced as needed. Results are recorded on the environment checklist.
Where a signal system is required, the Program Manager tests it monthly and assigns the responding staff person on each shift as described in HE-02 and STF-01.

Before admitting a nonambulatory person or a person age 65 or older, the Administrator requests the separate fire clearance through CCL and does not admit the person until the clearance is received and filed. The Administrator also confirms the bedroom location allows safe evacuation.
Before using any postural support that would make a resident nonambulatory, the Administrator confirms that the fire clearance in 22 CCR §80020 and §80072(a)(8)(D) is in place.

For residents who use wheelchairs, walkers or other mobility devices, the Program Manager confirms that doorways, hallways, bathrooms and the exits are usable by that resident, and arranges reasonable modifications consistent with the ADA through the landlord or the Administrator.

The Administrator documents any substantial change to the physical plant or room use. If it changes the services described in the plan of operation, the Administrator notifies CCL within 10 working days and updates the floor plan (see GOV-02 and SB-04).
The Administrator reviews this policy and the environment checklist at least annually and after any CCL or regional center finding, and records the review under GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Secures and maintains a lawful lease and property that allow licensed care; funds repairs, modifications and required fixtures and furnishings.
Ensures the physical plant meets 22 CCR §85087 and §85088; obtains fire clearances; manages the lease, floor plan and capacity; keeps the plan of operation current.
Conducts weekly environment checks, assigns bedrooms, tests lighting and the signal system, and records and corrects hazards.
Keep common areas and bedrooms clean and safe; report hazards, broken equipment and accessibility problems the same shift.
Are encouraged to personalize their rooms and to tell staff about repairs or comfort concerns.

documentation: Lease and landlord information showing licensed care is permitted
Floor plan and grounds sketch
Bedroom assignment and capacity record
Fixture count (persons per toilet, washbasin, tub or shower)
Weekly environment checklists and repair requests
Monthly emergency lighting and signal system test log
Fire clearance(s) from CCL, including separate clearance for nonambulatory or age 65+ residents
Records of accessibility modifications

policies.title: Fire Safety, Emergency Preparedness and Drills
policies.applies_to: All staff, the Administrator and all residents; all shifts including night supervision
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from fire and other emergencies by keeping a current fire clearance, training staff in emergency procedures, practicing evacuation, and reporting fires and explosions to CCL on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a fire clearance obtained through CCL under 22 CCR §80020 at all times. A separate fire clearance is obtained before admitting a nonambulatory resident or a person age 65 or older. All staff know the facility's emergency procedures and their own role in them. Night staff (10 p.m. to 7 a.m.) must be able to help in an emergency and must be trained in the facility's planned emergency procedures and in first aid, as required by 22 CCR §85065.6. Where a signal system is required, a staff person is assigned to respond to it, per 22 CCR §85065.6(i). Fire drills are held at the frequency required by Title 22, which the Administrator confirms with the CCL licensing analyst and records in the Emergency Disaster Plan (SA-01). As an agency standard, the home conducts drills at least quarterly and includes at least one drill during sleeping hours. Every fire or explosion is reported to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days, as required by 22 CCR §80061. Emergency procedures are part of the plan of operation required by 22 CCR §80022 and are updated whenever they change.

definitions.definition: Approval from the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal, obtained through CCL, that the home meets fire safety requirements for the residents it serves.
The hours of 10 p.m. to 7 a.m., when night staff must be on duty and trained for emergencies under 22 CCR §85065.6.
A practice in which staff and residents leave the building by planned routes to an assigned safe meeting place, with the time and any difficulties recorded.

procedures: Before licensure and before each change of resident population, the Administrator confirms through CCL that the fire clearance is current and covers the residents to be served, including any nonambulatory resident or person age 65 or older, and files the clearance in the facility's licensing file.

The Administrator and Program Manager post an evacuation floor plan showing exits, routes, meeting place, fire extinguisher locations and alarm locations in a prominent place on every level of the home.

The Administrator writes the fire and evacuation procedures in the Emergency Disaster Plan (SA-01), including assignments for each shift: who calls 911, who helps each resident who needs assistance, who checks rooms, who takes the resident roster and emergency contact list, and who meets responders.

Before working alone or being counted in the staffing plan, each new staff member is trained on the emergency procedures, shown the exits, extinguishers, alarms and meeting place, and signs a training record. The trainer is the Administrator or Program Manager.

Night staff complete training in the planned emergency procedures and first aid before working any shift between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. The Administrator keeps the training dates and certificates in the personnel file (see STF-05).

The Administrator confirms the Title 22 fire drill frequency with the CCL licensing analyst and records it in SA-01. The Program Manager schedules drills at that frequency or at least quarterly, whichever is more often, and varies the day and time, including at least one drill during sleeping hours.

During each drill, the Program Manager or designee times the evacuation, notes which residents needed help and what help they needed, and records any obstacle. Residents are given the choice and support to take part in a way that suits their abilities.

After each drill, the Program Manager records the date, time, shift, staff present, number of residents evacuated, time to reach the meeting place and corrective actions on the drill log, and reviews it with staff within 7 days.

Smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and fire extinguishers are checked monthly. The Program Manager records the checks and arranges service, battery replacement or replacement of any defective device the same day.

Where a signal system is required, the Program Manager assigns on each shift, including nights, a named staff person responsible for responding to it, and tests the system monthly. The assignment is written in the shift schedule.
The Administrator keeps exits, hallways and stairs clear, forbids blocked or locked exits that stop emergency egress, and corrects any storage or furniture that blocks exit routes immediately.

In a fire, staff follow the posted procedure: get residents to safety first, call 911, account for every resident using the roster, and do not re-enter the building until released by the fire authority.

After any fire or explosion, the Administrator telephones CCL by the next working day, then submits the written report to CCL within 7 days. The report includes each affected resident's name, age, sex and admission date, the date and nature of the event, any physician findings and treatment, and the disposition.

If a resident is injured and needs medical treatment as a result of the fire or any other emergency, the Administrator also reports the injury to CCL by the next working day with the 7-day written report, and notifies the resident's authorized representative and the regional center as described in BSP-04 and REC-02.
If the event changes how the home operates or the plan of operation, the Administrator reports changes that affect services to CCL within 10 working days and updates the plan under 22 CCR §80022.
The Administrator reviews each fire or explosion event, drill log and corrective action at least annually as part of quality review (GOV-04) and updates the training and procedures as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains fire clearances, confirms drill frequency, makes all CCL reports, and ensures emergency procedures and training are current.
Schedules and records drills, checks alarms and extinguishers, assigns signal system response, and trains staff.
Remain awake and available during night supervision hours, know emergency procedures and first aid, and respond to the signal system and any emergency.
Know evacuation routes and their assignments, assist residents safely, and report hazards immediately.
Take part in drills with the support they need and tell staff about concerns, such as difficulty hearing alarms.

documentation: Current fire clearance(s) from CCL
Emergency Disaster Plan and evacuation floor plan
Staff emergency procedure training records and first aid certificates
Fire drill log with date, time, shift, evacuation time, resident support needs and corrective action
Monthly alarm, extinguisher and signal system check log
Next-working-day CCL notification record and 7-day written report for any fire or explosion
Copies of notices to authorized representatives and the regional center

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, the Administrator and all residents; all cleaning, laundry, food, personal care and health care tasks
policies.purpose: To prevent the spread of infection among residents and staff, to protect staff from exposure to blood and other body fluids, and to ensure that outbreaks and ill personnel are handled and reported as the law requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written infection control plan on form LIC 9282 and keeps it with the plan of operation, as required by 22 CCR §85022(a)(1). All staff are trained in the plan and follow standard precautions in every task. Staff health screening, including a TB test, is completed by or under a physician no more than one year before or seven days after employment, and personnel who are ill are relieved of duty, as required by 22 CCR §80065. Epidemic outbreaks are reported to CCL by the next working day, with a written report within 7 days, under 22 CCR §80061, and are reported immediately to the local fire authority; the local health officer is notified when appropriate. Staff who may be exposed to blood or other potentially infectious materials are protected under the federal Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030.

definitions.definition: Practices applied to every resident and every task, including hand hygiene, gloves, cleaning of surfaces, safe handling of laundry and sharps, and respiratory etiquette.
An unusual number of cases of the same illness among residents or staff in a short time, such as influenza, norovirus or COVID-19.
Contact of a staff member's eyes, mouth, broken skin or other mucous membrane with blood or other potentially infectious material.

procedures: Before licensure, the Administrator completes form LIC 9282, the infection control plan, and files it with the plan of operation. The Administrator reviews and updates it at least annually and whenever services or the resident population change.

Each new employee is trained on the infection control plan, hand hygiene, glove use, cleaning and disinfecting, laundry handling, safe food handling, and when to stay home, before working alone. Training is recorded in the personnel file (see STF-05).

Each employee obtains a health screening and TB test by or under a physician no more than one year before or seven days after the start of employment. Results are kept in the personnel file (see STF-04).

The Program Manager asks every employee at the start of each shift to report fever, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, cough or other signs of contagious illness. An ill employee is relieved of duty and does not return until free of contagious symptoms or released by a health care provider.
Staff perform hand hygiene before and after resident contact, before handling food or medication, after toileting assistance, after glove removal and after contact with body fluids.

Staff wear gloves and other personal protective equipment for tasks that involve blood or body fluids. The Administrator ensures a supply of gloves, masks, gowns, eye protection, disinfectant and hand sanitizer is always available in the home.

Staff clean and disinfect high-touch surfaces daily, bathrooms and shared equipment after use, and spills of blood or body fluids immediately using an EPA-registered disinfectant per the label. The cleaning schedule is posted and initialed.
Soiled linens and clothing are handled with gloves, washed separately from food items on a hot cycle or as manufacturer's instructions allow, and not shaken or carried against the body.
Sharps, such as lancets used by the resident for self-monitoring, are placed in a puncture-resistant sharps container located where used. Needles are never recapped, bent or broken by staff.

The Administrator offers hepatitis B vaccination, at no cost, to any employee with expected exposure to blood, and keeps a written exposure control plan under 29 CFR 1910.1030 that includes post-exposure evaluation and follow-up.

After an exposure incident, the employee washes the area, tells the Program Manager immediately, and receives prompt medical evaluation. The Administrator documents the incident on an exposure incident form and keeps it confidential.
The Program Manager encourages recommended vaccinations for residents and staff, supports residents to attend preventive care, and records refusals in the resident's record (see HW-02).

When two or more residents or staff have symptoms suggesting an outbreak, the Program Manager notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator separates ill residents when feasible, increases cleaning, arranges medical care (see HW-04), and consults the local health officer when appropriate.

The Administrator immediately notifies the local fire authority of an epidemic outbreak, telephones CCL by the next working day, and sends CCL a written report within 7 days with each affected resident's name, age, sex and admission date, the date and nature of the event, physician findings and treatment, and disposition.

The Administrator also notifies each affected resident's authorized representative and the regional center as described in BSP-04 and REC-02, and applies the guidance of the local health officer to restrict visitors or activities as advised.
The Administrator reviews infection events, staff illness, exposure incidents and cleaning logs at least quarterly under GOV-04 and revises the infection control plan and training as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains LIC 9282, ensures supplies and training, manages exposure follow-up, and makes outbreak notifications and reports.
Screens staff for illness each shift, enforces cleaning and hand hygiene practices, and escalates suspected outbreaks.
Follow standard precautions, use protective equipment, report symptoms and exposures right away, and stay home when ill.
Advises on infection control, immunizations and outbreak response when engaged under HW-02.
Are taught and helped to wash hands, cover coughs and report feeling unwell.

Staff infection control training records
Health screening and TB test results in personnel files
Employee illness and return-to-work notes
Bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan, hepatitis B vaccination offers or declinations, and exposure incident forms
Cleaning schedule and sign-off logs
Outbreak notifications and CCL reports with proof of the next-working-day call and 7-day written report
Resident immunization and refusal records

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Program Manager, direct support and cooking staff, and all residents
policies.purpose: To ensure residents receive nutritious meals that match their preferences, health needs and cultural choices, and that modified diets, allergies and choking precautions are identified, documented and carried out safely.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs staff in the numbers needed to meet residents' food service needs, as required by 22 CCR §85065(e)(1), and uses support staff for cooking as allowed by 22 CCR §85065(c). Menus are part of the plan of operation required by 22 CCR §80022, are kept current, and are followed (see SB-07). Residents help plan menus and choose foods. Every resident's modified diet, food allergy, texture requirement and dysphagia or choking precaution is recorded in the Needs and Services Plan under 22 CCR §85068.2, ordered by a health care provider where required, and carried out exactly. All staff who prepare or serve food, or who help residents eat, are trained on these precautions before doing so.

definitions.definition: A diet changed in texture, fluid consistency, calories, sodium, carbohydrate or other content because of a medical need or provider order.
Difficulty swallowing, which can lead to choking or aspiration.
The cooks, direct support staff and support staff scheduled to plan, prepare, serve and clean up meals so that residents' food needs are met.

procedures: At admission, the Program Manager records each resident's food likes and dislikes, cultural and religious food practices, allergies, medical diet orders and eating or swallowing difficulties in the Needs and Services Plan under 22 CCR §85068.2, using the medical assessment and information from the resident, authorized representative and regional center.

If the resident has a modified diet, allergy or swallowing concern, the Program Manager obtains the written diet order or recommendation from the resident's physician, dietitian or speech-language pathologist, files it in the resident's record, and adds it to the Needs and Services Plan.

The Administrator creates the sample and weekly menus with resident input, ensures they offer a balanced selection and any modified versions needed, and keeps them current as part of the plan of operation (see SB-07 and 22 CCR §80022).
The Program Manager posts the current menu where residents can see it and writes any substitutions made. The menu and substitutions are retained for the period in REC-01.

The Program Manager posts a confidential resident diet and allergy list in the kitchen and in a place staff can see. It names each resident who has a diet restriction, texture requirement, allergy or choking risk, and is updated within 24 hours of any change.

The Program Manager schedules at least one trained staff person at each meal who is responsible for food preparation and service, and makes sure the staffing plan covers food service so that direct care and supervision are not reduced during meals, as required by 22 CCR §85065(e)(1).

Before staff work independently in the kitchen or help a resident eat, the Program Manager trains them on safe food handling, allergen avoidance, the resident diet list, texture modifications and thickened liquids. Training is recorded in the personnel file.

For a resident with dysphagia or choking risk, staff follow the written precautions: correct positioning, size of bites, pace, supervision during meals, prohibited foods, and the emergency response. Staff stay with the resident throughout the meal.
Staff train in and know how to respond to choking by abdominal thrusts and first aid and keep first aid training current (see HW-03 and HW-04).

Food is stored, prepared and served under sanitary conditions. Perishable food is kept at safe temperatures, the refrigerator and freezer temperatures are checked and logged daily, and leftovers are dated and discarded on schedule.
The Program Manager makes sure residents can get snacks and drinks between meals, and that residents are not denied food or drink as a form of discipline (see SB-05).

If a resident refuses meals, loses weight, shows signs of dehydration or has a change in eating or swallowing, staff report it to the Program Manager the same day. The Program Manager contacts the health care provider and updates the Needs and Services Plan (see HW-04).
The Program Manager reviews each resident's weight, diet and dining supports at least every six months and after any change of condition, and records the review.
Residents who wish to cook, shop or plan meals are supported to take part to the extent they choose, and the support is recorded in the person's plan (see PCS-02).
The Administrator reviews menus, diet lists and food storage logs at least annually, and the plan of operation is updated if menus or food service practices change.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the staffing plan covers food service, menus remain current in the plan of operation, and training and supplies are provided.
Records diets and allergies in the Needs and Services Plan, obtains provider orders, posts the diet list, and trains staff.
Prepare and serve food as written, follow diet and choking precautions, support resident choice, and report problems the same day.

responsibilities.role: Health Care Provider / Dietitian / Speech-Language Pathologist
responsibilities.duty: Provide diet orders, texture recommendations and swallowing guidance for residents who need them.
Help plan menus, choose meals and tell staff about food needs or concerns.

Written diet orders and swallowing assessments
Current menus and substitutions
Posted diet and allergy list
Staff training records on food handling and choking precautions
Refrigerator and freezer temperature logs

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Program Manager, all staff who drive or arrange transportation, and all residents
policies.purpose: To make sure residents can safely get to medical and dental care, work, activities and community outings, and that anyone who transports residents is licensed, supervised and prepared.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] describes how transportation is provided in the plan of operation required by 22 CCR §80022. The licensee ensures residents are transported to needed medical and dental care, as required by 22 CCR §80075. Only staff with a valid California driver license and a clean, acceptable driving record drive residents, and the license is kept in the personnel file. Staff provide direct supervision during potentially dangerous activities, as required by 22 CCR §80065. Vehicles are kept in safe working condition and are accessible to residents with disabilities in line with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Residents are supported to use public transit, paratransit and other community transportation so that they have real choices about getting around, not only agency vehicles.

definitions.definition: A vehicle owned or leased by [AGENCY NAME] and used to transport residents.
A vehicle owned by a staff member and used to transport residents only when approved by the Administrator in advance and covered by proper insurance.
Door-to-door public transportation for people with disabilities who cannot use fixed-route transit.

procedures: The Administrator writes the transportation plan in the plan of operation, covering medical and dental trips, work and day program, community outings, vehicles used and how rides are arranged. It is updated under 22 CCR §80022 whenever the arrangements change.

Before any staff member drives a resident, the Administrator verifies and copies the staff member's valid California driver license, obtains a driving record check, and confirms the staff member is at least 18 years old. The documents are placed in the personnel file (see STF-05).

The Administrator confirms that any vehicle used to transport residents is registered, insured with the required liability coverage, and in safe operating condition, and keeps copies of registration and insurance proof.
Personal vehicles are used only with the Administrator's written approval, proof of the owner's insurance, and a record of the vehicle and driver.

The Program Manager arranges and schedules transportation to medical and dental appointments, including follow-up visits and emergency care, as part of 22 CCR §80075, and records each trip, destination and escort in the resident's record.

A staff member accompanies a resident to an appointment where the resident needs help communicating, understanding information or consenting, and brings the medication list, face sheet, and any needed paperwork and documents the visit results (see HW-02 and IR-05).

Staff perform a quick vehicle check before each trip, including seatbelts, lights, tires, wheelchair securements and lifts, and fuel. Defects are reported to the Administrator immediately and a vehicle with a safety defect is not used.

Every rider is buckled in with a working seat belt or is secured in a wheelchair using a manufacturer-approved tie-down and occupant restraint system. Staff load and unload residents with attention to their dignity and safety.
Drivers do not use handheld phones or other devices while driving, do not drive while impaired by alcohol, drugs or fatigue, and follow all traffic laws.

Staff provide direct supervision during outings and on transport, at a level set by each resident's Needs and Services Plan, including at roadways, parking lots, loading areas and other potentially dangerous places (see 22 CCR §80065). Staff do not leave a resident alone in a vehicle.
Residents who can travel on their own, and who choose to do so, are supported through travel training for public transit or paratransit as described in the person-centered plan (see PCS-03).

The driver carries a first aid kit, phone, emergency contact list and the information needed to handle a medical emergency or breakdown. If a resident is injured or becomes ill, the driver pulls over safely, calls 911 if needed, notifies the Program Manager, and follows HW-04 and BSP-04.

If an accident, injury, missing person or other incident occurs during transport, the driver reports it to the Administrator immediately, and the Administrator completes the required notifications and reports under BSP-04 and REC-02.
The Administrator reviews driver files, vehicle maintenance and trip records at least annually and updates the transportation plan and any needed vehicle upgrades or accessibility changes.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the transportation plan, verifies driver licenses, vehicle insurance and safety, and makes any required reports.
Schedules transport, assigns qualified drivers and escorts, and checks that supervision matches each resident's plan.
Drive safely, inspect vehicles, secure riders, supervise residents during trips, and report incidents immediately.
Choose and help plan their transportation, and tell staff about trips they need or difficulties they have.
