Driver license copies and driving record checks in personnel files
Vehicle registration, insurance and maintenance records
Pre-trip vehicle check log
Trip log with date, destination, driver and residents transported
Medical and dental appointment records
Incident and accident reports
Travel training records for residents

policies.title: Water Safety (Pools and Bodies of Water, If Applicable)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Program Manager and all staff, and all residents, if the home has a pool, spa or similar water feature or if residents use a pool or body of water on outings
policies.purpose: To prevent drowning and water-related injuries by controlling access to pools and other bodies of water and by ensuring trained, certified supervision whenever residents swim or use water.
policies.policy: This policy applies only if the home has a pool, spa, pond or similar body of water on the property, or if residents use a pool or body of water elsewhere. If it does not apply, the Administrator records that finding in the licensing file. Whenever residents use a pool or body of water that needs swim rescue, an adult non-client holding a valid water safety certificate is present and gives direct supervision, as required by 22 CCR §80065. Each resident's swimming ability and any water-related risk is recorded in the Needs and Services Plan. Grounds and any water feature must comply with 22 CCR §85087 so that residents are not exposed to hazards. [AGENCY NAME] limits unsupervised access to water, and a resident is never left alone near water.

definitions.term: Body of water needing swim rescue
definitions.definition: A pool, pond, lake, ocean or similar water in which a person could drown and rescue by a trained swimmer might be needed.
A current certificate showing the person has completed training in water safety and rescue, such as lifeguarding or water safety instruction from a recognized provider.
Staff are close enough to see, hear and reach the resident immediately and are watching the resident continuously.

procedures: Before licensure and at each annual review, the Administrator inspects the property and records whether any pool, spa, pond or other water feature exists. If none exists and the home will not take residents to swim, the Administrator records "Not applicable" and signs and dates the record.

If the home has a water feature, the Administrator ensures it is enclosed or secured to prevent unsupervised access, such as with fences, self-closing and self-latching gates, locks or covers, and keeps it in good repair, consistent with the grounds requirements of 22 CCR §85087 and local law.

The Administrator ensures that rescue and safety equipment, such as a life ring, reaching pole, first aid kit and phone, is kept at the water and in working order, and that the posted rules, depth markings and emergency numbers are visible.

At admission and annually, the Program Manager assesses each resident's swimming ability, comfort in water, seizure history, behavior and any other risk, and records it in the Needs and Services Plan, along with the level of supervision needed (see PCS-01 and HW-03).
A resident whose assessment shows a drowning risk, such as a seizure disorder or inability to swim, receives additional supervision and any needed flotation device, as written in the plan.

Before any water activity, the Program Manager confirms that an adult non-client with a valid water safety certificate will be present and is designated as the water watcher. The certificate copy is on file or taken on the outing.

The water watcher stays within reach of residents in the water, watches them at all times, does not use a phone or perform other duties, and has an assigned alternate when a break is needed. Residents who are not in the water but near it are also supervised.
Staff count residents before entering and after leaving the water and record the activity, the water watcher, the residents present and any problems on the activity log.
Residents are supported to choose whether to swim and are not required to participate. Their choice, and any plan to teach swimming, is respected and recorded (see IR-01).

If a resident is in distress, the water watcher or staff retrieves the resident using safe rescue, calls 911, begins first aid or CPR as trained, and notifies the Program Manager and Administrator immediately (see HW-04).

After any drowning scare, injury or death, the Administrator makes the reports described in BSP-04, REC-02 and HW-05, including the next-working-day report to CCL and the written report within 7 days.

The Administrator checks the water safety certificates for expiration dates at least quarterly, schedules renewals before they expire, and reviews this policy, the enclosure and the equipment at least annually and after any water incident.

responsibilities.duty: Determines whether the policy applies, secures water features, verifies water safety certificates, and makes any required reports.
Assesses each resident's swimming ability, writes supervision levels into plans, designates the water watcher, and keeps the activity log.
Gives continuous direct supervision during water use and performs rescue and first aid if needed.
Keep residents away from water without supervision, support resident choice about swimming, and report any hazards.
Make their own choices about swimming and follow the safety rules they have been taught.

documentation: Record that the water safety policy applies or is not applicable
Water safety certificates for each designated water watcher
Needs and Services Plan sections on swimming ability and supervision level
Water activity logs with date, participants and water watcher
Inspection records for enclosures, gates and rescue equipment
Incident reports for any water-related event

policies.title: Staffing Ratios, Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, support staff, volunteers, the Administrator and any relief or on-call personnel at [AGENCY NAME], an Adult Residential Facility licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing and vendored by the regional center (service code 915 or 905).
policies.purpose: To make sure enough trained, cleared and capable staff are on duty at all hours to meet each resident's needs, to meet or exceed the Title 17 and Title 22 minimums, and to keep an awake staff person on the premises overnight.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs personnel who are competent and in the numbers needed to meet resident needs (22 CCR §80065; 22 CCR §85065(b)). Basic direct care staffing meets 17 CCR §56004 whenever residents are under facility supervision: Level 2, one direct care staff per up to 6 residents; Level 3, one per up to 3; Level 4, one per up to 2; and Levels 5 and 6, one staff for the first resident. When the home serves more residents than these counts, [AGENCY NAME] adds the weekly direct care hours that §56004(d) assigns to the home's service level. (The regulation's legacy levels map to current Levels 2-6 as follows: Level 3 = old 3/4A/4B; Level 4 = old 4C-4E; Level 5 = old 4F-4H; Level 6 = old 4I.) For regional center residents who rely on others for all activities of daily living (ADLs), day staffing is as the regional center specifies and never less than 1:3 (22 CCR §85065.5). Overnight (10 p.m.-7 a.m.), at least one trained staff person is on the premises, and [AGENCY NAME] schedules that person awake at all times. Homes of 15 or fewer residents are required to have at least one person on call on the premises. For regional center residents who need total care, night supervision is as the regional center requires and never less than 22 CCR §85065.6 (f) and (g). The DDS rate models for Level 3 and above assume awake staff around the clock. When more than one standard applies, [AGENCY NAME] follows the highest. Volunteers and residents are never counted toward required staffing, and residents are never used as substitutes for staff (22 CCR §80065). If CCL requires added staff, [AGENCY NAME] complies. Support staff for office work, cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance are scheduled so that these tasks do not reduce direct care coverage (22 CCR §85065(c)). This policy does not list official checklist items because none were assigned to it.

definitions.definition: An employee who is 18 or older, cleared under STF-02, oriented under STF-03, and on duty in the home providing care and supervision to residents.
Any time a resident is in the home or in the care of staff, including outings, appointments and transportation. The basic staffing minimum applies at those times.
A staff person on the premises between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. who is awake, alert and able to respond to residents and emergencies.
The ARM level (2-6) approved for the home by the regional center. It sets the minimum staffing and training under 17 CCR §56004.
A resident who relies on others for all ADLs. This resident triggers the stricter day and night standards in 22 CCR §85065.5 and §85065.6.

procedures: The Administrator records the home's licensed capacity, the RC-approved service level, and each resident's ADL dependence and supervision needs from the IPP and Needs and Services Plan. These are entered on the written staffing plan.

The Administrator calculates the minimum basic direct care staffing for the service level under 17 CCR §56004, using the ratios in the policy statement. The Administrator then adds the weekly direct care hours required by the §56004(d) table when the number of residents exceeds the basic count. The calculation is signed and dated.

For any resident who relies on others for all ADLs, the Administrator confirms the regional center's written day and night staffing requirement. The Administrator never schedules fewer than 1:3 on days or less than the §85065.6 night minimum.

The Administrator sets the staffing plan by shift (day, evening, night) at the highest applicable standard. The plan is shared with the vendoring regional center and updated whenever residents, levels or needs change.
The Administrator prepares a written weekly schedule showing each person's name, role and shift, and posts it where staff can see it. Schedules are kept for at least five years.

Only paid employees who are 18 or older, cleared under STF-02, and oriented under STF-03 are counted as direct care staff. Volunteers, residents, visitors and persons doing only office, cooking, cleaning, laundry or maintenance work are not counted.

The Administrator schedules support staff for cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance in addition to direct care staff. Food service is staffed so that residents' meals and modified diets are provided (see HE-04).

For overnight shifts (10 p.m.-7 a.m.), the Administrator assigns at least one staff person who is awake for the entire shift. No staff person may sleep on duty. The night person must be trained in the facility's emergency procedures (SA-01) and in first aid, and must be able to help in an emergency.

Night staff make documented checks of residents at the frequency stated in each resident's Needs and Services Plan. If a signal or alarm system is installed for any resident, the Administrator names the staff person responsible for responding and writes this into the shift assignment.

If a staff person cannot work a scheduled shift, they call the Administrator or on-call supervisor at [PHONE] as early as possible. The Administrator uses the on-call list to find a qualified replacement. The departing staff person stays until relieved, and a shift report is exchanged at every change.

The Administrator provides direct supervision at potentially dangerous activities and areas. Whenever residents use a pool or body of water that requires swim rescue, an adult non-resident who holds a valid water safety certificate is present (see HE-06).
For outings, appointments, medical transportation and home visits, the Administrator schedules enough extra staff so that residents who remain in the home still have the required staffing.
The Administrator supervises any volunteer on duty and records the volunteer's name, date and tasks. A volunteer is never left alone with residents unless STF-02 clearance is on file.

When a resident's condition or behavior changes, or after an emergency or disaster, the Administrator reviews staffing the same day and adds staff as needed. The Administrator also asks the regional center to review the resident's service level when needs have changed (see PCS-01 and HW-04).
If CCL requires additional staff, the Administrator obtains the written reasons, adjusts the schedule by the date stated, and keeps the written notice in the facility file.

Each month the Administrator compares posted schedules with actual time records, corrects any shortfall within the same shift or next day, and notes the review in the staffing log. Scheduling and pay follow STF-08.

responsibilities.duty: Calculates and approves staffing, maintains the written schedule and on-call list, assures awake overnight coverage, and responds to CCL and regional center staffing requirements.
Work assigned shifts, stay until relieved, supervise residents continuously, stay awake on night shifts, and report staffing gaps immediately.
Perform office, cooking, cleaning, laundry and maintenance tasks so that direct care staff remain with residents.
Funds staffing at or above the required levels and approves any change to the staffing plan.

documentation: Staffing plan and ratio calculation signed by the Administrator
Weekly posted schedules (kept at least five years)
Time records and monthly schedule reconciliation log
On-call and relief staff list
Written regional center staffing requirements for total-care residents
Any CCL written notice requiring added staff
Night check records
Volunteer sign-in and supervision log

policies.title: Criminal Record Clearance (Live Scan) and Exemptions
policies.applies_to: All applicants, employees, volunteers and other persons requiring clearance at [AGENCY NAME], and the corporate CEO if the licensee is a corporation.
policies.purpose: To make sure that no one works or is present in the home before California criminal record clearance, an exemption, or an approved transfer is on file.
policies.policy: Every person who is employed at or has initial presence in [AGENCY NAME] must first have a California criminal record clearance, a criminal record exemption, or an approved transfer (22 CCR §80065(i); 22 CCR §80019). No staff person works or is present in the home, alone or supervised, until one of these is in place. The Administrator applies for clearance using Live Scan (LIC 9163) and the Criminal Record Statement (LIC 508). Fingerprints are also required for a new corporate CEO (22 CCR §80019(d)). Because the research behind this manual does not cover separate registry checks, [AGENCY NAME] confirms with CCL and the vendoring regional center whether any additional check applies before hiring. This policy does not list official checklist items because none were assigned to it.

definitions.definition: The electronic fingerprinting process used to obtain a California criminal record clearance, requested on form LIC 9163.
Written confirmation from CCL that the person has no disqualifying record.
CCL's written approval allowing a person with a record to work or be present. It is issued only after CCL reviews the person's request.
CCL's approval to move an existing clearance or exemption to this facility.
A person's first presence at the facility in any role, including as a volunteer.

procedures: Before the first interview ends, the Administrator tells every applicant that employment is conditional on criminal record clearance and that no one may work or be present before clearance, an exemption or an approved transfer is in place.
The applicant completes and signs the Criminal Record Statement (LIC 508) and gives the Administrator a copy of valid photo identification.

The Administrator completes the Live Scan request form LIC 9163 with the facility's information. The applicant goes to a Live Scan site and returns the receipt (transaction record) to the Administrator within [NUMBER] days.
The Administrator files the LIC 508 and the Live Scan receipt in the applicant's personnel file (see STF-05) and logs the date of the request.
The Administrator checks with CCL and the vendoring regional center whether any additional registry or background check applies to this home and records the answer in the facility file.

The applicant does not work, orient, shadow, or enter the home as staff until the Administrator has received CCL's written clearance, exemption or transfer approval. The Administrator does not schedule the person in the interim.

If the result shows a criminal record that needs an exemption, the Administrator gives the applicant CCL's instructions and does not allow work or presence until CCL approves the exemption in writing.

If CCL denies an exemption or the person is not eligible, the Administrator ends the hiring process the same day and documents the outcome. Anyone already on site is removed from the premises immediately.
For a person with an existing clearance or exemption, the Administrator completes the transfer process with CCL and does not allow work or presence until CCL's approval is received.
The Administrator confirms that any new corporate CEO is fingerprinted under §80019(d) before taking the position, and that any change in the licensee's officers is reported to CCL.

As an agency rule, every employee must tell the Administrator in writing within one business day of any new arrest or conviction. The Administrator reviews the matter with CCL and may remove the person from duty pending the outcome.

The Administrator keeps clearance and exemption letters in the personnel file, makes them available to CCL and the regional center on request, and reviews all files each quarter to confirm every person working has a clearance on file.

responsibilities.duty: Starts Live Scan for each applicant, verifies clearance before any work, keeps records, and removes anyone who is not cleared.
Completes LIC 508, gets fingerprinted promptly, and reports any new arrest or conviction.
Ensures the corporate CEO and other required persons are fingerprinted and that no one works without clearance.

documentation: LIC 508 Criminal Record Statement
LIC 9163 Live Scan request and receipt
CCL clearance, exemption or transfer letter
Clearance tracking log with dates
Quarterly file review checklist
Written confirmation from CCL or the regional center on any additional checks

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
policies.applies_to: All new and current direct care staff (direct support professionals), night staff and the Administrator, who is responsible for overseeing training at [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To make sure every direct care staff person completes the Title 17 orientation, the two-segment Direct Support Professional Training (DSPT), and ongoing continuing education so residents receive competent care.
policies.policy: Every new direct care staff person completes a 40-hour on-site orientation (17 CCR §56038(a)(1)) covering program design, IPPs, individual rights, medications, emergencies and fire, Special Incident Reports and abuse reporting. Direct care staff also complete the two 35-hour competency-based segments of the Direct Support Professional Training (year 1 and year 2) or pass the challenge test (17 CCR §56033). Segment 2 must be completed within two years of hire (§56033(a)(2)(B)). DSPT is free to the staff person through DDS. Staff who work nights must be trained in the facility's emergency procedures and in first aid (22 CCR §85065.6(b)). Continuing education is at least 8 hours a year at Level 2 and 12 hours a year at Levels 3 and 4; Level 4 staff who do not have six months of experience take 12 additional hours in the first six months (§56038). Because §56038 was amended in the DDS SIR rulemaking effective 5/1/2026, the Administrator confirms the current text each year. [AGENCY NAME] pays all staff for required training time. On-the-job training topics follow 22 CCR §80065(f). This policy does not list official checklist items because none were assigned to it.

definitions.definition: The 40-hour on-site training required for new direct care staff under 17 CCR §56038(a)(1).
Direct Support Professional Training: two 35-hour competency-based segments with tests or a challenge test.
A test a staff person may take to show competency in a segment without completing the full coursework.
Required yearly training hours based on the home's service level.

procedures: On the hire date, the Administrator gives each new direct care staff person the training schedule showing orientation, DSPT segments 1 and 2, first aid, and CE requirements, and records the dates by which each must be done.
The Administrator confirms the person has criminal record clearance (STF-02) before any orientation takes place on site.

The Administrator or a designated qualified trainer delivers the 40-hour on-site orientation. It covers the facility's program design (SB-04), IPPs and Needs and Services Plans (PCS-01), individual rights (IR-01, SB-05), medications (HW-01), emergencies and fire (SA-01, HE-02), SIRs (BSP-04) and abuse reporting (BSP-03).
Each orientation session is recorded with date, hours, topics, trainer and the staff person's signature. The Administrator tracks the running total toward 40 hours.

New staff work alongside an oriented staff person and are not left alone with residents until the Administrator has signed off in writing on their competence in emergency procedures, first aid, residents' rights, medication assistance and abuse reporting.
Staff assigned to nights must complete training in the facility's planned emergency procedures and first aid before working a night shift, and the Administrator records the dates.
The Administrator enrolls each direct care staff person in DSPT segment 1 within [NUMBER] days of hire and arranges paid time for classes and testing. Staff are never charged for DSPT.
Segment 2 is completed within two years of hire (§56033(a)(2)(B)). The Administrator checks status every quarter and moves up the schedule if a person is at risk of missing the deadline.

The Administrator determines continuing education hours for each staff person from the home's service level, including extra hours for Level 4 staff without six months of experience, and sets a yearly CE plan.

Each January the Administrator reviews the current text of 17 CCR §56038 and §56033 and any DDS or regional center notices to confirm the requirements, noting that §56038 was amended effective 5/1/2026.
All training time, including orientation, DSPT, first aid and CE, is paid time and is recorded on time records (see STF-08).
The Administrator files certificates, sign-in sheets, test results and orientation records in each personnel file (STF-05) and gives the regional center and CCL access on request.
If a person is behind on training, the Administrator gives a written plan with dates, may limit duties, and does not count the person toward ratio if a competency sign-off is lacking.

responsibilities.duty: Schedules, delivers or arranges, tracks and documents all training and verifies deadlines are met.
Attend and complete orientation, DSPT, first aid and CE, and keep their certificates.
Deliver content accurately and document attendance and competency.
Provides paid time and resources for training.

documentation: Training schedule per employee
Orientation record (40 hours) with topics, dates, trainer and signatures
DSPT segment 1 and 2 completion and test records
First aid and emergency procedures training records
Annual CE plan and hours log
Written competency sign-off
Quarterly training status report

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff and the Administrator at [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff by documenting each employee's health screening and TB test, removing ill staff from duty, and keeping administrator HIV/TB training current.
policies.policy: Each employee has a health screening that includes a TB test performed by or under the supervision of a physician no more than one year before or seven days after the start of employment (22 CCR §80065(g)). Ill personnel are relieved of duty (§80065(h)). The Administrator completes HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator and updates it every two years (22 CCR §85064(k)). Screening records are kept in the personnel file. [AGENCY NAME] follows the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) for staff who may be exposed to blood or other potentially infectious materials. This policy does not list official checklist items because none were assigned to it.

definitions.definition: A physician's or physician-supervised evaluation showing the person is physically able to perform the job and free of communicable disease.
Tuberculosis screening done by or under a physician within the window set in 22 CCR §80065(g).
Removed from work with residents because of illness that could harm residents or prevent the person from doing the job.

procedures: The Administrator tells every applicant at the offer stage that a health screening and TB test are required, with the test to be done no earlier than one year before and no later than seven days after the first day of work.

The applicant gives the Administrator the physician's or clinic's written health screening and TB test result. If the applicant does not have a recent one, [AGENCY NAME] arranges the screening and pays for the cost.
The Administrator reviews the documents the day they are received and enters the test date and result on the health screening tracking log. Any test dated outside the allowed window is rejected.
If the TB test is missing on day seven of employment, the Administrator removes the person from duty until it is received.

If a TB test result is positive or a health condition raises concern, the Administrator follows the physician's or local public health department's written instructions before the person returns to work.
Health screening and TB test results are filed in the confidential section of the personnel file (STF-05) and are not shared except with CCL, the regional center, or as required by law.

Any employee with signs of a communicable illness (such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea, rash or persistent cough) must stay home and call the Administrator at [PHONE]. The Administrator relieves the person of duty and arranges coverage under STF-01.
An employee who has been ill returns after the symptoms are gone, or with a physician's written release when the Administrator requests one. The Administrator records the dates of absence and return.

For staff who may be exposed to blood or other infectious materials, the Administrator keeps an exposure control plan, provides training on it at hire and yearly, and offers hepatitis B vaccination at no cost. Exposure incidents are reported at once and documented (see HE-03).
Within six months of becoming administrator, the Administrator completes HIV/TB training and repeats it every two years. The Administrator records the dates and files the certificate.
Each quarter the Administrator reviews all personnel files to confirm each screening and TB record is on file, and acts on any gap within one business day.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies screening and TB results, removes ill staff from duty, completes HIV/TB training, and keeps records.
Obtain the screening and TB test on time and stay home when ill.
Pays for required screening and makes sure sick staff are replaced.

documentation: Physician's health screening statement
TB test result and date
Health screening tracking log
Record of illness-related removals and returns
Administrator HIV/TB training certificate
Exposure control plan and vaccination offer or declination records
Quarterly file review checklist

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: The Administrator and anyone who creates, keeps or reviews personnel files at [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To keep a complete, accurate and confidential file for each employee that shows each requirement was met and can be shown to CCL and the regional center at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel file for every employee that includes: name; driver's license if the person drives residents; start date; a statement that the person is 18 or older; training records; health screening and TB test; and criminal record clearance or exemption (22 CCR §80065). Orientation, DSPT and continuing education hours are recorded in the file (17 CCR §56038). Inhaler training and any related documentation are filed in the personnel file (22 CCR §80075). Records are kept at least five years (17 CCR §54326(a)(3)) and are available for CCL and regional center review. Files are confidential and kept in a locked location. This policy does not list official checklist items because none were assigned to it.

definitions.definition: The complete set of records for one employee, kept in a secure location.
A signed statement, supported by identification, showing that a staff person who gives care or supervision is 18 or older.
A dated record of every training, including topic, hours, trainer and the employee's signature.

procedures: On the hire date, the Administrator opens a file for each new employee and uses a checklist to track each required item.
The file includes: full name, address and phone; job title; start date; and a signed statement of age with a copy of valid identification.
If the employee drives residents, the Administrator copies the valid driver's license and the proof of insurance, and notes the license expiration date to check every year (see HE-05).
The Administrator files the criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer approval, the LIC 508 and the Live Scan receipt (see STF-02).
The Administrator files the physician's health screening and TB test record (see STF-04).
The Administrator files the orientation record, DSPT segment 1 and 2 records, first aid and emergency procedures training, and the yearly CE record, with date, hours and trainer for each.

When an employee is trained to help with metered-dose or dry-powder inhalers, the Administrator files the licensed professional's training documentation, the procedures, the trained staff names and the yearly review (see HW-01).
The Administrator files the signed job description (SB-01), the signed Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries acknowledgment (STF-06), and the signed acknowledgment of personnel policies (SB-02).
The Administrator reviews every file each quarter, lists gaps and corrects them within [NUMBER] days. Anyone with an unresolved gap in clearance or TB documentation is not scheduled.
Personnel files are stored in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator and the Governing Body may open them, except as needed for CCL or regional center review.
On request, the Administrator provides files to CCL and the regional center during monitoring (see GOV-06) and logs the date and the person who reviewed them.
Files are kept at least five years after the person leaves employment, and then destroyed securely. If any dispute, audit or investigation is pending, files are held until it is closed.
A staff roster showing each person's name, position and start date is kept current and is available on site.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains every file, runs quarterly reviews, protects confidentiality and gives access to regulators.
Provide accurate documents and copies of new training, licenses and certificates.
Makes sure records are complete, secure and retained.

documentation: Personnel file checklist
Age statement and identification
Driver's license copy (if driving)
Clearance or exemption
Health screening and TB test
Orientation, DSPT, first aid and CE records
Inhaler training documentation (if applicable)
Quarterly file review log
Staff roster
Records access log

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers, relief staff, the Administrator and the licensee at [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To make sure residents receive care free of abuse, exploitation and prejudice, with their personal rights, privacy and dignity respected, and to set clear boundaries between staff and residents.
policies.policy: Care is given without physical or verbal abuse, exploitation or prejudice (22 CCR §80065(l)). Staff may not borrow from residents, take their money or property, or use residents as substitutes for required staff. All staff must report personal-rights violations (§80065(m)). Staff respect each resident's dignity, privacy and personal rights as listed in 22 CCR §80072, including freedom from corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse and punitive actions, and freedom from interference with eating, sleeping or toileting. Staff also respect resident confidentiality consistent with HIPAA's administrative requirements (45 CFR 164.530) and IR-04. Violation of this policy leads to discipline up to and including termination and reporting as required by law. This policy does not list official checklist items because none were assigned to it.

definitions.definition: Using a resident's money, property, labor or person for the benefit of staff or anyone other than the resident.
The limit between a paid staff relationship and a personal, financial, romantic or social relationship.
Any act or failure to act that denies a right listed in 22 CCR §80072.
A consequence meant to punish, such as withholding food, shelter, clothing, medication or aids, or interfering with eating, sleeping or toileting.

procedures: At hire and each January, every staff person receives a copy of this policy and the list of residents' personal rights, and signs an acknowledgment that is filed in the personnel file (STF-05).
Staff treat residents with respect: they address residents by their preferred name, knock before entering bedrooms and bathrooms, and provide personal care privately.

Staff never use corporal or unusual punishment, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, threats, coercion or mental abuse. They never interfere with eating, sleeping or toileting, and never withhold shelter, clothing, medication or aids as a consequence.

Staff do not borrow money or property from residents, accept gifts of value, ask for loans, sell items to residents, or take any resident money or property. Any gift offered is declined and reported to the Administrator the same day. Resident funds are handled only as described in SB-08.
Staff do not enter personal, romantic, sexual or financial relationships with residents, and do not use personal social media to contact residents or post about them.
Staff do not take photographs or video of residents, or share information about residents, except as the resident or authorized representative agrees in writing and as IR-04 allows.
Staff do not use residents to do staff work, supervise other residents, or cover any staff post. Residents may do chores only as part of their own plan and with their consent (see IR-01).
Staff do not use personal errands, personal use of resident rooms or vehicles, or use of resident phones or accounts. Staff do not bring visitors into the home without the Administrator's approval.
Staff do not discuss residents' health, behavior, finances or history with anyone who does not have a need to know. Records are kept secure (IR-04, REC-01).
Staff do not use alcohol, cannabis or illegal drugs, and do not report to work impaired. The Administrator relieves any impaired person of duty immediately.

Any staff person who sees or suspects a personal-rights violation, abuse, neglect or exploitation reports it immediately to the Administrator, or if the Administrator is involved, to [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT] and to the authorities as BSP-03 requires. Reports are never delayed to ask permission.

The Administrator documents the report, protects the resident right away, and follows BSP-03 and BSP-04 for reporting and investigation. No staff person is punished or retaliated against for reporting in good faith.
The Administrator tells residents and their representatives about the right to complain to CCL and to [AGENCY NAME], and gives them the complaint contacts under IR-03.

When a violation of this policy is found, the Administrator removes the person from resident contact pending review, keeps written findings, and applies corrective action under SB-02, up to termination.
The Administrator reviews this policy with all staff at least once a year and after any incident, and keeps a record of the training.

responsibilities.duty: Follow professional boundaries, respect resident rights and privacy, and report any violation right away.
Trains staff, investigates reports, protects residents, applies discipline and prevents retaliation.
Ensures staff conduct standards are enforced and reviews serious violations.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy and the residents' rights list
Annual training sign-in sheet
Reports of rights violations and any investigation notes
Corrective action records
Gift declination log
Record of resident and representative notice of complaint rights

policies.title: Administrator Certification, Qualifications and Continuing Education
policies.applies_to: Adult Residential Facility (ARF) licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing and vendored by a regional center (service codes 915/905, ARM Levels 2–6)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is always directed by an administrator who holds a current California ARF administrator certificate, meets the Title 17 experience and continuing education requirements for the facility's service level, and has completed the regional center residential services orientation before the first admission.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will operate the facility only under a certified ARF administrator who meets 22 CCR §85064 and §85064.2 and the Title 17 requirements in 17 CCR §56037 and §56003. The administrator must be at least 21 years old and hold a high school diploma or GED (22 CCR §85064). The administrator must hold a current certificate issued through the CDSS Administrator Certification Bureau. The path to certification is the 35-hour CDSS-approved Initial Certification Training Program (ICTP), then the state exam within 60 days of finishing the training (maximum three attempts, $100 exam fee). The administrator then applies on form LIC 9214 within 30 days of passing, with form LIC 508, Live Scan fingerprints (LIC 9163) and the $140 fee (22 CCR §85064.2). The certificate is renewed every two years with 40 hours of continuing education, 4 of them on laws and regulations; up to 24 hours of regional center-approved DDS training may count (22 CCR §85064.3). Where the facility will serve 7–15 clients, the administrator must also have one year of residential care experience (22 CCR §85064). Under 17 CCR §56037 the administrator must have 6, 9 or 12 months of developmental disability experience for Level 2, 3 or 4 respectively, unless the regional center waives it in writing, and must complete 8, 12 or 12 hours of Title 17 continuing education each year for Level 2, 3 or 4. For a facility at Level 5 or 6, [AGENCY NAME] will confirm the requirements in writing with the vendoring regional center before the service level is approved. The administrator must complete HIV/TB training within six months of becoming administrator and update it every two years (22 CCR §85064). The administrator must complete the regional center's residential services orientation before the first admission (17 CCR §56003). No resident will be admitted until all of these items are in the administrator's file. The facility's official policy checklist for this policy lists no separate items, so no checklist item numbers are cited here.

definitions.definition: The 35-hour Initial Certification Training Program approved by CDSS for ARF administrator applicants.
A person who passed the state exam, applied for and received the ARF administrator certificate, and keeps it current by recertification.
Renewal of the administrator certificate every two years with 40 hours of CE, including 4 hours on laws and regulations.
The orientation offered by the regional center (at least every six months) that the administrator must complete before the first admission.
The annual hours of training required of the administrator by 17 CCR §56037 for the facility's service level.

procedures: Before the application is filed, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms that the person named as administrator is at least 21, has a high school diploma or GED, and meets any experience requirement for the facility's size and ARM level. The confirmation is dated and filed in the administrator's file.
If the person is not yet certified, the owner enrolls them in a CDSS-approved 35-hour ICTP and keeps the certificate of completion.

The administrator schedules the state exam to fall within 60 days of finishing the ICTP. The owner tracks the deadline on the compliance calendar and pays the $100 exam fee. No more than three attempts are allowed, so the administrator prepares before each attempt.

Within 30 days of passing the exam, the administrator submits form LIC 9214, form LIC 508, Live Scan fingerprints (form LIC 9163) and the $140 fee to the CDSS Administrator Certification Bureau. The administrator keeps copies and proof of delivery.
The owner confirms the Live Scan result and the certificate issue date, and files a copy of the certificate in the administrator's personnel file and in the licensing binder.

The administrator confirms Title 17 experience in developmental disabilities for the facility's level (6 months for Level 2, 9 for Level 3, 12 for Level 4). If the experience is short, the owner requests a written waiver from the vendoring regional center and keeps it on file. For Levels 5 and 6, the owner obtains the regional center's requirements in writing.

The administrator registers for the next regional center residential services orientation, which is offered at least every six months, and attends before the first admission. The attendance record or certificate is filed. [AGENCY NAME] does not accept a referral or admit a resident until it is on file.

Within six months of becoming administrator, the administrator completes HIV/TB training and files the certificate. The administrator repeats the training every two years, and the owner puts the due date on the compliance calendar.
The administrator keeps a continuing education log that shows date, hours, provider, topic, whether the course is regional center-approved DDS training, and a copy of the certificate.

Each year the administrator completes the Title 17 continuing education hours for the facility's level (8, 12 or 12 hours for Level 2, 3 or 4). The administrator confirms with the regional center or CDSS whether the same hours may also count toward the 40-hour recertification requirement. Hours are counted twice only when written guidance allows it.

Over each two-year certification period, the administrator completes 40 hours of CE, including at least 4 hours on laws and regulations. Up to 24 hours of regional center-approved DDS training may count toward the 40.
The owner reviews the CE log at 12 months and 18 months of each certification period. If the administrator is behind, a training plan with dates is set in writing.
At least 90 days before the certificate expires, the administrator submits the recertification package with proof of CE. The owner checks that the certificate is renewed before the expiration date.

If the administrator leaves or the certificate lapses, the owner notifies CCL and the regional center as required by REC-02 and appoints a replacement who meets this policy. The replacement completes any missing items before taking over. The owner does not name an interim administrator who lacks a certificate.
At each annual policy review (GOV-03), the owner audits the administrator's file against this policy and records the result.

responsibilities.duty: Names a qualified administrator, pays fees, tracks deadlines, and makes sure no admission occurs before orientation and certification are complete.
Keeps the certificate current, completes the ICTP, orientation, HIV/TB training and CE on time, and keeps all records in the file.
Maintains the compliance calendar with due dates for exam, application, HIV/TB update, annual CE and recertification.
Offers the orientation, approves the service level, and decides any waiver of Title 17 experience.

policies.title: Wage and Hour and Labor Compliance
policies.applies_to: Adult Residential Facility (ARF) licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing and vendored by a regional center (service codes 915/905, ARM Levels 2–6)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] pays all direct care and other employees lawfully under federal and California wage and hour law, and that the facility's staffing plan under 22 CCR §80065 is carried out with properly paid, competent personnel.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will pay every employee at least the highest minimum wage that applies where the facility is located, and will follow the federal Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), 29 CFR Part 552 (domestic service), and California wage and hour law. California's statewide minimum wage is $16.90 per hour in 2026, and many cities and counties set higher rates (for example, $18.42 in the City of Los Angeles and $17.75 in San Diego). The DDS rate-model direct support wage of $18.20 per hour is a rate assumption, not a pay rule, and may be below the local minimum in some cities. [AGENCY NAME] will not set pay by the rate model alone. Employees earn paid sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days a year under Labor Code §246. [AGENCY NAME] does not assume that any overtime, companionship or live-in exemption applies. Employment counsel must review 24-hour shifts, sleep time, and meal and rest period rules (Wage Order 5) before they are used, because those rules have not been verified for this manual. This policy supports 22 CCR §80065, which requires that personnel be competent and in the numbers needed to meet client needs; that supervising and care staff be 18 or older; that clients not substitute for required staff; and that ill personnel be relieved of duty. Volunteers are not counted in the staffing plan and are not used to avoid paying employees.

definitions.definition: The federal Fair Labor Standards Act, which sets minimum wage, overtime and recordkeeping rules.
Federal regulations on application of the FLSA to domestic service, including home care workers.
The highest of the federal, California and local (city or county) minimum wage in effect where the employee works.
All time an employee is under the employer's control or required to be on duty, as determined under law and counsel's advice.
Leave accrued under Labor Code §246 of at least 40 hours or 5 days a year.
The California Industrial Welfare Commission wage order for the public housekeeping industry, which counsel will review for meal, rest and shift rules.

procedures: Before hiring, the owner identifies the city and county of the facility and records the current federal, California and local minimum wage rates in the payroll file.

The owner sets every position's starting rate at or above the applicable minimum wage and compares it with the rate-model assumption of $18.20. If the facility's local minimum is higher, the local rate controls.

Before the first employee is hired, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] engages employment counsel or a payroll provider to review the shift pattern, including any 24-hour shift, sleep time, on-call time, overtime and meal and rest periods. Counsel's written advice is filed.

The owner classifies each position as exempt or non-exempt in writing. Direct care staff are treated as non-exempt (hourly, overtime-eligible) unless counsel advises otherwise in writing. Companionship and live-in exemptions are not assumed.
Each employee receives a written notice of pay rate, pay day, paid sick leave and employer information at hire. The employee's signed acknowledgment is filed in the personnel record.

Employees record time worked by a method that captures actual start and stop times, including time spent on handoff reports, medication documentation, training and mandatory meetings. Employees do not work off the clock.

Supervisors approve timesheets each pay period, and the administrator reviews them to confirm that scheduled and actual hours match the staffing plan in STF-01 and that overnight awake coverage is paid for all hours worked.
The administrator reviews the schedule weekly for overtime. Overtime is paid at the rate required by law, and any overtime not approved in advance is still paid.

Paid sick leave is credited at the start of employment or as it accrues under Labor Code §246 (at least 40 hours or 5 days a year), and balances are shown on pay statements. An employee who is ill is relieved of duty and not penalized for using paid sick leave.
The owner pays wages on regular pay days with an itemized wage statement and keeps payroll records for the period the law requires, as confirmed by counsel.
Clients are never used to cover required staff duties, and volunteers are not scheduled in place of paid staff. The administrator checks each posted schedule against this rule.
When the local or state minimum wage changes (each January 1 or any other date), the owner updates pay rates before the effective date and notifies employees of the new rate.

The owner reviews the staffing budget against the applicable minimum wage and rate-model income at least annually and before each rate or service-level change. Any shortfall is reported to the governing body (GOV-01).

Employees may raise wage complaints with the administrator or owner. The administrator investigates within 10 days, corrects errors in the next pay period, and records the result. No employee is retaliated against for raising a complaint.
Counsel reviews this policy and the wage practices at least once a year and when the law changes.

responsibilities.duty: Sets lawful pay rates, funds payroll, keeps counsel engaged, and corrects any underpayment promptly.
Approves schedules and timesheets, tracks overtime and sick leave, and keeps the schedule consistent with the staffing plan.
Advises on 24-hour shifts, sleep time, meal and rest periods, exemptions and recordkeeping.
Record all time worked accurately and report any pay concerns to the administrator.

documentation: Current minimum wage rate sheet (federal, state and local)
Position classification list (exempt or non-exempt)
Counsel's written advice on shifts, sleep time and meal and rest periods
Timesheets, schedules and overtime records
Pay statements and payroll registers
Paid sick leave accrual and use records
Signed new-hire pay notices
Wage complaint log and results

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: Adult Residential Facility (ARF) licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing and vendored by a regional center (service codes 915/905, ARM Levels 2–6)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate, confidential and locked record for each resident, and retains and destroys records according to California licensing and Title 17 vendor requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will keep a separate record for each resident that holds the Needs and Services Plan required by 22 CCR §85068.2 and its supporting documents, consumer notes and progress reports, medication records, and service documentation. Vendor billing and service records will be kept at least five years (17 CCR §54326(a)(3)). Medication central storage records and records of destruction of unretained prescriptions will be kept at least one year (22 CCR §80075). The retention period for the rest of the record will be the longer of five years or any other period required by law, as confirmed with counsel. Records will be kept locked, with access limited to authorized persons and logged. Records are kept as required by the privacy standards in 45 CFR 164.530, and HIPAA practices are set out in IR-04. The facility's official policy checklist lists no separate items for this policy, so none are cited here.

definitions.definition: The written plan completed before admission under 22 CCR §85068.2, covering the resident's needs, assessments and the facility's plans to meet them.
Dated staff notes of services provided to or events affecting a resident, used to support progress reports and billing.
A periodic written report on the resident's progress toward IPP objectives, sent to the regional center.
The plan included in the Needs and Services Plan when a resident has a restricted health condition (22 CCR §80092.2).
The minimum time a record must be kept before it may be destroyed.

procedures: On or before the day of admission, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] opens an individual record and a separate locked medication file for each resident, and assigns each a unique record number.

The administrator completes the Needs and Services Plan before admission, after determining the program can meet the person's needs. The plan covers the person's desires and background, entrance to the facility, specific service needs, mental and emotional functioning, and the facility's plans to meet those needs. It is filed in the record.

The following supporting documents are filed behind the plan: the written medical assessment, the functional capabilities assessment, the mental health intake assessment (if any), the initial assessment under HSC 1180.4(a) completed on or before the day of admission, and the individual emergency intervention plan.

The 1180.4(a) assessment records input from the resident, the authorized representative and any person the resident chooses. It also records the resident's advance directive on de-escalation, seclusion or manual restraint, early warning signs and triggers, calming techniques, medical conditions that raise restraint risk, and trauma history.
If the resident has a restricted health condition, the Restricted Health Condition Care Plan is filed in the record as part of the Needs and Services Plan.

The administrator records who took part in developing the plan, including the resident or representative, participating relatives, the placement or referral agency and the person responsible for admissions.

Staff write dated, signed consumer notes at the time of service or by the end of the same shift, and file them in the record. Staff do not alter entries; errors are corrected by a single line, initials and date.
The administrator prepares and files progress reports as set out in PCS-02 and sends them to the regional center on its schedule. Copies are kept in the record.
The administrator updates the Needs and Services Plan when the resident's needs change and on the schedule set in PCS-01. Each version is dated, and earlier versions are kept.

Medication records, central storage records and records of destruction of unretained prescriptions are kept in the medication file. Destruction of unretained prescriptions is witnessed by the administrator and one other adult who is not a client, and the record is kept at least one year.

Vendor billing and service records are kept together by month and resident so they can be produced on request for at least five years (17 CCR §54326(a)(3)). They are available to the regional center for monitoring.

Records are stored in a locked cabinet or in a password-protected system, and the key or password is limited to the administrator and designated staff. Each person who reviews a record signs and dates an access log.
Records are shown to CCL, the regional center or other authorized persons only as allowed by law and IR-04. The administrator logs each disclosure with date, person, purpose and what was released.
When a resident leaves, the administrator completes the record, notes the date of discharge, and boxes and labels the record with its earliest destruction date. The record is stored locked.
The administrator reviews all records at least once a year to check that the required documents are present and current, and records any corrections made.

Records past their retention period are destroyed by shredding or secure deletion with the owner's approval. Each destruction is logged with date, record type and method. Records are never destroyed while a complaint, audit, investigation or legal action is pending.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the record system, completes the Needs and Services Plan, controls access, and carries out retention and destruction.
Write timely, accurate consumer notes and medication records, and keep records secure.
Provides locked storage, approves destruction, and makes sure records are available to authorized reviewers.
Reviews health-related documents at the intervals set in HW-02.

documentation: Individual resident record with Needs and Services Plan and all required assessments
Restricted Health Condition Care Plan (if any)
Consumer notes and progress reports
Medication central storage and destruction records
Vendor billing and service records
Record access and disclosure log
Annual record review checklist
Record destruction log

policies.title: Required Reports to the State and Regional Center
policies.applies_to: Adult Residential Facility (ARF) licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing and vendored by a regional center (service codes 915/905, ARM Levels 2–6)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] sends every required report to CDSS Community Care Licensing (CCL), the regional center and other authorities on time and with the required content.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will make all reports required by 22 CCR §80061 to CCL, the resident's authorized representative and other agencies. CCL must receive a report by the next working day, followed by a written report within 7 days, for: any death; deaths from injury, abuse or other than natural causes (including deaths away from the facility); use of an AED; injury needing medical treatment; any unusual incident or client absence that threatens health or safety; suspected psychological abuse; epidemic outbreaks; poisonings; catastrophes; and fires or explosions. Suspected physical abuse of a dependent adult is reported to the local ombudsman, CCL and law enforcement within 2 hours if there is serious bodily injury, and otherwise within 24 hours. Within 10 working days, [AGENCY NAME] reports to CCL organizational changes, mailing address changes, a change of corporate CEO (with fingerprints), and plan-of-operation changes that affect services. [AGENCY NAME] also sends Special Incident Reports to the regional center under 17 CCR §54327 (amended May 1, 2026), and consumer progress reports under §56026. An independent review or audit is delivered when the facility's regional center payments reach the thresholds in WIC §4652.5. The annual CCL license fee ($454 for 4–6 beds) is paid on time. The facility's official policy checklist lists no separate items for this policy, so none are cited here.

definitions.definition: CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, which licenses and inspects the ARF.
The first day after the event on which CCL offices are open; weekends and state holidays do not count.
A report of a reportable incident sent to the regional center under 17 CCR §54327.
The person legally authorized to act for the resident, who must also receive certain reports.
A review (regional center payments of $500,000–$1,999,999 per year) or audit ($2,000,000 or more per year) of vendor finances under WIC §4652.5, due 9 months after fiscal year end.

procedures: The staff member on duty who learns of a reportable event first gives immediate care and makes the person safe (HW-04, BSP-04). Staff then notify the administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] at [PHONE] right away, day or night.

If suspected physical abuse of a dependent adult involves serious bodily injury, the administrator or staff member reports it within 2 hours to the local ombudsman, CCL and law enforcement. If there is no serious bodily injury, the report is made within 24 hours. The time, person spoken to and report number are recorded (BSP-03).

For deaths, AED use, injuries needing medical treatment, unusual incidents or absences that threaten health or safety, suspected psychological abuse, epidemic outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes, and fires or explosions, the administrator telephones the CCL regional office by the next working day and records the call. Epidemic outbreaks are also reported immediately to the local fire authority.
Where appropriate, the administrator reports poisonings, epidemic outbreaks and catastrophes to the local health officer, and records the contact.
The administrator sends the resident's authorized representative the report content required for the events in §80061(b)(1)(A)–(H), as soon as possible.

Within 7 days of the event, the administrator submits the written report to CCL. It states the resident's name, age, sex and admission date; the date and nature of the event; physician findings and treatment; and the disposition. A copy goes in the resident's record and the incident file.

The administrator sends the regional center a Special Incident Report under 17 CCR §54327 as required for the incident type and by the deadline in the regional center's current instructions. The administrator checks the amended May 1, 2026 rule and regional center guidance at least once a year and after any change. BSP-04 describes the investigation.

Consumer progress reports are prepared by the administrator and sent to the regional center under 17 CCR §56026 on the regional center's schedule (PCS-02). A calendar shows the due dates, and the date sent is logged.

Within 10 working days of a change in organization, mailing address, corporate CEO (including fingerprints for the new CEO) or in the plan of operation that affects services, the administrator sends written notice to CCL. The owner prepares the plan-of-operation update (SB-04) for review.
When CCL substantiates a complaint, the administrator provides copies to the designated parties as the regulation directs, and records the date sent.

At the start of each fiscal year, the owner estimates the facility's annual regional center payments. If they are expected to reach $500,000–$1,999,999, an independent review will be needed; at $2,000,000 or more, an independent audit. The owner engages a qualified independent accountant and records the due date, which is 9 months after the fiscal year end (WIC §4652.5).
The owner delivers the independent review or audit to the regional center by the due date and keeps the transmittal in the finance file (GOV-05).
The owner pays the annual CCL license fee of $454 (4–6 beds) by the due date shown on the CCL invoice. If it is paid late, a 50% late fee is added, so the owner calendars the payment 30 days ahead.

The administrator keeps a report log listing each report, the date of the event, the date and time reported, the person reported to, the date the written report was sent and any follow-up. The owner reviews the log monthly.

At each quarter, the administrator checks the log against incident files and the compliance calendar to make sure no report was missed or late. Any late report is explained in writing and the cause is corrected (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Makes or supervises all reports, tracks deadlines, and keeps the report log.
Give emergency care, notify the administrator immediately, and write an accurate incident account before the end of the shift.
Reports organizational and address changes, pays CCL fees, and arranges independent review or audit.
Reviews the report log and identifies trends under GOV-04.

Written 7-day reports to CCL and copies of Special Incident Reports
Notices of change to CCL (10 working days)
Progress report transmittals
Independent review or audit and delivery record
CCL fee invoices and payment receipts
Quarterly report timeliness review

official.notes: The booklet says the application fee plus Section A and B documents must be submitted to the licensing agency as one packet, in the same sequence as the booklet. Incomplete packets are returned in full. Originals must carry original signatures, and the applicant should keep a photocopy. Excluded Section A items: LIC 200, 215, 308, 309, 400, 402, 401, 401a, 403, 403a, 404, 500, 501, 503, 508, 999 and 9054. Excluded Section B items: B1 (partnership/corporate documents), B2 (administrator qualification and certification), B12 (water bacteriological analysis), B16 (first aid card) and B17 (orientation certification). Items that do not apply to ARFs: B3 (social worker qualifications; group home and FFA only), B13 and B14 (insurance and theft & loss; RCFE only), B18 (group home and FFA rate-setting statement) and A17.
